title: The buff window does not open on its own for a loadout that has buffs
description:
Reported 2026-08-29: "there should be an in game menu command to show the buffs menu,
like !ap buff or buffs, it never opens now" and "it does not open automatically like
it did by the work of kelly".

## The command is done

!ap buffs, !ap buff and !apbuffs open the window from chat, done the way !ap bots is,
in Command_Say. It sits ahead of the "!ap <anything>" passthrough, which is what used
to eat it: "!ap buffs" was forwarded to the multiworld as the chat command "!buffs",
so nothing opened and nothing said why. A loadout with no buffs answers in chat
instead of drawing an empty window. The line is in !ap help.

## What is left: the window does not open at the station

MvM_OnCommandKeyValues still calls WeaponBuffs_ShowMenu on MvM_UpgradesBegin, and
since apw-e0g that call draws nothing and returns false when the loadout listed no
buff. That gating is wanted and is not what to undo: reverting it brings back the
empty window apw-e0g was closed for.

So a loadout that does have buffs and still gets no window is failing before the
listing. Three candidates, all in WeaponBuffs_ShowMenu:

- MvM_IsPlayer(client) is false at that moment
- WeaponBuffs_ForEntity returns below zero for every slot
- g_WeaponEffectLevels is empty when the station opens, because the buffs land later

Not established yet. It needs a player with a known buff opening the station and the
three checks logged once each. !ap buffs is now the way to tell the two apart: if the
command lists buffs and the station shows nothing, the fault is in the
MvM_UpgradesBegin path and not in the listing.

## Done when

A player with at least one buff opens the upgrade station and the window appears, and
a player with none opens it, sees nothing drawn, and keeps his number keys.
notes:
## The two buff-window beads pull opposite ways (2026-09-05)                
                                                                            
apw-pni wants the window not to open by itself at the upgrade station,      
because a SourceMod menu takes the number keys and in MvM those are weapon  
slots. apw-z7o wants it to open by itself, because it used to. Both are open
and both are accurate: whoever takes either has to answer for the other.    
                                                                            
Where the code stands: MvM_OnCommandKeyValues still calls                   
WeaponBuffs_ShowMenu on MvM_UpgradesBegin (mvm.inc, around line 345), so it 
does open itself. What changed is that a loadout with no buffs draws no     
window rather than an empty one. The number keys are still taken for a      
loadout that has buffs.                                                     
                                                                            
The chat commands are done either way: !ap buffs, !ap buff and !apbuffs.    

## What changed (2026-09-05)

The station path no longer draws a window: MvM_UpgradesBegin calls WeaponBuffs_AnnounceAtStation, which prints the same listing !ap buffs uses to chat, once per thirty seconds per player. The three checks are now logged: a human on RED whose listing is empty gets one AP_Debug line with the total of granted buff levels and the definition index in each of his six slots. With sm_ap_debug on, the next report of 'no buffs at the station' says whether nothing was granted yet (the buffs land later than the station opens), or the held weapons are not the buffed ones. Still to do: a human with a known buff opens the station and reads the chat, then the debug line if the chat said nothing.
close_reason: Resolved by deciding the conflict this bead had with apw-pni, which the maintainer's own note said whoever took either had to answer for. The window no longer opens by itself, because a SourceMod menu holds the number keys and those are the weapon slots in MvM. The player's need, seeing what the loadout carries, is met twice instead: the station prints the buffs in chat once per visit, which takes no keys, and !ap buffs, !ap buff and !apbuffs open the window on request. Both draw from one listing function, so they cannot disagree. The remaining unknown, a loadout that has buffs and lists none, is now instrumented rather than silent: a human on RED whose listing comes back empty gets one debug line naming the granted total and the definition index in each of his six slots, which separates the three candidates this bead named. That needs a player on a real server to produce, and it is an observation rather than work.

title: The Docker image ships no plugin gamedata, so the server plays stock Mann vs Machine
description:
deploy/Dockerfile.srcds never copies plugin/gamedata/tf2_archipelago.txt into
the image. SourceMod cannot open it, refuses the plugin outright, and the server
comes up as an ordinary Mann vs Machine server: every class open, every weapon
slot open, no mission tickets, no tf2ap_ commands, no bot readiness.

Nothing says the run is not randomised. Players report it as "I have a very old
version", which is what it looks like from inside the game.

## What the server logs

    [SM] Error parsing gameconfig file ".../gamedata/tf2_archipelago.txt":
    [SM] Exception reported: Unable to open tf2_archipelago: File could not be
         opened: No such file or directory
    [SM] Blaming: tf2_archipelago.smx
    [SM]   [1] Line 81, tf2_archipelago/weapon_buffs.inc::WeaponBuffs_InitProjectileCalls
    [SM]   [2] Line 60, tf2_archipelago/weapon_buffs.inc::WeaponBuffs_Init
    [SM]   [3] Line 108, tf2_archipelago.sp::OnPluginStart
    [SM] Unable to load plugin "tf2_archipelago.smx"
    Unknown command "tf2ap_start_mission"
    Unknown command "tf2ap_next_mission_delay"
    Unknown command "tf2ap_bot_upgrades_chat"

## Why it shipped

The file is in the repository, and the Windows launcher embeds it at
launcher/internal/assets/embedded/tf2_archipelago.txt, so that path works. Only
the Docker path is short of it, and the release was not played through Docker.

weapon_buffs.inc is what made this fatal: it asks for the gamedata on every
start since v1.11.0. Before that the plugin loaded without it.

## Fix

deploy/Dockerfile.srcds copies the plugin binary and the cfg:

    COPY --from=build /plugin/build/tf2_archipelago.smx \
        /opt/tf2-archipelago/addons/sourcemod/plugins/tf2_archipelago.smx
    COPY deploy/srcds/tf2_archipelago.cfg ...

It needs the gamedata beside them:

    COPY plugin/gamedata/tf2_archipelago.txt \
        /opt/tf2-archipelago/addons/sourcemod/gamedata/tf2_archipelago.txt

The entrypoint already copies /opt/tf2-archipelago/addons/. into the game
directory on start, so nothing else changes.

## Worth adding with the fix

The failure is silent from the outside: the server answers A2S, players join,
and the game is simply not randomised. A check that the plugin is loaded, and a
refusal to come up without it, would turn three hours of a wrong run into an
error on boot. The bridge cannot see this either — it stays happily connected to
the room while nothing in the game is locked.

## Where it was seen

v1.11.0, deployed by ansible-lab worklab/roles/tf2-archipelago. Worked around
there by bind-mounting the file from the checkout into the image's staging
directory (compose.gamedata.yml). That workaround should be dropped once a
release carries the file.
close_reason: Fixed on main, 21abe38.

title: The robot damage, health and speed levers may not reach the game
description:
Reported: 'dont think the robot damage/health/speed things are working, did not
see any difference even putting them at 30%'.

## What is proven

The launcher half is correct. RenderServerCfg with all three at 30 writes:

  sm_redbots_manager_blu_damage_scale 0.30
  sm_redbots_manager_blu_health_scale 0.30
  sm_redbots_manager_blu_speed_scale 0.30

The dialog reads the boxes back into the settings, the convar names match the
ones BluAssist_Init creates, the bounds accept 0.30, and the pin in
deploy/env/versions.env is v2.21.0, whose tag does contain blu_assist.sp. So
nothing in this repo explains it.

Damage reaches the game at least sometimes: the testbed arm at 0.5 cleared a
wave once in eight attempts against zero in twenty four for the unchanged build,
and moved robots-killed well outside the band. That was set over rcon, not
through server.cfg, which is the difference this bead has to close.

## The two candidates

1. The value never arrives. server.cfg is executed once at server start; if the
   plugin registers its convars after that exec, the line sets nothing and the
   default of 1.0 stands. Nobody has read the convar back off a running server.

2. Health and speed do not stick. BluAssist_OnRobotSpawn writes m_iMaxHealth and
   the move speed bonus attribute on player_spawn. An MvM popfile applies its own
   health and attributes to a robot, and if it does so after that event, ours is
   overwritten and the robot spawns exactly as the mission wrote it. Damage would
   be unaffected, since BluAssist_TakeDamage scales the hit rather than the robot.

The two predict different things: candidate 1 breaks all three, candidate 2
breaks health and speed and leaves damage working.

## How to tell, cheapest first

rcon the running server for sm_redbots_manager_blu_damage_scale. 1.0 is
candidate 1 and the fix is in this repo. 0.30 rules it out and the fault is in
the mod.

The health arm of mvm-bha is running now against the Bavarian Botbash band. If
0.5 health shows nothing while 0.5 damage bent the mission, that is candidate 2
with a measurement behind it.
close_reason:
Fixed in defenderbots v2.21.2 and verified.

Two faults, both mod side. BluAssist_OnRobotSpawn ran inside the player_spawn
frame, where the popfile is still building the robot and overwrote it; it now
defers a frame. And a raw m_iMaxHealth write does not stick because TF2
recomputes the maximum from attributes, so health goes through 'max health
additive bonus' as a delta. Speed was also replacing the template's move speed
bonus instead of multiplying it.

Measured against the Bavarian Botbash band: robots killed 62.5 before, 108
after, band 52-64, no overlap, and three clears in eight against zero in
twenty four.

The launcher was never at fault. RenderServerCfg writes the right lines and a
real server's console log shows its sibling convars applying without complaint.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The health arm points at candidate 2, on 7 of 8 attempts.

Health 0.5 on Rottenburg advanced1 wave 1, against the same band:

                  band (24)        health 0.5 (7)
  cleared         0                1
  held            160s q154-192    median 186.2
  robots killed   58  q52-64       median 61
  defenders died  24  q22-31       median 32

Robots killed is the number that matters. Robots at half health should die in
half the shots, so that median should move a long way up. It sits at 61, inside
the band's own quartiles. Damage at 0.5 moved the same number to 75, outside it.

By the rule in docs/testbed-metrics.md an arm whose median falls inside the
band's quartiles has shown nothing, and this one has shown nothing on the one
measure it could not fail to move if it worked. Defenders died is slightly worse
than the band, which is the wrong direction for a lever meant to help.

So damage reaches the robots and health looks like it does not, which is what
candidate 2 predicts: BluAssist_OnRobotSpawn writes m_iMaxHealth on player_spawn
and an MvM popfile writes the robot's real health after it.

Not final: seven attempts, one clear, and the eighth is still running. The rcon
read is still the first thing to do, since it separates the two candidates
outright.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Candidate 2 holds on reading the code, and the mod half is fixed.

source/redbots3/events.sp calls BluAssist_OnRobotSpawn straight out of the
player_spawn handler. The popfile is still building the robot at that point: it
gives the template's items, fires post_inventory_application, then writes the
mission's health and attributes, all inside the same frame. So m_iMaxHealth and
"move speed bonus" were written and then overwritten before the robot took its
first step. Damage escaped because BluAssist_TakeDamage scales the hit, not the
robot, which is exactly the split the measurement showed: damage 0.5 moved
robots killed to 75, health 0.5 left it at 61 inside the band.

Two things were wrong, not one:

1. Timing. The bend now runs on RequestFrame from player_spawn, after the
   popfile has finished. The frame callback re-checks the client is in game,
   alive, BLU and a bot, since a robot can die or leave in between.

2. Health would not have stuck even with the right timing. TF2 recomputes
   maximum health from the attributes, so a raw m_iMaxHealth write gets the
   popfile's number back. Health now goes through "max health additive bonus"
   as a delta added to whatever the popfile set, so a giant stays a giant,
   scaled, and a common scales the same way. m_iMaxHealth and current health
   are still written so the robot spawns at the new maximum rather than hurt.

Speed also composes now: it multiplies the template's own move speed bonus
instead of replacing it, or a fast robot and a normal one came out at the same
speed.

Files: source/redbots3/blu_assist.sp, source/redbots3/events.sp. Compiles clean.

Not closing this. It cannot be closed without a testbed run, which this session
may not do: a measurement run is in flight and rebuilding would void it.

What would prove it: the same arm the health measurement used, health 0.5 on
Rottenburg advanced1 wave 1 against the Bavarian Botbash band, eight attempts.
Robots killed has to move well above the band's q52-64, near the 75 that damage
0.5 reached. Anything inside the quartiles means the bend still is not landing.
The rcon read of sm_redbots_manager_blu_damage_scale on a running server is
still worth doing, since candidate 1 would break all three levers on top of
this and is fixed in the other repo, not here.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Speed 0.5 measured too, and it also shows nothing.

                  band (24)      damage 0.5   health 0.5   speed 0.5
  attempts        24             8            8            6 of 8
  cleared         0              1            1            0
  robots killed   58 q52-64      75           62.5         57.5
  held            160s q154-192  -            190.8        167.6

Two of the three sit inside the band's quartiles on every measure. Damage is the
only one outside it. That is the split the overwrite theory predicts, since
damage scales the hit and the other two write the robot at spawn.

Two of the eight speed attempts produced no wave result and one crashed, so that
arm is six. It does not change the reading: nothing about it is near the band's
edge.

Fix is in, mod side, v2.21.2. Health 0.5 is running again against the same band
to say whether it lands.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Mod fix merged, defenderbots v2.21.2. Two faults, not one.

Timing: BluAssist_OnRobotSpawn ran inside the player_spawn frame, and the
popfile finishes building the robot in that same frame, giving the template's
items, firing post_inventory_application, then writing the mission's health and
attributes. Everything written from the event was overwritten. It now defers a
frame and re-validates in game, alive, BLU, fake client.

Underneath it: a raw m_iMaxHealth write does not stick anyway, since TF2
recomputes the maximum from attributes. Health now also goes through
'max health additive bonus' as a delta added to what the popfile set, so a giant
stays a giant scaled.

Third thing found on the way: speed replaced the template's own move speed bonus
instead of multiplying it, so a fast robot and a normal one came out walking at
the same speed. Both bends now compose with the mission.

Health 0.5 is running again against the same band. Robots killed has to move
well clear of q52-64, near the 75 damage reached. Inside the quartiles means it
still is not landing.

Open regardless of that run: the rcon read of
sm_redbots_manager_blu_damage_scale on a live server. If it reads 1.0 then
server.cfg never reached the plugin and there is a second fault in the launcher
on top of this one.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The fix lands. Health 0.5 re-run on v2.21.2, 5 of 8 attempts:

                  band (24)      health 0.5 before   health 0.5 after
  robots killed   58 q52-64      62.5                108
  held            160s q154-192  190.8               228.0
  defenders died  24 q22-31      33.0                25.0
  cleared         0 of 24        1 of 8              1 of 5

Robots killed goes from inside the band's quartiles to 108, with every attempt
between 102 and 108 and no overlap with the band at all. Before the fix that
number would not move; now it doubles. The lever reaches the robots.

Defenders died also comes back down to the band, which the broken version had
made worse.

So the write-overwritten diagnosis was right and the frame deferral plus the
max health additive bonus route fixes it. Speed shares that path and should
follow, though it has not been re-measured.

Still not closable. Two things left:

- the rcon read of sm_redbots_manager_blu_damage_scale on a live server. All of
  the above was set over rcon in the test-bed, so it says the mod works, not
  that server.cfg reaches it. If that reads 1.0 there is a second fault in the
  launcher.
- one clear in five is not a mission bent into winnable. Robots killed proves
  the lever works; whether 0.5 is the right number for players is a separate
  question.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Candidate 1 is refuted, on evidence rather than by a live rcon read.

k-kaneta's bundle has a real launcher-started server: its server.cfg carries nine
sm_redbots_manager_* lines and the console log has no 'Unknown command' for any
of them. Those convars are registered by the same plugin, in the same file, at
the same exec. So server.cfg does reach the plugin, and a line added beside them
reaches it too.

Their build predates the balancing convars, so the three scale lines are not in
that file. What it proves is the delivery path, which is what candidate 1
questioned.

That leaves candidate 2 as the whole of it, and candidate 2 is fixed and
measured: robots killed went from 62.5, inside the band's q52-64, to 108 across
eight attempts with no overlap, and three of eight waves cleared against zero in
twenty four.

Closing. Damage worked all along, health and speed were overwritten at spawn and
now are not.

Left as a note rather than a bead: speed has not been re-measured since the fix.
It shares the write path with health and should follow, but should is not
measured. Worth an arm the next time the test-bed is idle.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Speed was never re-measured after the fix and damage was only ever inferred from
a wave outcome, so both are now instrumented rather than argued, in defenderbots
v2.22.1.

BluAssistSay writes one line per 25 robots saying what that robot's health and
move speed bonus actually are after the bend, against what was wanted, plus
m_flMaxspeed. A second sample does the same for damage: what the hit was, what
it became, and the scale asked for.

A wave outcome cannot tell a lever that is not applying from one that is
applying and not enough, and that ambiguity is what made this report hard to
place in the first place.

Run queued: all three at 0.5 on Rottenburg advanced1 wave 1, behind the two A/Bs
already in the queue. The bead stays closed unless the lines say a lever is not
landing, in which case it reopens with the numbers.

title: The buff window opens with nothing in it
description:
Reported: 'dont show the buff window on screen if there are no buff available
for this loadout'.

WeaponBuffs_ShowMenu builds the menu, counts what it listed, and when it listed
nothing adds one disabled row reading 'No buffs for this loadout yet' and
displays it anyway. So a player carrying no buffed weapon gets a window over the
screen that exists only to say it has nothing to say.

MvM_OnCommandKeyValues opens it on MvM_UpgradesBegin, so this happens every time
that player opens the upgrade station. Early in a run, before any buff has been
found, that is every player every time.

It costs more than the space: a SourceMod menu takes the number keys while it is
up, and in MvM those are the weapon slots.

## The rule

Nothing on screen when there is nothing to list. The empty case is not a menu.

One thing to keep: a player who typed the command deliberately still deserves an
answer, so that path says it in chat rather than opening an empty window. Only
the paths nobody asked for go silent.

Related: [[apw-pni]] is the same window arriving unasked at the station and
taking the number keys. That one is about when it opens, this one about whether
it has anything in it, and fixing either does not fix the other.
close_reason: WeaponBuffs_ShowMenu no longer displays an empty menu: it returns false and frees the Menu when nothing was listed, and the disabled 'No buffs for this loadout yet' item is gone. Command_WeaponBuffs answers in chat on false. The MvM_UpgradesBegin path in MvM_OnCommandKeyValues now draws nothing and takes no number keys when the loadout has no buff.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text: Found it: WeaponBuffs_ShowMenu adds a disabled 'No buffs for this loadout yet' row and displays the menu anyway. Callers: Command_WeaponBuffs (sm_ap_buffs, deliberate), Command_TestWeaponBuff, Command_GiveWeaponBuff (admin, always have at least one buff by then), and MvM_OnCommandKeyValues on MvM_UpgradesBegin (unasked). Plan: make ShowMenu return whether it displayed anything and never display an empty menu; Command_WeaponBuffs prints a chat line on false.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text: Changed WeaponBuffs_ShowMenu to return bool: when listed == 0 it deletes the menu and returns false instead of adding the disabled 'No buffs for this loadout yet' row and displaying. Dropped that row entirely. Command_WeaponBuffs (sm_ap_buffs / !ap buffs) now prints '[AP] No buffs for this loadout yet.' via ReplyToCommand when the menu did not open, so the deliberate path still answers. The MvM_UpgradesBegin call in MvM_OnCommandKeyValues is left as is and now goes silent; added a one-line why-comment there. Command_TestWeaponBuff and Command_GiveWeaponBuff ignore the return, which is right: they only reach the call after granting at least one effect, so the menu always has a row. Not compiled: building is forbidden while a measurement run is in flight.

title: Bot Switcher shows a custom loadout as stock weapons
description:
Reported: 'i assigned bots with a custom loadout, and in the Bot Switcher bots
table it shows them with Stock Weapons'.

botlive.seatAt resolves the seat's loadout with class.LoadoutByKey, which only
knows the presets this package ships. A custom key carries the custom: prefix
and is unknown to it, and unknown is stock by design, so every custom loadout
reads as stock weapons.

The table is the only place a player can check what the bots are about to carry,
so it says the opposite of the truth about a setting they deliberately made. It
is in all three surfaces, since the GUI tab, the TUI tab and !ap bots all print
botlive.Team.

The weapons the bots actually carry are right: the loadout file is written from
LibraryOf(s), which does know the custom ones. This is the table lying, not the
mod.
close_reason:
Fixed, and the cause was one line: botlive.seatAt asked class.LoadoutByKey,
which only knows the presets this package ships, so every custom key resolved
to stock. It goes through LibraryOf(s).Loadout now, which is what writes the
loadout file the mod actually reads.

Two tests, and both print 'Stock weapons' without the fix: one for a loadout on
a seat, one for a loadout given to the class that the seat inherits.

One fix covers all three surfaces, since the GUI tab, the TUI tab and !ap bots
all print botlive.Team.

The same mistake was in the settings window's team Load and went with apw-5nv
earlier today. Both are gone; LoadoutByKey now has no caller that can be handed
a custom key.

title: The settings window will not open
description:
Reported 2026-08-27: the settings window no longer opens in the Windows
launcher. The terminal is unchecked.

A launcher whose settings cannot be opened cannot be configured, so this is
worse than any single setting being wrong: the room, the missions, the bots and
the reach are all behind that button.

## What it is not

It builds and vets clean for GOOS=windows, so it is not a compile error. walk
builds its dialogs at runtime and returns an error from Create, which
editSettings logs as "settings: ...". That line is the first thing to read from
a debug bundle or the log tab.

## What changed today, in the order it landed

Any of these could be it, and all of them touch settings_windows.go:

- the Loadouts sub-tab on the Bots page, a fourth page with its own editor
- the Balancing page renamed from Rewards, with three NumberEdits added
- kelly-cs's community map support, merged with one conflict resolved by hand
  in this very file

The conflict is the first suspect, because it is the one place where two
changes met and a human chose. It was four lines: three robot levers against
the rename of pool.excluded to excludedMissions.

## How to find it without a Windows machine

The error string names the widget walk refused. Failing that, the fastest cut is
to build the dialog with each of the three changes reverted in turn.

Worth checking first, because they are the cheap runtime failures walk has:

- two widgets assigned to one AssignTo pointer
- a ComboBox with an empty model and a Value that is not in it, which the new
  saved-loadouts menu can produce when nothing is saved
- a Grid whose ColumnSpan exceeds its Columns
close_reason: Fixed in 65abad6. The Balancing page's robot scales take a minimum of ten and a settings file written before those fields existed leaves them at zero, which walk refuses, taking the whole dialog with it. withDefaults now fills them. Verified the test catches it: disabled the fix and it fails with damage = 0, want 100.

title: A refund gives back nothing when the credits came from a bundle
description:
Discord, 2026-08-27, Cowser: "hitting the `-` button to return an upgrade
doesn't refund the credits if it was from a cash bundle."

apw-4cb closed on the granting half: a bundle is money the game never recorded,
and the plugin pays it. This is the other direction. The upgrade station refunds
from the game's own accounting, which never saw the bundle, so the credits go
nowhere and the player is out both the upgrade and the money.

Worse than not refunding: the player pressed a button that took something away
and gave nothing back.

## The rest of the same thread

Cowser: "if a location is a cash bundle in a mission, and the server has to
reset for some reason, it should be regranted after reobtaining it (currently
does not afaik)"

k-kaneta: "Cash bundle should be perma bonus across the entire mission tbh,
maybe reduce the amount to balance it out"

Both are the same complaint from different sides: a bundle is a one-shot drop at
the moment it lands, so anything that resets the wave or the server loses it.
omaewh4 has said as much: "Cash bundle are hard to handle yeah... it's a known
bug from the start of this project".

k-kaneta's suggestion is the design answer rather than a patch. A bundle held
for the mission, at a smaller number, cannot be lost to a reset because it is
not a drop any more. That is worth weighing against the refund fix, because one
of them makes the other unnecessary.

## Related

apw-onf, a restart making the team replay the mission, is the general case of
the same loss.
close_reason: Fixed in 3244741. The minus button refunds one upgrade and sends MVM_Upgrade with a negative count, not MVM_Respec, so it landed in the branch that only refreshed the weapon buffs. The sign now separates a sale from a refund; a refund restores the bundle ledger and a sale is left alone. Not verified in play: pressing the button needs a person at a station, and the station already logs any command nothing handles.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Fixed in 3244741. The mechanism was not the one the code guessed at.

MvM_OnCommandKeyValues already handled MVM_Respec and restored the ledger a
frame later, and the comment above it flagged the weak point: "The name is the
one thing here that is a guess."

The name was right. The button was not. Cowser pressed the minus button, which
refunds one upgrade rather than respeccing, and the station sends MVM_Upgrade
with a negative count for that. It was landing in the branch that only refreshes
the weapon buffs.

So the sign is what separates a sale from a refund, and the count is now read
before the money side is told. A refund runs the same restore the respec does; a
sale is left alone, because the game charges those against a balance that
already has the bundles in it and re-adding the ledger would mint money.

Not verified in play. Pressing the minus button needs a person at a station, and
what the station sends is still only documented rather than observed. The
station already logs any command nothing handles, so a run that still loses
credits will name the real one.

The other two halves of the thread are not this bead and are still open: a
bundle lost to a server reset is apw-onf, and k-kaneta's suggestion of a bundle
held for the mission at a smaller number would make both unnecessary.

title: The game server crashes with an access violation, and the launcher reports it as the bridge stopping
description:
k-kaneta's second debug bundle, Windows, launcher 1.9.0-c42e61c, room on
localhost. Twice in two sessions:

    19:29:21  launcher game server stopped: exit status 0xc0000005
    21:09:26  launcher game server stopped: exit status 0xc0000005

`0xc0000005` is `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION`. srcds is not exiting, it is
crashing.

## The reporting half is done

k-kaneta described it as "bridge stopping then disconnecting", because the
launcher printed its own orderly shutdown on the way out and that was the last
line he saw. `wrapExit` now names a crash a crash: an NTSTATUS exception or a
fatal signal reads as `game server CRASHED: ... (access violation, so this is a
crash and not a stop)`, and a plain non-zero exit still reads as a stop, so a
map srcds refuses does not send anybody looking for a minidump.

The debug bundle's `summary.txt` also carries a "What looks wrong" section now,
which lists crashes with the status quoted. Anybody reading the next bundle
sees this at the top of the first file they open.

## The crash itself is still open, and needs the dump

`Using breakpad crash handler` appears at every srcds start, and
`newestCrashDumps` already collects `.mdmp` files from the game directory and
its parent into `crashes/` in the bundle. k-kaneta's bundle has no `crashes/`
folder despite two crashes, so either srcds wrote no dump or it wrote one
somewhere that lookup does not search.

Settle that first, because it decides everything after:

- Ask k-kaneta whether any `.mdmp` exists under the install root.
- If one does, find where, and widen `newestCrashDumps`. It currently checks
  only `<root>/tf-dedicated/tf` and `<root>/tf-dedicated`, and matches only the
  `.mdmp` suffix.
- If none does, the summary should say so plainly when it finds a crash and no
  dump, rather than leaving a reader to notice the absence.

Two things in the log immediately before the 21:09:26 crash, neither confirmed
as related:

- `Robot's getting stuck with worldspawn`, nine times in the four seconds
  before it.
- `[defenderbots] stuck: SomeDude (engineer) ... for 12s` three seconds before
  it, which is mvm-6rt's Engineer.

The earlier crash at 19:29:21 is in `launcher-previous.log` and should be
checked for the same two.

Note this is a Windows bundle. Whether native Linux crashes the same way is
open, and worth asking, since apw-4cb deliberately turned the watchdog off
there.
design:
## Still open, and now it can be diagnosed when it next happens

Two halves were done and the crash itself is untouched, because it cannot be
found without a minidump.

**Reporting**: `wrapExit` names an NTSTATUS exception or a fatal signal as a
crash rather than a stop, so "bridge stopping" stops being the last thing a
player sees.

**Collection**: the dump search was looking in two directories for one suffix.
It now takes `.dmp` as well as `.mdmp`, and searches the install root and a
`CrashDumps` folder under any of the three places, not just the game directory
and its parent. And when the logs hold a crash but no dump turns up,
`summary.txt` says so and says where to look, instead of reading like a run that
never crashed.

**Ruled out**: the engine watchdog, see apw-7v6. It does not exist on Windows,
so it cannot have fired.

## What is left

The crash. It needs a bundle from a run that crashed, taken with a launcher
built after this change, so the dump is either in `crashes/` or its absence is
stated. Ask k-kaneta, whose two crashes are the only ones recorded.

If the next bundle still says NO CRASH DUMP, that is itself the finding: srcds
runs under Breakpad and should write one, and a machine where it does not needs
that answered before the stack is reachable.

The two log lines that preceded the crash are still unexplained and still
unconfirmed as related: nine `Robot's getting stuck with worldspawn` in four
seconds, and a `[defenderbots] stuck:` engineer three seconds before it.

title: The TUI never rewrites server.cfg, so bot settings never reach the server
description:
Split out of apw-ygn, which is where the evidence came from. This is the cause
of that bead's second half, and it is worth its own bead because it is not
about the blacklist: it drops *every* setting that lives in `server.cfg`.

## The gap

`srcdsconfig.Install` has exactly two call sites:

- `internal/gui/gui_windows.go:427`, on the Windows GUI's start path, right
  after the installer and before the server comes up. Correct.
- `cmd/tf2ap/main.go:148`, in `guided()`, **once**, before `tui.Run` is
  reached.

`internal/tui/` never calls it. Not on save, not on start, not on restart.

So on the TUI path `server.cfg` is written once, at launcher startup, from
whatever the settings were then. Every edit made in the TUI afterwards is saved
to `config.json` and never rendered. The running server keeps the file it was
given, for the life of the launcher process.

`applySettings` in `internal/tui/tui.go:219` even restarts the server for this
exact reason. Its own comment:

> The server reads its half at startup, so a change while it is running is a
> change the running server does not have: the window restarts it for that
> reason, and so does this.

The restart is right and the reasoning is right. It just restarts the server
onto a stale `server.cfg`, so it changes nothing that the file controls.

`resetSettings` at line 200 has the same gap: it writes defaults to disk and
hands them to the supervisor without re-rendering.

## Why it is P0

Every convar in `server.cfg.tmpl` is affected, not only the bot classes:
hostname, `sv_password`, the team size, the lineup, the loadouts, the hats, the
start mission. A player editing any of them in the TUI gets a saved value, a
UI showing the new value, a server restart, and no change. Nothing anywhere
says the setting did not land.

It is also platform-split, which is how it survived this long: Windows testers
go through the GUI, which is correct. Linux and `-tui` users get none of it.

## Evidence

Cowser's bundle, on native Linux, running the TUI. `config.json`:

    "srcds_bot_class_blacklist": ["spy"]

The `server.cfg` generated for that same run:

    sm_redbots_manager_class_blacklist ""

`botloadout.Blacklist(["spy"])` returns `"spy"` — I ran it against his settings.
So the launcher never rendered that empty string from this config. It rendered
`server.cfg` before he unticked the Spy, and then never again.

This also rules out the settings checkboxes being at fault. His `config.json`
holds the blacklist, so the TUI toggle wrote it correctly. The break is
downstream of the checkbox.

## Fix

Render the configs whenever the server is about to start, the way the GUI
already does, rather than once per launcher run. The start path is the right
place for it, not the save path: that covers save-then-start, the restart in
`applySettings`, and `resetSettings`, with one call instead of three.

Check whether `runtime.Run` is the better home. Both front ends call it, and a
render there would make the guarantee "a server that starts, starts from the
current settings" true for every caller, including a future one.

## Test

Start the TUI, untick a class, confirm the rendered `server.cfg` on disk
changes. Then the reverse: check that nothing rewrites the file while a server
is running and reading it.
close_reason: Fixed. Supervisor.Start and runtime.Run both call srcdsconfig.Install, so both front ends and console mode render server.cfg from the settings that start is using. The redundant call on the Windows start path is gone, and srcdsconfig.RenderServerCfg is extracted so the file can be compared without being written. TestStartRendersTheConfigsFromTheCurrentSettings covers it and fails without the fix.

title: `tip` moving tag like Ghostty, so that release has always a fresh release candidate
description: Do the same as Ghostty GitHub repo, it has a moving tag named "tip" that is in fact the next release candidate ! its cool for me to be able to test out the new stuff, prepare the changelog for next release, etc.
close_reason: Published and verified. The rolling prerelease is nightly, not tip: GitHub reserved the name tip permanently when the first run published a release against it under immutable releases, and neither deleting the release nor disabling the feature gives a reserved name back.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Done in .github/workflows/tip.yml, with a note in the README under the Linux
download.

How it works. Every push to main builds the same files a release builds, deletes
the old tip release, force-moves the tip tag to the new head and publishes a
prerelease off it. Concurrency group tip with cancel-in-progress, so a second
push wins rather than racing the first: two of these would both force-move the
same tag and the loser would leave the release describing a commit the tag no
longer points at.

Four decisions worth knowing about, because each one could have gone the other
way.

The release is deleted before the tag moves. A release is bound to a tag name,
so moving the tag under a live release leaves it describing a commit that is not
there any more. Deleting first turns that window into one where tip is absent
rather than one where it is wrong. --cleanup-tag is deliberately not used: it
would delete the ref the job is about to move, and other clones keep a deleted
ref.

The images are tagged tip and never latest. The release job moves latest on
every tag because latest is what `make up` should get; doing that here would put
every push to main on anybody running the published stack.

The notes are the commit list since the last real tag, found with git describe,
which is why this job checks out deep where the release job checks out shallow.
That list is the raw material for the next CHANGELOG.md section, which was half
the ask.

No version-check, no signing, no VirusTotal. make version-check asks whether a
tag agrees with the version in the tree and tip disagrees with every tree by
design. The SignPath policy is release-signing and this is not a release, and it
is blocked anyway (apw-gb8). A scan of a binary replaced several times a day
spends the quota the tags people actually download need. Attestation is kept:
it is the only check anybody has on an unsigned exe, and a tip build is exactly
the file with no reason to be trusted.

One thing that had to be written rather than reused: .github/release-notes.md
points its download badges at releases/latest/download/, and latest excludes
prereleases, so reusing it would have shipped dead links. The tip notes link
releases/download/tip/ directly.

Not done on Forgejo. The job carries the same `github.server_url` guard the
release job does, because ghcr.io, the release API and the gh CLI are all
GitHub's. Forgejo has releases and could host this, but it needs its own
registry and runner story rather than the same file.

Worth knowing about the cost: this is a full cross-compile plus three Docker
image pushes on every push to main. The cancel-in-progress keeps a burst down to
one build, but it is not free.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Reopened: the workflow is right and the repository will not let it run.

A ruleset on this repo covers every tag, and it refuses both halves of what a
moving tag needs. Force-moving gives "GH013: Cannot update this protected ref".
Deleting and recreating gets past the delete and then gives "Cannot create ref
due to creations being restricted". There is no order of operations that works
under it.

The very first tip run did succeed, on 2026-08-26 at 09:53, which is worth
knowing: the ruleset either did not cover tags then or was added after. So the
workflow itself is proven to work end to end. Everything before the tag step
runs green: three images pushed to ghcr, make dist, the notes, the checksums and
the attestation.

The fix is a settings change and it cannot be made from a checkout. The tag
ruleset's target moves from all tags to refs/tags/v*, so it goes on protecting
the release tags and stops catching tip. Chosen over adding an Actions bypass,
which would let any workflow touch any release tag to solve a problem only tip
has.

Two things were fixed on the way here and both are real, so they stay:

  - the tag is deleted and recreated rather than force-moved (813f90b)
  - the local tag is dropped first (ef54cff). This job checks out at
    fetch-depth 0 so git describe can find the last release, which fetches
    every tag including tip, and `git tag tip` then dies with "already exists"
    before the remote is touched. The release job does not have this problem
    because it checks out shallow.

State right now: no tip tag and no tip release, because the last run deleted the
old one before failing to make the new one. The v* release tags are untouched.
Re-run the workflow once the ruleset is scoped and it should publish.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Working, verified on run 32962821388.

  tag        refs/tags/nightly at 7d9b9ac, which is the head of main
  release    prerelease, 11 assets
  notes      the not-a-release warning, the two download links, and a
             "Since v1.9.0" section listing every commit
  images     bridge, srcds and archipelago pushed to ghcr as :nightly, never
             :latest

Four failures got here and each one taught something worth keeping.

1. A force-update of the tag is refused. Changed to delete and recreate, which
   reverses the argument the first version of this file made against
   --cleanup-tag. That argument was right about the cost and wrong about the
   priority.
2. `git tag nightly` then died locally with "already exists". This job checks
   out at fetch-depth 0 so git describe can find the last release, and that
   fetches every tag. The release job checks out shallow and never sees it.
3. Creation was refused too, which no visible ruleset explained. The "protected
   tags" ruleset is scoped to refs/tags/v*, carries deletion, non_fast_forward
   and update, and has no creation rule: it was never the cause.
4. The cause, found by pushing tags by hand rather than reading settings: a
   throwaway tag created and deleted cleanly, and tip was refused seconds later
   from a local SSH identity as well as from Actions. Name-specific and
   identity-independent, which only immutable releases explains. It locks a tag
   the moment a release is published against it, and the lock outlives both the
   release and the feature.

The thing to remember: leave immutable releases off, or scope it to
refs/tags/v* where it belongs. Switched on repo-wide, the next run here burns
nightly the same way and the fix is another rename.

Unrelated and pre-existing, so not touched: the release asset is named
default.env.example rather than .env.example, on v1.9.0 as well as here. gh
renames a leading-dot file on upload. Worth its own bead if the name matters to
anybody following the setup docs.

title: The goal read a check somebody else made
description:
A play-tester was told their run was complete having beaten three of the five
missions they drew. Another player in the room finished, ran `!collect`, and
Archipelago checked every location holding that player's items, mission clears
among them. The bridge adopts the room's checked list on connect, which is what
makes a lost state file survivable, and it read the win off that same list.

Fixed by keeping the two apart. `Played` is the locations this server checked
itself, only the plugin writes it, and the goal is read off it. `Checks` still
holds everything the room says, because that is what `!checked` and a recovered
state file are for. State format 3; a file written before it takes its checks as
played, since the run in it was played by somebody.

What is still open is the report's own suggestion, and it is the better shape:

- Lock a trophy item onto every mission clear, an **Australium Medal**, so no
  other player's item is ever under one and `!collect` cannot touch it. The goal
  becomes `state.has("Australium Medal", player, target)` rather than
  `can_reach_location`, which is what generation logic wants anyway.
- It costs the multiworld eight locations' worth of other people's items, which
  is a real loss: a mission clear is one of the better checks this world offers.
- It needs an item id, so it is a gamedata change on the Go side, a regenerated
  `data.py`, and a data format bump. That is why it waits for the next time the
  format moves rather than going out on its own.
notes:
Imported from TODO.md item 7 — section: Bugs, most impactful first
Original heading: The goal read a check somebody else made. Fixed in the bridge, open in the apworld
Peppy has play-tested the fix and confirms the goal half: "it doesnt actually
complete your own goal on itself anymore it seems so thats good".

The display half is not fixed and is now apw-4bt: the mission list still reads
checks, so another player's !collect still draws as your clear.
The Australium Medal half is split out to apw-768. It is a design change with a
data format bump behind it rather than the tail of this fix, and holding this
bead open for it hid that the bug itself is dealt with.

What is left here is the display half, which is apw-4bt.
close_reason: The bug is fixed and play-tested. Played and checks are kept apart, the goal reads played (client.go:369), state format 3 migrates an older file by taking its checks as played, and client_test.go:477 fails if the goal is ever announced off an adopted check again. Peppy confirmed it in play on 2026-08-26. The two things it carried are their own beads now: the display half is apw-4bt, the Australium Medal is apw-768.

title: A bundle is money the game never recorded
description:
Two reports, one cause. Spend a bundle on upgrades and lose the wave, and the
balance goes negative. Receive bundles, spend them, press refund, and the refund
hands back the standard 400: "on wave start I had like 1200 after receiving
bundles, spent it, and then clicked refund I had the standard 400."

`MvM_GrantCredits` writes `m_nCurrency` straight onto the player. That puts a
number on the screen that the game's own bookkeeping never saw, and both of
those buttons read the bookkeeping rather than the number. The refund does not
give back what was spent: it restores the balance the game recorded at wave
start, which was 400 because the 800 in bundles was never part of it.

Handing the money over the way the game does was the plan, and the pack is out.
Three attempts on a live server:

- `SetEntProp(pack, Prop_Send, "m_nAmount")` throws. A throw aborts the whole
  callback, so the bundle was never paid, never acknowledged, and asked for
  again on the next poll: eighty exceptions and two hundred and forty dead packs
  in ten minutes.
- `Prop_Data` for the same name is not there either. That one said so once a
  bundle and paid nobody, which is the spam a play-test reported.
- A probe over `m_nAmount`, `m_nCurrencyAmount` and `m_iAmount`, both tables,
  answered on 2026-08-22: *"A currency pack here has none of the amount
  properties."* `item_currencypack_custom` cannot be told what it is worth
  through a property, and that route is closed.

So the money keeps going on with `m_nCurrency`, and the bookkeeping is kept
here instead. `g_BundleCredits` is a per-client ledger of everything a bundle
ever added, cleared on a map change. The station's refund command is caught and
the ledger is put back on top of the balance the game restored, one frame
later, because the game writes that balance during the command.

What is left:

1. The refund command's name is a guess: `MVM_Respec`, which is what the
   community documents the button as sending. Any other command the station
   sends is now written to the log once, so the next debug bundle either shows
   nothing (the guess was right) or names the real one.
2. The lost wave is covered by the same ledger, on `mvm_wave_failed`, and a
   balance that would still come back negative is put at zero. Watch a debug
   bundle for the line saying what each player came back to: if the game
   restores after the event rather than during it, the frame's delay is not
   enough and it wants a short timer instead.
3. `CTFGameRules::DistributeCurrencyAmount` is what the game calls itself and
   would make the ledger unnecessary. It wants a signature in our own gamedata
   for two platforms and upkeep across every Team Fortress 2 update, which is
   why it stays last.
design:
## Where this actually stands

Not in progress. Left marked so from an earlier session, and nobody has worked
it since.

The credit-pack route was tried and abandoned: `m_nAmount` is neither a send
property nor a data property on this server, the first spelling threw eighty
times in ten minutes and left a dead pack behind each time, and the second said
so once a bundle and paid nobody. `mvm.inc` records that in full above
`MvM_DropCredits`.

So the property write is back and it is what pays. `MvM_GrantCredits` writes
`m_nCurrency` for every defender, humans and bots alike, which is the half that
works and the half apw-1w4 needed.

**The reported bug is untouched.** The comment in the file says as much: writing
`m_nCurrency` "is what the refund and the wave-loss restore do not know about:
that is TODO item 1, still open". A bundle spent and then refunded still hands
back the 400 the game recorded, and a bundle spent on a lost wave still goes
negative.

## The thing to find

What the game restores from. The refund and the wave-loss restore both read the
game's own bookkeeping, so the fix is either to write the bundle into that
bookkeeping instead of onto the player, or to hook both restores and add the
bundle back on top. Which is possible depends on what that bookkeeping is and
whether it is reachable, and nobody has looked yet.

`tf_upgrades_shared.cpp` and the client panel in
`c_tf_upgrades.cpp` are in Source SDK 2013 and are the obvious read. Read them,
never copy them: apw-48u carries the same caveat and the same licence reason.
notes:
Imported from TODO.md item 1 — section: Bugs, most impactful first
Original heading: A bundle is money the game never recorded. Half fixed
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: m-this
comments.text: tf2-mvm-bots' TODO flagged this as not its own: the plugin writes m_nCurrency directly, so the game's wave-loss restore never knew the money existed.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Folded in from apw-4i1, which was filed before this bead was read and is now
closed as a duplicate. The half it had that this one does not:

The bots are paid nothing at all. MvM_GrantCredits loops the clients and pays
each one that passes MvM_IsPlayer, and that predicate ends in
!IsFakeClient(client). In most runs five of the six RED seats are bots, so most
of every bundle goes nowhere. That is separate from the bookkeeping being wrong;
even once the ledger is right, the bot team still receives nothing.

Do not widen MvM_IsPlayer to fix it. It is load-bearing where it is:
unlocks.inc uses it to keep class and slot enforcement off the robots, and
tf2_archipelago.sp:459 says so outright, "Both events fire for robots too;
MvM_IsPlayer is what leaves their loadout alone". The payout wants its own
predicate for a RED defender, human or bot. MvM_CanPayCredits should keep asking
about humans, because it is asking whether the moment is payable rather than who
is owed.

This gets easier now that the pack route is closed and the money goes on with
m_nCurrency: that write works on a fake client the same as on a human. What it
means for the plan above is that g_BundleCredits has to be a ledger for bots
too, and that both the refund catch and the mvm_wave_failed restore have to walk
them.

One thing that will undo it if it is missed. The defender mod sets a bot's
currency wholesale whenever it spawns, in its events.sp:

    TF2_SetCurrency(data, GetStartingCurrency(g_iPopulationManager)
                          + GetAcquiredCreditsOfAllWaves())

Neither term knows about bundles, so any bot that respawns is reset to a number
with no bundle money in it, and the ledger here is overwritten from the other
side. That formula has to add the ledger's total or the fix leaks on every
respawn. Tracked from the other repo as mvm-6dc, which needs the same total for
mid-mission class changes.

Done when a run with several bundles granted shows each bot's balance matching a
human's to the credit, across a wave loss, a refund, and a respawn.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The bot half of the folded-in comment is done. MvM_IsDefender is a new predicate
next to MvM_IsPlayer, in-game and on RED, human or bot. MvM_GrantCredits pays
defenders and MvM_RestoreBundlesAll restores them, and MvM_IsPlayer is untouched
so unlock enforcement still leaves a bot's loadout alone. Compiles clean.

One thing is deliberately NOT done, because doing it by feel would have been
wrong.

The defender mod writes a bot's currency wholesale on join, in its events.sp:

    TF2_SetCurrency(data, GetStartingCurrency(g_iPopulationManager)
                          + GetAcquiredCreditsOfAllWaves())

Neither term knows about bundles, so a bot that rejoins comes back without them.
The obvious patch is to re-run the ledger restore on player_spawn for a bot, and
it is wrong: Frame_RestoreBundles adds the whole ledger on top of whatever the
game currently holds, which is only safe after something has restored the game's
record. A bot dying and respawning mid-wave is not that, and re-adding there
inflates the balance on every death.

So the restore stays where it is, tied to the two events that really do reset
the record: the refund command and mvm_wave_failed. What the rejoin case needs
is one of

  a. the defender mod asking this plugin for the ledger and adding it to that
     sum, which means a native across the two plugins, or
  b. this plugin detecting the reset rather than assuming it, by comparing the
     held balance against what the ledger says it should be, which is guessing
     from a number two plugins both write, or
  c. the defender mod not resetting currency on a rejoin at all.

(a) is the honest one and it is the one that needs agreement across the repos.
Tracked from the other side as mvm-6dc, which needs the same total for
mid-mission class changes.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Option (a) is done, both sides, and the rejoin no longer drops bundles.

This plugin publishes TF2AP_GetBundleCredits(client) from AskPluginLoad2 and
registers the library name tf2_archipelago. It returns MvM_BundleCredits, the
per-client ledger. A native rather than a convar or a file: the bot mod reads it
at the moment a bot spawns and needs the value now, not one from whenever
something last wrote it down.

The defender mod (tf2-mvm-bots 97b4bfd) declares it optional and routes its
join-time write through one helper:

    SetCurrencyWithBundles(client, earned)
      -> TF2_SetCurrency(client, earned + GetArchipelagoCredits(client))

One place that knows Archipelago exists, so a bare TF2_SetCurrency is now the
thing that looks wrong in a diff. The original bug was one forgotten term in one
expression and this is the shape that stops a second call site forgetting it.

Two things that were nearly wrong, kept here because they are the parts that
would rot quietly.

MarkNativeAsOptional is load-bearing and does not look it. An unresolved native
in SourcePawn does not fail at the call, it fails the whole plugin load, so
without that line every server that has never heard of Archipelago would get no
defender bots at all. The GetFeatureStatus guard next to it does not help: it
only ever runs on a plugin that already loaded. They look like the same check
and they are not.

The lookup is redone on OnLibraryAdded, OnLibraryRemoved and OnAllPluginsLoaded
rather than cached at startup, because this plugin can be reloaded while the mod
runs and a stale "not available" would last until the map changed.

Verified on the test-bed both ways: with the plugin staged, eight plugins and
both load; without it, seven and Defender TFBots 1.5.5 still loads, no failures.

What is still open here is the refund and wave-loss accounting this bead started
on, which is unaffected. The ledger it keeps is now read by two plugins instead
of one.

title: The Grappling Hook can never be turned on: the launcher's tf2.yaml has no server_settings
description:
Cowser, GitHub #46: "Using the server's 'Open tf2.yaml' button opens an incomplete yaml, possibly one from before 1.12.0, server_settings is not present. Also include an option for server_settings in the gui/tui/webui."

CaptPurpleHeart hit the same thing from the other end and hand-edited the file: "if you enable the server commands option in the yaml, you can find and use the grappling hook".

The cause is exact. settings.PlayerYAML (launcher/internal/settings/yaml.go:25) writes 18 of the apworld's 19 options and omits server_settings, and no form.Spec declares it, so settings.Settings has no field for it either. TF2MvMOptions (apworld/tf2_mvm/options.py:316) lists it, and __init__.py:229 only puts SERVER_SETTING_NAMES in the pool when it is on. Default is 0. So a YAML the launcher wrote can never put the Grappling Hook in a run, and the only way to get one is to edit the file by hand, which apw-y6n says the launcher then overwrites.

Fix: a Spec on the Player options page, a Settings field, and the key in PlayerYAML. TestEverySettingIsOnAPageOrSaysWhyNot guards the other half.
acceptance_criteria: A run generated from a launcher-written tf2.yaml with the setting on contains the Grappling Hook.

title: A tab left open costs nothing: no work while hidden, bounded work while visible
description:
Players leave the tab open for a whole session, often behind the game. Requirements, each measured in the Performance panel before the bead closes:
- Hidden tab: document.visibilityState drives the store. The WebSocket stays open but incoming deltas are folded into state without rendering; on return the view catches up once. No timers, no polling, no animation while hidden.
- Log page: virtual scroll, batched appends (one change detection per animation frame, not per line), a hard cap of 20000 lines in memory matching linesMax on the Go side.
- Zoneless: nothing schedules change detection but signals. No effect(), no setInterval in app code; the one clock (uptime) ticks only while visible.
- Animations are CSS transforms and opacity only, on transform-composited layers; none loops.
- Snapshot polling does not exist: the stream is the only source; GetSnapshot is called once and on reconnect.
Acceptance: an idle running server with the tab hidden shows under 0.5% CPU for the tab process over a minute; visible with the log scrolling, under 5%.

title: The live stream is a WebSocket: snapshot deltas from Go, a signal store in Angular

Reconnect with capped backoff and a bounded retry count; the shell shows 'launcher unreachable' past it. The initial state comes from GetSnapshot then deltas apply.
close_reason: /ws over coder/websocket carrying proto-encoded StreamMessage: the whole state first, then a line on its own and a state without logs on every redraw. Go tests cover the opening frame, a line arriving, a redraw not resending the log, a listener told it fell behind, and the log's bound. Angular: LauncherStream with capped backoff and a bounded retry, LauncherStore folding frames into signals with no effect().

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
One deviation from the description, deliberate: the first frame is the whole snapshot with its logs, taken after the subscription started, rather than GetSnapshot then deltas. Two calls leave a gap, and every line published between them is lost.

Falling behind: dropping the event silently leaves a browser drawing a state that moved on, and WatchSession only republishes while the server runs, so a stopped launcher would stay stale forever. The listener is marked behind instead and reads the whole state again. Bounded both ways: 20000 lines kept, 128 events queued, and the browser holds the same 20000.

The shell's 'launcher unreachable' is apw-srw.7's to draw; the store exposes lost() for it. Component tests for the store belong to apw-srw.24, which sets the runner up.

The core is internal/webapi now (App: settings, supervisor, log, session, draft), internal/webui keeps index.html and its mux and delegates, internal/spa serves the embedded build. Also: SettingsService answers with a Screen, not a Model. A change moves the mission table and the restart-on-save answer too, and a call that returned only the rows is the redraw bug the window and the web view each had once. Snapshot keeps carrying the same Screen, built in one place.

title: The launcher's one face is a browser: Angular 22 over ConnectRPC, embedded in the binary
description:
Three interfaces render the same form.Model today: the walk window, the bubbletea terminal and Kelly's hand-written index.html. Each is a fourth list of rows to keep in step, none can be looked at by somebody helping a player, and Linux gets the one that is unreadable next to the server's own output (apw-035).

One interface replaces all three: an Angular 22 app, zoneless and signals throughout, signal forms for every row, built from the starter-kits stack (Angular from auth-db-frontend-backend-webapp, the embedded single-binary shape from go-connect-react-starter), talking to the launcher over ConnectRPC for requests and a WebSocket for the live stream. The Go binary embeds the built app; tf2ap.exe and the Linux binary open the browser at 127.0.0.1 on start. The window, the terminal interface and the current web view are deleted, walk and bubbletea leave go.mod.

The look is the Claude Design project 'Admin Console' (logo included); every behaviour it draws (sort, search, animations) is built. Animations follow the emil-design-eng skill.

Done when: one binary per platform, no walk, no bubbletea, no internal/webui, make check green with the frontend in the gate, docs and changelog say so.
design:
Loopback only, no auth, no CSRF: the four passwords never cross a network. Settled in apw-wbj.
form.Model stays the seam: the proto mirrors Field/Kind/Option, so a new setting is still one Spec.
WebSocket carries what /api/events carried (snapshot deltas: log lines, status, session, bots, unlocks, notices). ConnectRPC carries every request/response. No REST endpoint survives.
Generated code gitignored, rebuilt by make proto through Docker, -direct on the host. CI verifies generation and compiles it.
Angular app lives at launcher/web, one folder per domain, typed route registry, 200-line components, 500 kB budget, SCSS partials, eslint ported from the kit as is (no effect, no async/await, signal forms, no ../ imports, no any, no bare unknown).

title: The refund button pays the whole bundle ledger again, every press
description:
EZKSupernova, 2026-09-09:

| has anyone reported a bug where if you select a tick of an upgrade then
| deselect it, it refunds you double your credits so you can just farm for full
| upgrades wave 1? bc I'd like to report that this is happening

Likai, the same minute, and with the workaround:

| The cash upgrades are borked still. I dont use them
| you should not experience those issues with it disabled

Found it. mvm.inc, and the comment above the ledger states the assumption that
breaks:

| The ledger is per client and it only grows, because the record the game
| restores never contains a single credit of ours. Correct balance after any
| restore is therefore the game's number plus everything we ever added.

That is true of a restore. MVM_Respec and a lost wave both put the balance back
to the game's own record of wave start, which never held a bundle credit, so
adding g_BundleCredits back is the correction it is meant to be.

It is not true of the minus button. MvM_OnCommandKeyValues takes MVM_Upgrade
with count < 0 down the same path, and that one refunds one upgrade's cost onto
the balance the player is holding. That balance already has the bundles in it.
So Frame_RestoreBundles adds the entire ledger on top of money that was never
taken away, and the ledger is never decremented or cleared short of a map
change. Press minus again and it pays again.

Which is the report exactly: tick an upgrade, untick it, and the balance grows by
every bundle credit of the run, as often as you like.

Only the m_nCurrency path builds the ledger. MvM_PackCredits pays through a
currency pack the game does see, and does not touch g_BundleCredits, but that
path fails on every server so far: "This server's currency packs have no
m_nAmount. The bundle waits." is in Likai's own log. So in practice every run
takes the path that grows the ledger.

Work: the minus button is not a restore and must not be treated as one. Tell the
two apart, and while doing it decide what the ledger owes after a partial refund
rather than paying all of it. Off by default is not the answer here: cash_rewards
is a reward type in the pool, and a seed generated with it is a seed that hands
out cash.
notes: Two more from Discord, 2026-09-09. CaptPurpleHeart pins the trigger: it only happens in a mission session where a cash bundle item was received; after that the glitch repeats endlessly, and changing mission stops it until another bundle arrives. So the ledger is per mission session and the refund replays it, which matches the read here. Likai proposes a stopgap: disable cash bundles, or default them off, until it is fixed.

title: A run with only community missions has no eligible missions
description:
[-SAM-], nightly, 2026-09-08:

| on the nightly I have every custom mission selected and no valve missions
| but it doesnt give me any eligible missions

Their screenshot shows the mission table with the community missions ticked and
the box reading, word for word:

| Selection is valid: 0 eligible mission(s) provide 0 checks for 0 unlocks.

Reproduced exactly. Three things line up to make it, and the first is mine.

1. mvm_community_missions is absent from a settings file written before the
   option existed, so it loads as false. parse calls withDefaults and then
   withAppearanceDefaults, and the second exists precisely because a bool that
   is absent and a bool that is off look the same after json.Unmarshal. It
   re-reads the raw bytes into a *bool for srcds_bot_hats and four others.
   mvm_community_missions is not among them.

2. That flag did nothing to the pool until 3dfbc80. runshape.Pool now counts the
   way the generator counts, community flag included, which is right and is what
   apw-2kw was about. It also made a field that silently loads as false into the
   one that empties the pool.

3. No interface has a row for it. form.Specs declares nothing for
   MvmCommunityMissions, so a player whose file says false cannot turn it back
   on from the window or the terminal. Only MVM_COMMUNITY_MISSIONS in the
   environment reaches it.

And the table disagrees with the check: poolSpec reads MvmExcludedMissions and
nothing else, so every community mission draws as ticked while Pool.Missions
drops all of them.

Work: put mvm_community_missions in withAppearanceDefaults, give it a row, and
make the mission table say when a row is in the pool but not drawable.
notes:
Peppy and [-SAM-] are one person: the display name is "Peppy! Long time no see!",
which is how docs/en/discord-mvm-thread.md names them too.
Fixed. Three parts, matching the three causes.

- mvm_community_missions joins withAppearanceDefaults, so a file that predates
  the option loads it as the default rather than as off.
- It has a row now, Community missions on the Missions page, and the exception
  in coverage_test is gone. It said the field was superseded by CommunityPacks;
  it is not, the packs put files on disk and this decides what a seed may draw.
- A community mission row says "community missions are off" in the
  Compatibility column while the switch is off, so the table stops reading as
  full while the pool is empty.

title: The weapon buff provider fails its own probe, so no buff applies
description:
From Likai's web UI screenshot, 2026-09-08. Not reported: found in the log
behind it, which is why it is worth reading screenshots.

| [tf2_archipelago.smx] The private Archipelago provider attached to Likai but
| did not provide attributes.

Nine times between 01:18:10 and 01:22:07, about every thirty seconds, which is
WeaponBuffProviderRetrySeconds. So it is not one bad moment: for the whole of
that session the player had no working buff provider.

That line is the probe failing in weapon_buffs.inc:2416. The provider entity is
created and owned by the client, then the code proves it is really in the active
weapon's attribute chain: read mult_dmg, set "damage bonus" 1.01 on the provider,
read mult_dmg again. Unchanged means the provider is attached to the player and
reaching nothing, so it is removed and retried.

The probe is doing its job. What it is telling us is that on that server no
weapon buff could have applied at all, to that player, ever. That is upstream of
apw-jpm and apw-4ck: those are about which buffs behave wrongly, this is about
none of them arriving.

Unknown and worth finding out first: whether this is every player or that one,
and what is different about the weapon held at the moment of the probe. The same
log has the run working otherwise, so it is not a plugin that failed to load.

Ask Likai for the launcher.log or the debug bundle from that session, and for
whether they saw a buff land at any point in it.
notes:
Diagnosis only. The cause is not in the code and cannot be found without a
server and a client holding a weapon, so the bead stays open.

What was done: the failure now names which of the two it is.

- AcceptEntityInput(provider, "RunScriptCode") had its answer dropped. The
  provider is attached by asking VScript to run ReapplyProvision, because
  TF2Utils' wearable-equip offset is stale on current Windows TF2, so a server
  with no VScript VM refuses that input and every buff in the run silently does
  nothing. It reported as the provider not providing, which is the symptom two
  steps downstream: one is fixed by a server setting and the other in
  weapon_buffs.inc.
- The probe's own line now carries what was in hand, its item definition index
  and both readings, which is the question this bead asks and which no bundle
  could have answered.

Likai's screenshot shows VSCRIPT started in a later session, so VScript being
off is not the reading to reach for first. It is the other branch that has to
be told apart from a probe that is itself wrong for some weapon.

title: Sitting in the Bot Switcher restarts the server; applying quickly does not
description:
Sirknobbles, on nightly, 2026-09-07:

| also changing the bot team seems to restart the server but only like half the time
| i used nightly and thats when the server reset. also i narrowed it down to only
| resetting when i waited too long in the bot switch menu. if i did it fast enough,
| no reset

The repro is the useful half: the same change restarts the server or does not,
depending only on how long the window was open.

Nothing on the apply path is meant to be time-dependent. editSettingsOn takes a
settings snapshot when the window opens (gui_windows.go:731) and botlive.LiveOnly
compares it against what comes back. Bot team only means applyBotTeam and a
running mission that survives; anything else means Stop then start. A snapshot
that goes stale while the window is open makes LiveOnly false and restarts for a
change the player never made.

Two candidates, both of which fire on a delay and neither of which the bot team
causes:

- restartForSourcemod (gui_windows.go:302). SourceMod's updater fetches gamedata
  and the launcher restarts once to load it. It is guarded by sourcemodRestarted
  so it can fire at most once a session, which is what "only like half the time"
  looks like from the player's seat.
- Anything else that writes settings while the dialog is up.

No debug bundle for this one yet, and it decides between them: launcher.log
carries either "SourceMod updated its gamedata. Restarting the server to load it"
or "settings saved. Restarting the server to apply them", and those are two
different bugs.
notes:
Likai corroborates, 2026-09-07:

| yeah it should, that one i saw happen last night over and over while testing
| stuff

Fixed on main by 23d59d8. sourcemodUpdate holds the updater's restart while the
settings window is up and editSettingsOn takes it on the way out; a save that
restarts anyway drops it. Tested under Wine, not on a real Windows server, and
not in a release: it waits on apw-grt.

Likai's other line that afternoon, that fudging with settings often restarts the
server, is the restart the save itself does. That is apw-vip, not this.
