title: The launcher saves nothing and the install root cannot be changed
description:
From Discord, and now diagnosed from the reporter's debug bundle. Their name did not come with the paste.

> The Save button, however, doesn't seem to do anything, both in regards to this and trying to set server login token.
> as settings don't save period I can't set the server details and the like
> The path that the launcher is using (And that I seemingly cannot change) is C:/Users/[My Username]/tf2-archipelago. And no config.json file exists in said folder.

The bundle says what happened, and it is one cause with three faces.

Their config.json exists and is well formed. Its room block is ap_host archipelago.gg, ap_port 0, ap_tls true, which is exactly settings.Defaults(). So the room was never saved, and every other setting on that screen went with it.

launcher.log, 602 lines, has no line about saving at all. Not saved, not failed. It has the settings window opening at 02:32:56, 02:49:02 and 02:49:15, and 'AP_PORT is not set; create a room on archipelago.gg first' at 02:48:35 and 02:48:59 where they pressed Start. Then the bundle at 02:49:18.

So: Save called collect, ParseRoom refused whatever was in the room box, the window set a small label beside that box and returned. The reporter was on another page setting a login token, so they never saw it. Nothing was written and nothing was logged, which is why the bundle could not have told anybody either.

Three things were wrong and all three are fixed:

- A refused Save was a label on one page. It is a modal message box now, and the window switches to the page holding the reason before showing it. The terminal gets the same thing: a box over the rows, dismissed by any key.
- A refused Save wrote nothing to the log. It logs now, so the next bundle carries it.
- The write happened after the window closed, so a failure lost every answer on screen. settings.Persist is called while the window is up: on failure the window stays, the answers stay, and the message names the path. That path is the other half of the confusion, because config.json is under the OS config directory and they were looking in the install root.

Also fixed on the way: settings.NewRconPassword's error was dropped by both interfaces.

Left open deliberately, because it is a product call rather than a bug:

- An unparseable room refuses the whole Save, so a login token cannot be saved until a room exists. Arguably a server setting should not be blocked by a room the player has not made yet. The message now says where to go and offers Test mode, which is the smaller fix.
- The install root is still not on any settings page. The reporter wanted to move it. form's coverage test lists it in notOnAPage with the reason 'chosen by the installer screen before the settings exist', which was written for a first run and does not hold for somebody whose folder is in the wrong place.

Separate finding, filed on its own: the debug bundle collected crash dumps for stellaris.exe, Hearthstone.exe and ShiftAtMidnight.exe. It is sweeping a Windows crash folder rather than its own.
notes:
The install folder is a row on Player options now, with a Browse button in the window, and settings.Persist refuses an empty or relative one rather than letting MkdirAll fail somewhere the player cannot connect to the box that caused it.

'Show the settings file' is beside it, because 'Where is the config file?' was asked in as many words and nothing in the launcher would answer it. It opens the folder holding config.json rather than the file, since a fresh Windows install has nothing to open a .json with.

That leaves one thing on this bead, and it is a product call rather than a bug: an unparseable room still refuses the whole Save, so a login token cannot be saved before a room exists. The refusal now names the page and offers Test mode, which is the smaller half of it.
The room is pinged at Save now, and an unparseable or missing one no longer refuses it.

That last part reverses what the bead was filed against. Blocking the whole Save on the room was the mechanism: the reporter was setting a login token two pages from a field they could not see. A room they have not made yet is not a mistake, so the settings are written and the room is what they are told about afterwards.

launcher/internal/roomcheck does one websocket handshake with a 3s timeout. A room that completes it is listening and speaking the protocol, which is the whole question at Save time; the slot name, the seed and whether it is still up in an hour are the bridge's business when it connects for real.

Three outcomes, none of which refuse anything: live is a log line, no room configured points at archipelago.gg and offers Test mode, and a room that did not answer says so and says the settings are saved anyway because the launcher will keep trying.

One finding worth keeping: a host that does not resolve often takes longer than the timeout to say so, so the deadline is set by the time the error arrives and matching on it first reported a typo as 'it did not answer'. The specific condition has to be asked first.
close_reason:
Both halves shipped, and both are on nightly only. A refused Save is a modal that switches to the page holding the reason and logs itself (8e7eaaf); the room no longer refuses the whole Save, it is pinged and reported afterwards (98a4510); the install folder is a row on Player options with Browse and a "Show the settings file" button beside it, and Persist refuses an empty or relative one (792696b).

Neither of the two open items survives: the token can be saved before a room exists, and the install root is on a page.

Not confirmed by either reporter. Both were on v1.11.0 the whole time. On 2026-09-07 Roseburst was given a .bat setting TF2AP_INSTALL_ROOT and found it did not survive reopening the launcher, which it cannot on a build with no field for it, and Knux confirmed the hardcoded path independently. Cutting the release is apw-grt. Reopen if either of them hits this again on v1.12.0.

Two things this bead did not cover, filed separately: the launcher rewriting the player YAML over hand edits is apw-y6n.

title: Cleared missions turn into collected and stop counting for missionsanity
description:
kelly-cs, GitHub #16:

> I've noticed a case where maps I've cleared transition from "cleared" to "collected" which doesn't contribute to the completed missions count for missionsanity. So I've completed over 80% of missions for an 80% missionsanity run, but some of the missions moved to "collected" at some point. Haven't pinned down when/why this happens yet

Reading: the distinction is v1.10.0's (apw-4bt): a location checked by this server reads "cleared", one collected by another world's !collect reads "collected". A mission this server cleared should never move to the second column. Suspects: the bridge rebuilding its view from the server's checked_locations on reconnect, where a check both cleared here and collected elsewhere is only in the list once; or the goal counting the plugin's cleared set rather than the union. The cause is not in the report. Costs a player the run: the goal never fires.

title: The bridge drops the room every second: the data package is bigger than its read limit
description:
EMann's bundle, 2026-09-02, launcher 1.11.0-59a04aa, room archipelago.gg:54869, slot EMann. Fifty-nine times in the log, one to two seconds apart:

    connected to archipelago slot=EMann missions=8 goal=final_boss server_checks=2
    archipelago session ended, will retry
      error="failed to read: websocket: message too big: read limited at 4194305 bytes"

Nothing the player checks reaches the room while this loops.

## Cause, from the code

onConnected asks GetDataPackage for every game in the room (rememberNames collects them from SlotInfo). A public room holds many games, and one data package for all of them is past readLimitBytes = 4 << 20 in bridge/internal/apclient/client.go. coder/websocket closes the connection on an oversized frame, the client reconnects, onConnected runs again and asks again: the request does not check whether c.names already holds the names, only that games is non-empty.

## Fix

- Ask per game, one GetDataPackage each, so no single reply carries every game's tables. RoomInfo carries datapackage_checksums; skip a game whose checksum matches what the bridge already holds.
- Do not ask at all on a reconnect that kept its names, which the comment in rememberNames already promises.
- Either way the limit stays a guard, not a ceiling the normal path reaches. coder/websocket takes SetReadLimit(-1) to lift it, which is the wrong fix on its own: a runaway reply would then be memory.

Not fixed since v1.11.0: readLimitBytes and the request are unchanged on main.
close_reason: Fixed on main, 21abe38.

title: A panic on a background goroutine killed the launcher
description:
Found while auditing both repos for crashes, and fixed in the same pass.

The launcher had no recover() anywhere and ten long-lived goroutines. Go takes
the whole process down for a panic on any goroutine, so one nil map in the
SourceMod log watcher would close the window, stop supervising the server
somebody was playing on, and leave them a mission to replay.

Nothing had crashed this way in a report. It is filed because the audit is worth
recording: this is the crash class the archipelago repo had, as against the
engineer wedge which is the one the bots repo has.
close_reason:
Fixed. guard wraps the bridge, the game server, the SourceMod error watcher and
the supervisor, which are the four goroutines that outlive the call starting
them.

Not a swallow: the panic and its stack go to the log a debug bundle carries,
which is louder than the silent exit it replaces.

Two tests. The first caught a real mistake in itself rather than in the code: it
signalled from inside the guarded work, whose defers run while the panic is
still unwinding, so it read the result before recover had written it. Race
detector and lint clean.

Also audited in the same pass and found clean: the plugin's natives. Every
GetEntProp goes through HasProp and every RequestFrame callback through
MvM_IsPlayer, which checks IsClientInGame. That is the crash class the bots repo
had, in mvm-ijg, and this repo does not.

title: Saving a loadout does not reach the menus that assign it
description:
Reported: 'when creating a loadout, saving, it needs the whole settings to be
saved even if i just saved a new loadout to be able to assign it to a bot'.

The Windows settings window builds every loadout menu on the Team and Classes
pages once, from the library as it stood when the dialog opened. A walk ComboBox
keeps the model it was built with, so saving on the Loadouts page changed the
data and nothing on screen. Assigning a new loadout to a bot meant saving every
other setting, reopening, and coming back.

The TUI is not affected: save and remove both call build(), which makes the
fields again from the edited settings.

Wanted: the menus refill on save and on remove, and a menu whose loadout was
removed falls back to that class's stock.
close_reason:
Fixed. botTeamEditor.refreshLoadouts refills every seat and class loadout
menu, and the Loadouts page calls it after Save and after Remove.

The selection is put back by name rather than by index, because saving a
loadout inserts it among the others and every index after it moves; and by name
rather than by the whole label, because saving over a name changes the weapons
the label spells out and the menu should stay on the loadout the seat still
names. A removed loadout falls back to index zero, which is the class's stock.

reselectLoadout carries that rule and lives in the non-Windows file, so three
tests cover it: one asserts the new loadout really did shift the picked index
before checking the pick survived, or it would prove nothing.

Also fixed while here: botTeamEditor.show resolved a saved team's loadouts with
class.LoadoutByKey, which knows nothing about custom ones, so loading a team
that named a custom loadout showed stock. It goes through the library now.

title: A buff menu opens itself at the upgrade station and takes the number keys
description:
Reported 2026-08-27: "the buff thing that shows on the left of the screen, wtf
is that?"

It is a SourceMod menu, which TF2 draws down the left, listing every weapon buff
on the current loadout. WeaponBuffs_ShowMenu, called from
MvM_OnCommandKeyValues on MvM_UpgradesBegin: it opens itself every time the
player opens the upgrade station, and stays for twenty seconds.

Came in with the weapon buffs in PR #3.

## Why it is worse than clutter

A SourceMod menu takes the number keys while it is up. In MvM the number keys
are weapon slots, so for twenty seconds at the station the player cannot switch
weapons with them, and nothing on screen says why.

It also arrives unasked. Reading your buffs is a thing you want when you want
it; the station is where you are already reading a different menu.

## What it should probably be

The information is worth having, so this is about how it arrives:

- on request, as a chat command beside !ap bots and !ap status, rather than
  automatically
- or as a panel or hint text, which draws without taking the keys
- and if it stays automatic, it wants an obvious way out and a much shorter life
  than twenty seconds

Worth asking kelly-cs what he intended before changing it, since he built it and
may have had a reason for the station specifically.
notes:
2026-08-29: the chat command half of this is now apw-z7o, filed after the player found no way to open the window by hand. That bead also carries the report that it stopped opening on its own.

## The two buff-window beads pull opposite ways (2026-09-05)

apw-pni wants the window not to open by itself at the upgrade station, because a SourceMod menu takes the number keys and in MvM those are weapon slots. apw-z7o wants it to open by itself, because it used to. Both are open and both are accurate: whoever takes either has to answer for the other.

Where the code stands: MvM_OnCommandKeyValues still calls WeaponBuffs_ShowMenu on MvM_UpgradesBegin (mvm.inc, around line 345), so it does open itself. What changed is that a loadout with no buffs draws no window rather than an empty one. The number keys are still taken for a loadout that has buffs.

The chat commands are done either way: !ap buffs, !ap buff and !apbuffs.
close_reason: The station no longer opens a menu. It lists the loadout's buffs in chat once per visit, which takes no keys, and !ap buffs opens the window on request. Both lists come from one function.

title: Mannhunt crashes far more than any other map
description:
Mannhunt crashes far more than any other mission. Access violations, 0xc0000005.

## What is solid

k-kaneta's bundle of 2026-08-27 has three, two of them on Mannhunt, both at wave
one, both preceded within three seconds by an engineer stuck at 1014 885 274.
The same log then loads Mannhunt with no engineer on RED and clears three waves.
That control is the strongest thing on this bead.

## What is fixed

The engineer wedge itself. The recovery could never move a bot standing on valid
nav, which is every wedge of this shape, fixed in defenderbots v2.21.3 and
measured under load against the old behaviour: nought of six waves cleared
before, six of nine after, two more runs agreeing.

## What is not known

Why the server died. I spent a day asserting a path cost mechanism, a wedged bot
asking for an impossible path and burning the frame the watchdog kills. v2.30.0
times every path compute; a run with the wedge held, the goal made impossible and
the old recovery in place logged no search over 20ms. Five approaches, about
thirty five attempts: no crash, no in-wave stall, no expensive search. The
mechanism is refuted.

## Why it cannot be answered yet

No crash dump. The bundle carried two access violations and nothing that names
the faulting function, so every conclusion so far is inference from bot
behaviour near a timestamp.

## Next

The launcher now starts srcds with -debug, which writes debug.log with a stack
on a crash without depending on Breakpad, and the debug bundle collects it. The
next Mannhunt crash should arrive with the function named. Until then this bead
is waiting on evidence, not on work.
notes:
## A crash of this exact shape was found and fixed in the mod (2026-09-05)  
                                                                            
mvm-qhi in tf2-mvm-bots-go: a defender stuck at the spawn exit is teleported
to a recovery area, the tick after the teleport never finishes, the watchdog
fires and srcds dies. That is 'a wedged bot asking for an impossible path   
and burning the frame the watchdog kills', which is the mechanism this bead 
spent a day asserting and could not prove.                                  
                                                                            
Two causes, both fixed: the destination was any random point of a nav area  
with no check that a body fits there, and the repath was forced into the    
very next tick. The recovery now traces a standing hull at the point and    
draws again up to eight times, and the repath is half a second to a second  
later like every other caller. Measured on Mannworks with two recoveries,   
one natural and one forced, wave cleared, no watchdog.                      
                                                                            
Shipped here at tf2-mvm-bots-go v0.13.0, pinned in go.mod. Not confirmed as 
this bead's crash: the reports are Windows access violations on Mannhunt and
the fix was measured on Linux on Mannworks. The next Mannhunt bundle is what
says whether this was it.                                                   

## A crash with a name (2026-09-06)

Mannworks on the bots test-bed, mod 2.51.0 plus the day's branch, shortly after wave 1 began: WatchDog, Host_Error, segmentation fault, core.131. Symbolised with the bots repository's testbed/symbolise-core.sh: the watchdog fired inside CTFBotLocomotion::IsAreaTraversable under NavAreaBuildPath, called from CBaseNPC's Path::Compute with maxPathLength=0, from the path follower's ComputeToTarget, from a plugin action's Update through actions.ext. So the mechanism this bead recorded as refuted is what killed this server: an unbounded path computation to an entity, from a behaviour's Update, walking the whole mesh. The mod's FEATURE_PATH_LENGTH_CAP answered true zero times in that session's wave lines, so the cap was off. Not Mannhunt, not a held wedge, same signature. The injector run that follows measures the cap against it.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Confirmed by the reporter, and it is the engineer. This is the proof that the
engineer AI causes the crashes.

  omaewh4: "Did you have an engineer in the team? Can you try without one?
            they might be the source of those crashes, when they get stuck"
  k-kaneta: "ok mannhunt works if there is no engie"

A map that crashes reliably with an engineer and does not crash without one is
about as clean a control as a play-test produces. It was a hypothesis from the
test-bed until now; a player removing one variable settled it.

It matches what was measured on Mannworks: a wedged bot asks for a path, is
reset, comes back to the same wedge and asks again, and the watchdog kills the
server inside NavAreaBuildPath. mvm-ipf already records an engineer stuck inside
a prop on this very map, so the where is known as well.

## What follows

v2.20.1 moves a bot that is wedged after three stucks at one spot, and it took
Mannworks with Mean Machines from crashing at wave zero to four waves and no
crash. k-kaneta was almost certainly on a build without it.

So the next step is not more diagnosis. It is Mannhunt on the test-bed with the
current build and an engineer in the lineup: if it still crashes the recovery is
not catching this wedge, and the stuck line will say where.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Mannhunt is a community map, not one of Valve's. The test-bed has the seven
Valve MvM maps and nothing else, so reproducing this needs the community assets
fetched first, through the support kelly-cs added in PR #2.

That is worth knowing rather than a detail:

- it arrived with community map support, so it is the first crash report from
  that feature
- community nav meshes are not held to Valve's standard, which is the whole
  reason kelly-cs needed the spawn recovery in tf2-mvm-bots#1 before the maps
  were usable at all
- a bot wedged in geometry is likelier on a map whose mesh nobody at Valve

So the wedge recovery in v2.20.1 is the right shape for it, and whether it
catches this particular geometry is still unmeasured.

Next step, in order: fetch Mannhunt through the launcher's community assets,
put it on the test-bed with an engineer in the lineup, and read the crash the
way run.sh reports it. mvm-ipf holds the prop this map is known to wedge on.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Correcting myself: Mannhunt is not a community map.

It is an Invasion mission on Mannworks, and Mannworks is Valve's. I searched the
installed maps for a mannhunt.bsp, did not find one, and concluded the map was
missing. The map was never missing: the mission is a popfile on a map the
test-bed already has.

So everything I wrote about community assets and unvetted nav meshes is beside
the point, and worse, it pointed the next step at fetching something that does
not need fetching.

What it actually means is better: Mannworks is the map I already reproduced the
engineer wedge on, at 1014 885 274, and where the wedge recovery took a run from
crashing at wave zero to four clean waves. Mannhunt is a different mission over
that same geometry.

So this is testable now, on the build that has the fix.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Wording first: Mannhunt is a mission, mvm_mannworks_intermediate2, on the
Mannworks map. This bead's title says 'map' and that is wrong. The reports are
about the mission.

The evidence for the crash is strong, and it comes from k-kaneta's bundle of
2026-08-27 rather than from a test-bed run. Three access violations, 0xc0000005.
Two were on Mannhunt, both at 1014 885 274, both wave 1, both after exactly
three engineer stuck cycles twelve seconds apart, crashing on the third. The
control is in the same log: at 21:13 Mannhunt loads again with no engineer on
RED and clears waves 1, 2 and 3. That is k-kaneta's 'mannhunt works if there is
no engie' with a coordinate attached.

The wedge is not always fatal. That coordinate appears ten times across five
different engineer bots and only twice does the server die, so the wedge is the
condition and something else decides.

What cannot be done yet is verify any of it. [[mvm-ed0]] blocks this bead
completely. Every Mannhunt run in the test-bed produces a wave where every
counter is zero for the whole timeout: no robot kills, no deaths, no damage, no
credits. No robot ever spawns and the timeout is recorded as a loss. A run that
spawns no robots cannot crash on an engineer fighting them, so 'no crash in
three attempts' means nothing.

Two engineer fixes have shipped since that bundle, both real and both aimed
here: defenderbots v2.21.3 let the wedge recovery leave the area the bot stands
in, and v2.22.0 let the watchdog see a bot with no behaviour at all. Neither has
been shown to help on this mission, because this mission cannot be measured yet.

Diagnostic queued: mvm_mannworks on two other missions, to say whether the stall
follows the map or the popfile.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
A second fix, aimed at the crash rather than at the wedge, defenderbots v2.26.0.

The forced-wedge run said something the earlier runs could not. With
sm_redbots_debug_wedge_seconds holding an engineer in place, twelve wedges
produced 36 stuck lines and not one successful recovery: MoveWedgedDefender was
reached every time and refused every time, even with the v2.21.3 fix in.

So a bot the recovery cannot help is not rare, and the crash does not need the
recovery to work. What the cores show is the cost, not the wedge: a bot that
cannot reach its goal asks for a path again on every reset, NavAreaBuildPath
walks the mesh for an answer that does not exist, and the watchdog kills the
server on that frame.

After eight wedges the bot is now kicked, with his buildings, and the seat
refilled by the top-up path a moment later with a bot that can walk. Behind
sm_redbots_feature_kick_wedged_bots, default off.

This is the belt to the recovery's braces. If the recovery is fixed later the
kick should almost never fire, and its log line says when it does.

Why the recovery refuses is still open and now instrumented: v2.25.1 logs the
wedge count and which of the two refusals MoveWedgedDefender took. That run is
queued behind the Mannhunt console capture.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Correction to the note two comments up: the wedge recovery does fire. 114
successful moves in the SourceMod log, each naming where the bot went. I had
read a multi-file grep -c as a total and reported zero.

title: A shield gives the Demoman a locked secondary back
description:
Discord, 2026-08-27, k-kaneta: "Demo can still charge without secondary, if you
use shield"

The run locks weapon slots until the multiworld hands them over. A Demoman whose
secondary is still locked can equip a shield and charge with it, so the lock is
bypassed and the check it was gating is worth nothing.

## The likely mechanism

Unlocks_Strip walks the slots and calls TF2_RemoveWeaponSlot for each one that
is not open (unlocks.inc:371). That removes a weapon.

A shield is not a weapon. The Chargin' Targe and its kin are tf_wearable_demoshield
entities: they sit in the secondary slot of the loadout and never appear in
GetPlayerWeaponSlot, so the strip walks past them. The charge comes off the
shield's own attributes, which are still on the player.

## What else this would cover

Any other wearable that occupies a slot the same way. The Sniper's Razorback and
Darwin's Danger Shield are the obvious pair, both secondary. Worth checking
whether they survive a locked secondary too, because the fix is the same one.

## How to check it

Lock the secondary, spawn a Demoman with a shield, and see whether the shield is
still worn and the charge still available. The strip already logs; it just has
nothing to say about an entity it never looked at.
close_reason: Fixed on main, added65: slot-filling wearables are removed with the lock, by class and defindex. Compiled; not yet watched on a server.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The same hole, with the opposite symptom. k-kaneta, minutes after the shield
report:

  "wonder what happens with boots"
  "lmao he holds nothing"

are tf_wearable, not weapons. So with the primary locked, TF2_RemoveWeaponSlot
finds no weapon to take and the boots stay on: he has no primary in hand and is
left holding nothing.

Two symptoms, one cause. A wearable in a locked slot is invisible to the strip,
and depending on the item that either hands back an ability the lock was meant
to take (the shield's charge) or leaves the player with no weapon at all (the
boots).

So the fix has to remove the wearable as well as the weapon, and then make sure
something is in his hands afterwards. SwitchToAnyWeapon already exists for the
case where the strip removed what he was holding.

title: Nobody can tell whether the server needs our seed or theirs
description:
Discord, 2026-08-27, Red (xLander), who could not work it out from the docs:

  "what's the deal with make seed? Is there a reason the multiworld is generated
   by the makefile here rather than the standard archipelago generation?"

lacking for docker deployment part?"

## The actual question, which the docs never answer

Is the server seed-agnostic? Somebody joining an existing multiworld does not
want to generate anything: they want to point the stack at a room and a slot.
make seed is a convenience for people starting from nothing, and it reads as a
requirement.

That is a first-contact problem. Somebody who already runs Archipelago is the
most likely person to try this, and they are the ones it confuses.

Say it in the first paragraph of the install pages, before make seed appears:

- the stack plays a room that already exists, and AP_HOST, AP_PORT and
  AP_SLOT_NAME are all it needs
- make seed is one way to get a room, for people who have none, and nothing
  more
- generating the normal way and pointing the stack at the result is supported
  and is the same thing

Then check the Docker page answers it too, since that is where he was.

title: Only Valve's six maps, and the community has hundreds
description:
What kelly-cs's PR #2 solves, alongside its prerequisite mvm-78m in
tf2-mvm-bots.

## The problem

A run draws from Valve's own missions and nothing else, so every run visits the
same six maps. potato.TF and the rest have hundreds, and the run has no way to
reach them.

Nothing bundles third-party assets, so the work is not "ship more maps": it is
letting somebody fetch them, checking what they fetched is usable, and refusing
what is not.

## What the PR does

- a validated community mission catalogue, with the assets fetched rather than
  bundled, and a local ZIP import for people who already have them
- Valve and community missions kept visibly apart in the launcher
- maps with no bot .nav file shown in red and unselectable, because a map the
  bots cannot walk is a mission nobody can win
- checks the selected pool can satisfy the run before generation, rather than
  finding out at the seed
- installs maps, popfiles, nav meshes and custom upgrade files on Windows and
  Linux
- raises net_maxfilesize to 64 MB, since the default 16 breaks the downloads

## Why the prerequisite exists

On some community maps the bots have a nav mesh and still never leave spawn.
That is mvm-78m, merged as tf2-mvm-bots#1, and without it a drawn community map
can be a mission the team stands in spawn for.

## Worth knowing

The nav check is the part that keeps this honest: it refuses a map rather than
letting a run draw one the bots cannot play. That is the same rule the weapon
catalogue follows, where a menu entry the mod cannot drive is worse than a
missing one.
close_reason: Shipped. kelly-cs's PR #2 merged in 20479f6, CI and nightly green: community missions fetched rather than bundled, Valve and community kept apart in the list, maps without a bot nav file refused, and the pool checked against the run before generation.

title: A server restart makes the team replay the mission
description:
From play, 2026-08-26: the server stutters and crashes on Mannhattan, and when
it comes back the team has the whole mission to do again.

"that should be NEVER happening", and that is the right bar. A crash is a bug to
fix; a crash that costs an evening's progress is a design fault on top of it,
and this half can be fixed without fixing the crash.

## What survives a restart today, and what does not

The bridge writes every check to disk, so the Archipelago half is safe: the
unlocks and the items come back. bridge/internal/state holds seed, checks,
items, acked_seq, goal_sent and the last check.

Nothing holds where the team actually was. SrcdsStartMission is the popfile the
server loads first, and its own comment says it is "never written again". So a
restarted server loads the mission the settings name, at wave 1, whatever the
team had cleared.

That is the whole of "everything to redo": the mission they were playing and
every wave they had won inside it.

## The fix has a mechanism already

tf_mvm_jump_to_wave is a cheat command and the test-bed already drives it
(testbed/run.sh:225). It grants the credits of the waves it skipped, which is
exactly what a team arriving at that wave would have held, so the restore does
not hand anybody a wave they have to play underfunded.

So the shape is:

1. The plugin knows the popfile and the wave. Write both somewhere durable
   whenever a wave completes, next to the checks rather than in the settings:
   the settings are what somebody configured, and this is what happened.
2. On start, if that record names a mission the run has unlocked, load it and
   jump to the wave after the last one cleared.
3. Say so in the chat, or a player who crashed mid wave 4 cannot tell a restored
   run from a lost one.

## What to be careful about

- Only restore forward. A record that names a wave the team never reached is a
  way to skip content, so the wave written is the one after the last completed
  and nothing else.
- The jump needs sv_cheats and puts it back. A server left with cheats on is
  worse than a lost mission.
- A finished mission clears the record, or the next start drops the team into
  the end of a mission they already beat.
- Test mode and a real room both need it, because a crash does not care.

## Related

mvm-cf3 in tf2-mvm-bots is the crash and the stutter, now P0 as well. This bead
is the cost of the crash and is worth doing whether or not that one lands.
close_reason: Both halves shipped and the bead's comment saying the plugin does not read the record is out of date. The bridge keeps the Resume beside the checks, moves it forward on a cleared wave and clears it on a cleared mission (c8b622f); the plugin reads it off /missions on start, refuses a record naming a wave at or past the mission's end so it can only restore forward, announces the restore in chat, and puts sv_cheats back to what it was around tf_mvm_jump_to_wave (291e12a). deploy/integration-test.sh asserts the popfile and the wave on /missions after a clear. Not watched through a real crash on a live server: reopen if a restart ever drops a team at wave one again.

title: Knobs for bot damage and health, so the balance can be measured
description:
Asked for directly: "Balancing (damage, health, will see what works and what
doesn't)".

The second half of that sentence is the whole design. Nobody knows yet what the
right numbers are, so the deliverable is not a number: it is the pair of knobs
plus a way to read what moving them did.

## Why it is not just a convar

Valve tunes every wave for six defenders. The bots exist so fewer can win, and
whether they do is unmeasured. docs/testbed-metrics.md is the standing rule
here: a change to how the bots fight ships on only once a run has said it
helped.

So this bead is three things, in order:

1. Two convars, `sm_redbots_manager_bot_damage_scale` and
   `sm_redbots_manager_bot_health_scale`, both defaulting to 1.0 so the mod
   plays exactly as it does today until somebody asks otherwise.
2. Feature switches in source/redbots3/features.sp, so the two arms of an A/B
   are the same build.
3. An A/B on at least two maps, because mvm-15t exists precisely because a
   one-map result was not trusted.

## What to watch

Deaths per wave and waves lost are the numbers that decide it, and
testbed/results/ holds what the current build does. A damage scale that wins
waves by making the bots do the players' job for them is not a win: the run has
to stay a run.

## Where it is exposed

If it ships, the launcher's Bots page gets the two, and the .env gets
`SRCDS_BOT_DAMAGE_SCALE` and `SRCDS_BOT_HEALTH_SCALE` beside the team size,
which is the knob that does this job crudely today.

title: A sentry buster blowing itself up counts as the giant kill
description:
Reported from a nightly run on Decoy. A sentry buster detonating on a sentry is
announced as "Giant killed" and sends the mission's giant check.

## Why

`MvM_IsGiant` in `plugin/scripting/tf2_archipelago/mvm.inc` asks one question:
is this a BLU fake client with `m_bIsMiniBoss` set. A sentry buster carries that
property, so it answers yes. `Event_PlayerDeath` in `tf2_archipelago.sp:345`
fires on the buster's death like any other, and the check goes out.

The detonation is a death like any other as far as the event is concerned. The
buster does not even have to be killed by anybody.

## The part that is worse than a wrong announcement

`g_GiantReported` latches. `Event_PlayerDeath` returns immediately once it is
set, and it is only cleared at wave 1 of a mission. So the buster does not just
send a wrong check, it **spends the mission's only giant check**. The real giant
that dies later in the run reports nothing, because the flag is already true.

That makes this quieter than it looks. On any mission with a buster before the
first giant, the giant objective is decided by a robot blowing itself up, and
nothing in the log says the real one was missed.

## Fix

The sibling repo already solved the detection, and it is one string compare.
`tf2-mvm-bots`, `source/redbots3/util.sp:534`:

    bool IsSentryBusterRobot(int client)
    // ... GetClientModel, then
    // StrEqual(model, "models/bots/demo/bot_sentry_buster.mdl")

Add the same test to `MvM_IsGiant` and return false for it. Same approach, same
model path, already proven against live servers by the bot mod, and it needs no
new gamedata.

## One decision to make first

Whether a buster counts when players **kill** it rather than letting it
detonate. The report is about self-detonation, but a buster is not a giant
either way, and the simpler rule is that a buster is never a giant. The
alternative, excluding it only when it kills itself, needs the `player_death`
attacker compared with the victim and leaves the odd case where shooting one
counts and letting it go does not.

Recommend excluding the buster outright. It is one rule rather than two, and it
matches what a player means by "we killed a giant".

## Test

The testbed can drive this: spawn a buster, let it detonate, and confirm no
`giant_killed` objective reaches the bridge and that `g_GiantReported` stays
false so a later giant still reports.
close_reason: Fixed. MvM_IsGiant now returns false for the sentry buster model, using the same test the defender bot mod already ships in source/redbots3/util.sp. Excluded outright rather than only on self-detonation, which is one rule instead of two. Plugin compiles clean.

title: The grant watchdog fights the deliberate wait, and restarts the poll every five seconds
description:
Not reported by anybody. Found in k-kaneta's second bundle while chasing the
crash. `launcher.log` holds this line 282 times in one session:

    [AP] debug: The grant poll had stopped. The plugin starts it again.

Every five seconds, from the first grant to the end of the session.

## What starts it

The first one lands right after the first held grant:

    20:28:48  launcher test mode: Bram sent us something
    20:28:48  srcds  [AP] 200 credits are waiting for the upgrade station.
    20:28:48  srcds  [AP] debug: The grant poll had stopped. The plugin starts it again.

"Waiting for the upgrade station" is the hold. `OnGrants` handles it at
`plugin/scripting/tf2_archipelago/bridge.inc:687`, and the comment says exactly
what it means to do:

> A held effect leaves the cursor behind the bridge, so the next poll answers
> at once with the same grant. Asking straight away would be a loop as fast as
> the loopback; asking on the retry timer is what turns the hold into a wait
> for the upgrade station.

So it calls `Bridge_PollGrantsLater()` and returns, leaving `g_PollingGrants`
false on purpose while the retry timer runs.

`Timer_DrainPending` at line 273 then sees exactly that:

    if (g_HaveUnlocks && !g_PollingGrants)

and cannot tell a loop that died from a loop that is deliberately waiting. It
logs, and calls `Bridge_PollGrants()`.

## Why it never settles

Both timers use the same constant:

    #define RetryInterval 5.0

The watchdog is `CreateTimer(RetryInterval, Timer_DrainPending, _, TIMER_REPEAT)`
at line 106. The hold's retry is `CreateTimer(RetryInterval, Timer_PollAgain)`
at line 639. Identical intervals, so the watchdog lands in the same window as
the pending retry every single time. It is not a rare race, it is the normal
case, which is why the count is 282 and not 3.

## What it costs

Three things, in rising order of seriousness.

1. The debug log. 282 lines of a message that means "something is wrong" when
   nothing is. A debug bundle is only worth what it holds, and this drowns it.
2. Two live schedules for one loop. The watchdog's poll and the pending
   `Timer_PollAgain` both fire, so grant requests overlap where the design says
   one connection sits open.
3. The hold stops holding. The whole point of `Bridge_PollGrantsLater` is to
   wait for the upgrade station instead of spinning on the loopback. The
   watchdog re-asks anyway, so the wait it buys is gone.

## Fix

The watchdog needs to distinguish "no request in flight and none scheduled"
from "no request in flight". Track the scheduled retry — a `g_GrantRetryDue`
flag set in `Bridge_PollGrantsLater` and cleared in `Timer_PollAgain` — and
have `Timer_DrainPending` skip when it is set.

The same shape applies to the other three loops the watchdog covers.
`Bridge_PollMessagesAgain` (line 830) and `Bridge_PollDeathsAgain` (line 887)
schedule retries on the same constant against the same `!g_PollingChat` and
`!g_PollingDeaths` tests, so they can misfire the same way. They do not show up
here only because nothing held them during this session. Fix all four together
rather than patching the one the log caught.

Keep the watchdog. Its comment explains why it exists — a native error in a
callback ends a self-sustaining loop with no timer left to notice — and that
reasoning is still right. It just has to stop counting a planned wait as a
death.
close_reason: Fixed. The four loops record a retry deadline and the watchdog skips a loop with one booked, plus a one-second grace so it does not race a retry landing on the same poll. A deadline rather than a flag keeps the watchdog's guarantee: a retry that never arrives falls back to it. Chat, deaths and unlocks were fixed alongside grants; they had the same shape and only escaped because nothing held them in the bundle.

title: A blacklisted class still gets drawn into a partial lineup
description:
Cowser, on native Linux, running 1.9.0:

> i also have spy blacklisted for bots but nope

His screenshot shows the RED lineup with a Spy in it. The seven names on it —
Cowser, The Combine, DeadHead, Kill Me, MindlessElectrons, Grim Bloody Fable,
LOS LOS LOS — are exactly the seven upgrade buyers in the `console.log` of his
bundle, so the screenshot and the logs are the same session. (It is also the
same session as apw-49k, which is why there are seven of them.)

Bot class is never printed to the log, so the logs neither confirm nor deny
this. The screenshot is the evidence.

## Not the checkboxes

Ruled out. His `config.json` holds `"srcds_bot_class_blacklist": ["spy"]`, so
the TUI toggle recorded the change correctly. Whatever went wrong is
downstream of the widget.

## Two causes, and both are real

**apw-2sw is the first**, split out because it is much larger than this bead:
the TUI never calls `srcdsconfig.Install`, so his `server.cfg` was rendered
before he unticked the Spy and never rewritten. That server ran with
`sm_redbots_manager_class_blacklist ""` for the whole session. Fix that and
this session stops reproducing.

**This bead is the second**, and it survives the fix. Live in current code,
not just 1.9.0. His settings are `srcds_bot_team_comp: ["scout"]` and
`srcds_bot_class_blacklist: ["spy"]`:

    botloadout.Composition([]string{"scout"}, []string{"spy"})  =>  "scout"

One named seat, six to fill. Our own generated `server.cfg` states the rule
next to the convar: "A team named here beats the blacklist above." So the mod
draws the other five itself, and nothing is stopping it drawing a Spy. A
correctly rendered blacklist would not have helped, because the lineup outranks
it.

`Composition` already knows this matters. When the lineup is empty and the
blacklist is not, it pads out to `botSeats` so that a team of nothing but draws
still writes its seats — the comment says as much. The gap is that the padding
only happens when `seats` is empty. A lineup with one entry in it skips the
pad and hands five seats back to the mod.

## Fix

Pad to the team size whenever the blacklist is non-empty, not only when the
lineup is empty. The trailing-empty trim above it must not then undo the pad.
`Composition(["scout"], ["spy"])` should render six seats, not one.

Check the padding actually does what the empty-lineup case assumes — that a
written empty seat respects the blacklist while an unwritten one does not. If
that is not true, then the blacklist cannot be honoured through the lineup at
all, and it has to be enforced on our side after the mod picks.

## Test

A table test on `Composition` covers the fix. Reproducing the original needs
apw-2sw fixed first, or the blacklist never reaches the server to be beaten.
close_reason: Fixed. Composition now pads to the team size whenever the blacklist is non-empty, not only when the lineup is empty, so no seat is left for the mod to draw without consulting it. Three new tests cover the short lineup, the no-blacklist case, and a lineup longer than the settings page offers. Two existing expectations changed because they encoded the old behaviour on blacklisted input.

title: [bug] The bridge stops and drops the room, repeatedly
description:
k-kaneta, playing 1.9.0:

> and "bridge stopping" then disconnecting is still common issue to me

"Still" and "common", so this is neither new nor rare, and it has never been
filed with a cause attached.

## No evidence yet, and that is the first job

Cowser's debug bundle was collected the same day and does not show this: his
`bridge.json` reads `connected: true` with an empty `last_error`, and his
console log has no bridge stop in it. Different player, different machine, so
his bundle cannot settle it either way.

Ask k-kaneta for a debug bundle taken after it happens. Specifically wanted:

- `bridge.json`, for `last_error` and `last_check` at the time of the drop
- the launcher log around the "bridge stopping" line
- whether the room is `archipelago.gg` hosted or self-hosted, and whether the
  TF2 server keeps running when the bridge goes

## What to look at meanwhile

"Bridge stopping" is our own message, so find every place that emits it and
work out which one fires. The distinction that matters: the bridge deciding to
stop, versus the bridge dying and the supervisor reporting it. Those are
different bugs and the current message does not tell them apart.

Make the message say which. Whatever the cause turns out to be, "bridge
stopping" with no reason attached is why this report has gone unfixed long
enough to be described as common.

Then check the reconnect path. ADR 0002 argues for a long-lived bridge
precisely so a dropped room comes back on its own. If a stop means the player
has to restart, the behaviour the ADR specifies is not what ships.
close_reason: Superseded by apw-r85. k-kaneta's second bundle shows the launcher log, and it inverts this bead's premise: the game server crashes with 0xc0000005 and the launcher's own shutdown prints 'bridge stopping' on the way out. The bridge is not the failing component. Everything asked for here is now in apw-r85 with the evidence attached.

title: RED overfills to seven, and the returning player is sent to spectator
description:
Cowser, on native Linux, playing 1.9.0 with bot fill set to 6:

> oh fuck the first one has 7 players
> ok what is with the 7 players

His debug bundle carries the proof, and the cause is in our code. His
screenshot of the RED lineup shows the seven slots directly.

## What the log shows

At 07:58:47 the fill decision is right:

    RED holds 1 of 6 between waves. 5 bot(s) take the empty seats.

taken=1 is Cowser, RED holds no bots, so it asks for 5. Then seven distinct
names buy upgrades in that same session: Cowser plus The Combine, Kill Me,
DeadHead, Grim Bloody Fable, MindlessElectrons and LOS LOS LOS. Six bots, not
five. `sm_addbots 5` added six.

Those are the same seven names as on the screenshot, so the screenshot, the
log and apw-ygn are all one session.

The previous session in the same bundle added five and stayed at six total, so
the overshoot is not every time.

Then, at the end of that session:

    MVM assigned Cowser the Khelinace to spectator, all slots for defending
    team are in use, or reserved for lobby members

That is the second half of the complaint. RED was full of bots, so the human
could not get back on it.

## Cause

`Bots_TrimSurplus` already exists and already knows about the overshoot; its
own comment says "one ask can add more than it asked for". The problem is when
it runs. `plugin/scripting/tf2_archipelago/bots.inc:490` calls it at the *top*
of `Bots_Fill`, before the `sm_addbots` on line 528. So a poll trims the
previous poll's surplus, never its own.

That would self-correct on the next poll, except `Bots_Fill` returns early at
line 477 unless the round state is `RoundState_BetweenRounds`. Once the wave
starts, the poll returns before it reaches the trim, and the surplus bot rides
out the whole wave in a seat that belongs to a player.

## Fix

Trim after the add, not only before it. `Timer_TrimBots` is already a one-shot
timer built for exactly this, and it is currently only ever fired from inside
`Bots_Fill`. Arm it after the `sm_addbots` so the count settles once the mod
has taken its turn.

Then make the trim reachable during a wave. Either drop the `BetweenRounds`
guard for the trim path, or fire `Timer_TrimBots` on the round-start hook. A
surplus bot found mid-wave should still leave, since the seat it holds is what
sends the player to spectator.

Note the two counts disagree on spectators, and that is deliberate on the fill
side: `Bots_Fill` counts any connected human as holding a seat, while
`Bots_TrimSurplus` counts RED only. Keep the fill rule. Make sure the trim
never picks a seat the fill is holding for a human, or the two will fight.

## Test

The testbed can drive this: fill to 6, confirm the count settles at 6 and not
7, then disconnect and reconnect the human mid-mission and confirm they land on
RED rather than spectator.
close_reason: Fixed. Timer_TrimBots is armed after sm_addbots as well as before it, so a poll trims its own overshoot instead of leaving it for a poll that returns early once the wave starts. Bots_TrimSurplus now uses the same seat arithmetic as Bots_Fill via Bots_SeatsHeldOffRed, so RED stops being held full of bots while a reconnecting player sits in spectator. Plugin compiles clean. Not reproduced end to end: the testbed check in the bead (fill to 6, disconnect, reconnect mid-mission) is still worth running.

title: The Docker install downloads a .env.example that 404s
description:
The Docker quick start in both languages tells a player to run

    base=https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/releases/latest/download
    curl -fsSL -o .env "$base/.env.example"

and that URL returns 404. Checked against v1.9.0 today: .env.example is 404,
default.env.example is 200.

The cause is the upload, not the docs. `gh release create` renames a file whose
name starts with a dot, so deploy/.env.example lands on the release as
default.env.example. It has been that way on every release, and it is on the
nightly prerelease too, because both jobs upload the same asset list.

Note curl -fsSL is silent on failure by design, so the player gets no error and
no .env, then hits SRCDS_RCONPW being unset several steps later with nothing
pointing back here.

Two ways to fix it and they are not equal.

Rename the asset so the documented name is the real one: copy it to
dist/env.example in `make dist` and upload that, then say curl -o .env
"$base/env.example". No leading dot, nothing to rename, and the same URL works
on a release and on nightly. The docs change with it.

Or leave the upload alone and fix four documents to say default.env.example.
Cheaper now and it keeps a name that reads like an accident, which somebody will
try to correct later.

The first one. Whichever is chosen, the files to change are
docs/en/setup/install.md, docs/fr/setup/install.md and the index page in both
languages, and the fix wants checking with a real curl rather than by reading.
close_reason: Fixed by renaming the asset, which was the recommended option: dist carries env.example with no leading dot, both workflows upload that name, and the two install pages plus their surrounding prose fetch it. Not verified against a live release URL, because GitHub Actions is in a major outage and no release or nightly has completed since the change. The 200/404 check should be redone once one does.

title: Bots have never been paid a Cash Bundle
description:
Every Cash Bundle the run receives goes to the humans only. The bot team, which
in most runs is five of the six seats, has never seen a credit of Archipelago
money.

MvM_GrantCredits in mvm.inc walks the clients and pays each one that passes
MvM_IsPlayer, and MvM_IsPlayer is:

    client > 0 && client <= MaxClients
        && IsClientInGame(client)
        && !IsFakeClient(client)
        && GetClientTeam(client) == TeamRed

The !IsFakeClient is doing the excluding. It is right everywhere else it is
used, so do not touch it: unlocks.inc leans on it to keep class and slot
enforcement off the robots, and tf2_archipelago.sp:459 says so outright, "Both
events fire for robots too; MvM_IsPlayer is what leaves their loadout alone".
The payout needs its own predicate for a RED defender, human or bot, and
MvM_CanPayCredits should keep asking about humans, since it is asking whether
the moment is payable rather than who is owed.

## Why it matters more than the credits

A bundle is 200 credits (cashBundleCredits, gamedata/items.go). Filler-heavy
spheres hand out a lot of them, and the player watches their own balance climb
while the team that has to actually hold the bomb stays poor. That reads as the
bots being bad at upgrading, which is the complaint that keeps coming in, when
part of it is that they were never given the money.

## What to watch out for

The pack path is deliberate and the docblock on MvM_GrantCredits explains why:
writing m_nCurrency puts a number on the player the game's bookkeeping never
saw, and the refund button and a lost wave both restore that record, which is
where the negative balances came from. So bots get a pack at their feet like
anybody else, not a property write.

That means it has to be verified that a bot actually walks over it. It is
dropped at the client's own origin between waves, which should be a touch on the
spot, but a bot frozen in spawn is a known state on the mvm-bots side and a bot
that is not standing where the pack landed is not paid. Count what was paid,
do not assume it.

The other half is the defender mod's own accounting. It sets a bot's currency
wholesale on spawn:

    TF2_SetCurrency(data, GetStartingCurrency(g_iPopulationManager)
                          + GetAcquiredCreditsOfAllWaves())

Neither term knows about bundles, so a bot that is paid and then respawns loses
the money again. Fixing the payout without fixing that formula gets the money in
and drops it on the next respawn. Tracked from the other side as mvm-6dc, which
needs the same running total of bundles granted.

## Done when

A run with several bundles granted shows each bot's balance matching the human's
to the credit, across a wave loss, a refund, and a respawn.
close_reason: Duplicate of apw-4cb, which is further along and already rules out the pack route this bead assumed. The half it had that apw-4cb did not, bots being excluded from the payout by MvM_IsPlayer, is folded in as a comment there.

title: Join from the launcher fails where the LAN browser succeeds
description:
The Blabber: "just getting the 'connection failed after 4 retries.' message, and
it stalls with like 2 bars" / "it tries to make me join" / "the server IS up, i
do start joining it".

Peppy walked him to the workaround: check the LAN tab in the server browser.
It was listed there, and connecting through it worked first try.

So the server is up and reachable; it is the launcher's own connect that fails.
The retry message and the two-bar stall are the symptoms to reproduce against.
design:
## Cause, from the evidence rather than a repro

`SteamConnectURL` built the link from `LocalAddresses()[0]`, and that was
whatever `net.Interfaces` returned first. The order is arbitrary and a machine
with Docker, WSL or a virtual machine on it has several addresses that answer
nothing.

Cowser's bundle carries four for one server:

    192.168.50.105   192.168.34.1   192.168.222.1   172.25.192.1

Three of those are adapters with no server behind them. A join aimed at one is
"connection failed after 4 retries" and a stall at two bars, while the LAN tab
of the server browser finds the server first try because it looks on the
network rather than at a list. That is The Blabber's report line for line.

The old comment already admitted the choice was arbitrary: "the link uses the
first address the machine has".

## Fix

`preferredOutboundAddress` dials UDP at 192.0.2.1, the documentation range.
Nothing is sent and nothing routes there: the dial only makes the kernel choose
a route, and the local address of that choice is the interface this machine
really reaches the network on. `LocalAddresses` puts it first, so the join link
and the displayed list both lead with it.

## Not reproduced

The Blabber's machine is not available and the fault needs several adapters to
show. The evidence is his symptoms matching this mechanism exactly, plus a
second bundle showing the multi-adapter case is real and common. Worth asking
him to try a build past this before the bead is closed.

If it still fails for him, the next thing to rule out is the password: the link
carries `+password` only when `SrcdsPw` is set, and a server with one set after
the link was built would refuse a join that looks identical from outside.
close_reason: The cause was diagnosed and the fix shipped: launcher/internal/lanaddr asks the OS which address this machine would send from, by dialling UDP at 192.0.2.1 so the kernel picks a route, and puts that first in the list the join link and the displayed addresses both read. That is the mechanism the bead names, and it matches The Blabber's symptoms line for line. Closed rather than held open waiting for one player to try a build: the fix is in every release since, and a second report of a two-bar stall reopens it. If it does recur, the bead's own next step is the password, since the link carries +password only when SrcdsPw is set.

title: De-upgrading appears not to take
description:
From the play-test: buy an upgrade, sell it again before leaving the upgrade
station, and it stays bought. Reported as "not sure if it is the AP or MvM in
general", and that is still the open question.

Nothing in this plugin touches a purchase. `Unlocks_EnforceSlots` removes
weapons in slots the run has not opened and leaves every other slot alone, and
the upgrade command is only read, never blocked.

The hypothesis worth testing first is item 1 above. `MvM_GrantCredits` writes
`m_nCurrency` straight onto the player, so after a Cash Bundle the player's
credits and the number the game recorded for the wave disagree. A refund pays
back through the game's own accounting, and accounting that has been written
around from outside is exactly the kind that refuses a transaction while
showing it as accepted.

That gives a test that costs one evening: sell an upgrade on a run where no
Cash Bundle has landed yet, and sell one after a bundle has. If only the second
fails, this is item 1 and not a Valve bug, and fixing item 1 fixes both.

The plugin now writes every purchase and every sale to the SourceMod log,
players included, with the credits held afterwards. So a bundle from the
evening says whether the sale reached the game at all, which is the half nobody
could see: a sale the station accepted and the game ignored looks the same as
one that worked, from the chair.
design:
## Prior art, and it points where the probe already pointed

Source SDK 2013 carries the upgrade code officially. Read it, never copy it:
its licence requires derivatives stay free and ship Valve's LICENSE, and this
repo is MIT, so the two cannot be mixed.

Two files matter, and which one matters is the whole question here:

- `src/game/shared/tf/tf_upgrades_shared.cpp` holds the shared `MVM_Upgrade`
  handling, the same message the probe drives with
  `FakeClientCommandKeyValues`.
- `src/game/client/tf/player_vs_environment/c_tf_upgrades.cpp` is the **client**
  upgrade panel.

The probe ran ten conditions and every one came back `credits_back: true` and
`upgrade_removed: true`, so the server takes the sale and returns the money.
The conclusion recorded here was that the leading remaining explanation is a
stale station panel rather than a server bug. That is a client-side claim, and
`c_tf_upgrades.cpp` is where it can be settled: how the panel holds its own copy
of the upgrade state, and what makes it refresh.

Read it for that question specifically. If the panel keeps a local tally and
only refreshes on certain events, a player who sells and sees no change is
looking at a stale panel over a server that already did the work, and no amount
of server-side testing will ever reproduce it.

Note there is no `RefundUpgrade` symbol in the public SDK, so the server-side
refund path may not be there in full. The client panel is the part that is, and
it is the part this bead now needs.
notes:
Imported from TODO.md item 5 — section: Bugs, most impactful first
Original heading: De-upgrading appears not to take. Open, and it may be item 1
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:

The test it names costs one evening and no code: sell an upgrade on a run where

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Unblocked, and the testbed can answer this without a play session. A probe is in
tf2-mvm-bots as testbed/stats/mvmbots_refund.sp: it picks a live defender bot,
optionally writes credits onto m_nCurrency the way MvM_DropCredits pays a
bundle, buys an upgrade and sells it straight back, and prints spent, returned
and sale_took as one line.

A bot is a fair subject because the defender mod buys through
FakeClientCommandKeyValues("MVM_Upgrade") (upgrade.sp:1170), which is the same
command the upgrade station sends for a human.

Driving it turned up something that changes what this bead is asking, and it is
worth writing down before the run finishes.

Every credit a defender bot has is written the same way a Cash Bundle is. The
mod gives bots money with TF2_SetCurrency, and that stock is

    SetEntProp(client, Prop_Send, "m_nCurrency", nAmount)

which is byte for byte what MvM_DropCredits does. So a bot has never held a
credit the game's own record of the wave knew about, and bots buy upgrades
successfully all day: the mod checks that the credits actually moved
(upgrade.sp:1157) and that check passes in play.

That is evidence against the broad version of the hypothesis. Money written from
outside is spendable; the game does not refuse a purchase for it. What is left
to test is narrower and more interesting: whether a *sale* specifically consults
the wave record that the write bypassed, which is exactly the asymmetry apw-4cb
describes for the refund button.

It also means a bot cannot be the control leg. There is no game-recorded money
on a bot to compare against. The control needs either a human, or the test-bed
host, which joins normally and holds the starting 400 the game issued it.

Two practical notes for whoever picks this up. The host is a statue that never
walks to the upgrade station, and MvM validates that a buyer is standing in it,
which is the likely reason the host accepted no upgrade at 400 credits. And
BOT_USE_UPGRADES=0 keeps a bot's money unspent but also keeps it away from the
station, so it is not the shortcut it looks like.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Tested on the bed. The hypothesis does not survive, and the bead needs a
different question.

Two legs, same subject, same upgrade, same cost. The test-bed host holds money
the game issued it, and the probe writes a bundle on top the way MvM_DropCredits
does:

  {"bundle":0,  "started":400,"held":400,"spent":150,"after_sell":400,"returned":150,"sale_took":true}
  {"bundle":200,"started":400,"held":600,"spent":150,"after_sell":600,"returned":150,"sale_took":true}

The credits come back in full either way. Money written onto m_nCurrency from
outside is not what stops a sale, so this is not apw-4cb and the two should stop
being linked as cause and effect.

What this does NOT show, and it is the half the report is actually about.

"De-upgrading appears not to take" says the upgrade stays bought. The probe
measures credits and only credits. A sale that hands the money back and leaves
the attribute on the player would pass every assertion above and still be the
bug that was reported, and that combination is more consistent with the report
than a refused sale is: somebody who got no money back would have said the sale
did nothing, not that the upgrade stayed.

So the next measurement is the attribute, not the balance. Read the upgrade's
level on the player or the weapon before the buy, after the buy and after the
sale, and the answer is in the third number. tf2attributes is already staged on
the bed for it.

Method, for whoever picks it up. testbed/stats/mvmbots_refund.sp, run between
waves as `mvmbots_refund_probe <credits> [host|bot]`, results in
addons/sourcemod/logs/mvmbots_refund.jsonl. Use the host, not a bot: every
credit a bot holds was written with TF2_SetCurrency, which is the same
m_nCurrency write, so a bot has no game-issued money to serve as a control.

title: "Let the mod pick" picks classes that are unticked
description:
Peppy: "the bot seats I set as 'Let the mod pick' still picks from classes that
I have unchecked in the Classes tab."

Two faults, both in the launcher, both about what a draw seat is worth.

A seat is a place in `sm_redbots_manager_team_composition`, counted from one,
and the mod reads a seat it cannot parse as a seat it should leave to the
lineup mode. Both settings pages stored the classes somebody named and dropped
the draws, so naming seat 4 and leaving the first three to the mod stored one
class, and the mod filled it as seat 1. The loadout file numbers seats from the
same list, so the Wrangler went to whichever engineer came first rather than to
the seat that asked for it.

And a team of nothing but draws stored nothing, which is an empty convar, and
an empty convar is what makes the mod fall back to the map's own default
lineup. It then treats that default as a team somebody named, and a named team
beats the blacklist: `IsBotClassBlacklisted` returns false for any class the
composition mentions. So the map's guess played the classes the Classes tab had
unticked, which is exactly the report.

Fixed. A draw seat is an empty entry rather than a missing one, end to end: the
window, the console form, `SRCDS_BOT_TEAM_COMP` and `SRCDS_BOT_SEAT_LOADOUTS`
through `SplitSeats`, and `Composition`, which writes `engineer,,heavyweapons`
and keeps seat 3 on 3. Trailing draws name no seat and are still dropped. When
every seat is a draw and some class is unticked, the seats go out as holes
anyway, so the string is not empty and the map's guess never gets to overrule
the ticks.

Tested where the bug was: `botloadout` for the convar and for the loadout
file's seat numbers agreeing with it, `settings` for the environment
round-trip, `tui` for a seat keeping its number when the seat before it goes
back on the draw, and `gui` for what the Bots tab means, which is now a plain
value the Win32 widgets are read into so it can be tested off Windows.

What is still open is the mod's own rule, and it belongs there: a lineup the
map guessed at should not beat a blacklist somebody set. tf2-mvm-bots item 7.

title: RED gets nine bots when the mission loads
description:
Peppy: "the server is putting 9 bots on red team sometimes, it happens when the
mission is loaded but once the wave is restarted it fixes itself."

One ask adds more than it asked for, and it is the mod that does the adding.
`sm_addbots N` runs `AddBotsBasedOnLineupMode(N)`, which calls
`AddBotsFromTeamComposition(N)` first: that adds the seats the named team still
wants and reports success only when it filled all N. A team that does not name
every seat cannot, so the caller falls through to the lineup mode and adds N
more on top. Three named seats and an ask for six is three plus six.

Which is nine, and it is nine at mission load rather than mid-mission because
that is the one moment RED is empty and the whole six are asked for at once.

Why the wave restart cleared it: the only trim this plugin ran was scheduled
three seconds after `mvm_begin_wave`, so between the map loading and the first
wave nothing counted the team at all.

Fixed here, which is the half this repository owns. `Bots_Fill` runs
`Bots_TrimSurplus` on its own poll now, so RED comes back to its size within
three seconds wherever the surplus came from, and the debug log says who left.

The other half is the mod's and it is the actual bug:
`AddBotsBasedOnLineupMode` has to subtract what the composition already added
before it falls back. It is filed as tf2-mvm-bots item 18, with the test-bed
repro, because a fix there is worth more than a trim here: a bot that is added
and kicked three seconds later still spent a seat and still cost the wave its
upgrade time.
design:
## Half of this is fixed, and by two different beads

**The symptom, by apw-49k.** The trim only ever ran three seconds after
`mvm_begin_wave`, which is why nine bots survived from map load until a wave
restart. `Timer_TrimBots` is now armed after `sm_addbots` as well, so a surplus
at map load is counted back within `BotTrimDelay` instead of waiting for a wave.
RED still reaches nine for a moment; it no longer stays there.

**The cause, by apw-ygn, but only with a blacklist.** This bead's own reading is
that `AddBotsFromTeamComposition(N)` reports success only when it filled all N,
and a team that does not name every seat cannot, so the caller falls through to
the lineup mode and adds N more. apw-ygn made `Composition` pad the lineup out
to the full team whenever the blacklist is non-empty, so in that case every seat
is named, N can be filled, and the fall-through never happens.

With no blacklist a short lineup is still left short on purpose, so
`["scout"]` against a six-man team still names one seat and the fall-through
still fires. That is the remaining half.

## What is left

Decide whether a short lineup should always be padded, or only when a blacklist
makes it necessary.

Padding always looks harmless — an empty seat means "the mod draws this one",
which is what an unnamed seat meant anyway — and it would close the
fall-through for good. But it changes what the convar says in the no-blacklist
case, and `Composition` documents an empty string as "the mod plays the map's
own default lineup". Whether six empty seats and no string are the same thing to
the mod is not established here, and guessing at it is how the padding got
written narrowly in the first place.

The testbed answers it: set a one-class lineup with no blacklist, count RED at
map load, then again with the padding widened.
