title: The server can bind a port the launcher never mentions again
description:
Mage Delta, 2026-09-09, on the released launcher:

| Anyone knows why it doesn't let me join my own server for the ap when it says
| it's running?
| I was using my IPv4 address but I didn't port forward on my machine (Yet it
| used to work without doing it till today)
| Wait a min, It says in the log that the port 27015 is unavaliable
| Is it meant to say that?

Their screenshot is srcds saying it:

| WARNING: Port 27015 was unavailable - bound to port 27016 instead
| WARNING: Port 27005 was unavailable - bound to port 27006 instead
| WARNING: Port 27020 was unavailable - bound to port 27021 instead

So the server came up on 27016 and everything the launcher says still names
27015: the join line, the connect lines it prints at start, the Join button and
SrcdsPort itself. The player is given an address nothing is listening on and a
running server, which is the shape of the report.

Answering their question: yes it is meant to say that, and no it is not meant to
be the launcher's last word on it. srcds takes the next free port rather than
refusing to start, which is reasonable of srcds and useless to anybody reading
the launcher.

The launcher reads four things out of the server's output already, in
runtime/connect.go: FakeIPAddress, LoadedMission, SourceModWasUpdated and
ItemServerLine. This warning is a fifth and nothing reads it.

Something else on the machine held 27015, which on this evidence is most likely
a game server the launcher itself left running: 27005 and 27020 were taken too,
and those three together are one srcds, not three unrelated programs. Worth
checking whether Stop leaves one behind before adding anything.

Work: read the line, say it where the player is looking, and put the port the
server actually bound into the join line rather than the one that was asked for.
Refusing to start would be worse: a second server on 27016 is a working server.

title: The mission table's column headers look sortable and are not
description:
EZKSupernova, 2026-09-08:

| Can the next update make it so the column headers in the Missions tab
| (Missions, Maps, Difficulty etc) actually work to sort the missions
| alphabetically? Right now, they look like you can click on them and then
| nothing happens, which makes filtering through specific missions a nightmare.

They are right about the cause and about the shape of it. declarative.TableView
draws a native list-view header, which is clickable-looking whether or not
anything is behind it, and poolModel implements walk.TableModel and not
walk.SorterModel. So the click lands, walk has nowhere to send it, and the
header draws its pressed state and nothing else.

Eighty-five missions in the table now that the Valve-map community ones are in,
which is what turned a header nobody pressed into one everybody does.

Work: implement Sorter on poolModel, sort the rows and the ticks together since
they are two parallel slices, and keep the ticks written back under the IDs form
gave the rows rather than by position.

The columns they name are not the ones the table has. It draws Mission, In the
pool and Compatibility, so worth asking what they were looking at, or splitting
the map out of the mission label while this is open anyway.
notes:
Done. poolModel implements walk.Sorter.

- The rows and their ticks were two parallel slices and are one slice of
  poolRow now, so a sort cannot move a tick onto another mission. A test asserts
  that after sorting every tick is still on the ID form declared it for.
- Column 0 sorts on the mission name, not the label, which opens with the
  archive: sorting on the label groups by archive and finding one mission by
  name is what was asked for.
- Sort(-1) reorders nothing. A TableView with a sorting model re-sorts on every
  row it is told changed and passes its own column, which is -1 before a header
  is pressed, so without the guard the first tick rearranged the table.

One thing decided rather than discovered: the table now opens sorted by mission
name. walk asks a Sorter model to sort by its default column as soon as it has
one and the sorted column lives unexported on the view, so it cannot both sort
on click and open in the declared order. Alphabetical is the better of the two
for eighty-five rows and is what the request was about.

Their column names, Missions/Maps/Difficulty, are still not the ones the table
draws. Left open as a question for them.

title: The mission table does not repaint a row until the mouse crosses it
description:
Peppy, relayed by the maintainer, 2026-09-08: a table needs the mouse passed
over it before the lines update.

poolModel.SetChecked writes p.inPool[row] and returns, and never publishes:

    p.inPool[row] = checked
    return nil

poolmodel_windows.go. The "In the pool" column is Value(row, 1), which reads
p.inPool[row] and answers Hint or HintOff. Nothing tells the table view the row
changed, so the text keeps saying what it said until Windows repaints the row
for its own reasons, which is what passing the mouse over it does.

setAll is the tell: it calls PublishRowsReset, so All in the pool and None in
the pool update at once, and one tick does not.

The worse half is a mission the launcher cannot play. SetChecked returns without
writing when the row is Disabled, so the model refuses the tick and the control
keeps drawing the tick the player just clicked. It reads as accepted and is not.
TestAnUnplayableMissionRefusesTheTick asks the model and passes; nothing asks
what is on screen.

Work: PublishRowChanged(row) on both paths of SetChecked, and a test that a
refused tick leaves the row reading as out of the pool.
notes:
Reported by the maintainer, not by Peppy: "you need to pass the mouse on them for
it to actually update the lines". The cause below was found from that.
Fixed. SetChecked publishes on both paths, so the In the pool column redraws
with the tick and a refused tick redraws as out of the pool instead of keeping
the tick the player clicked.

TestARefusedTickLeavesTheRowReadingAsOutOfThePool asks what the column would
draw, which is the part the old test did not.

title: Check Run Selection reports a refused selection as valid
description:
From [-SAM-]'s screenshot, 2026-09-08. The box says:

| Selection is valid: 0 eligible mission(s) provide 0 checks for 0 unlocks.

CheckSelection did not say that. It returned an error, "no missions remain in
the normal-or-harder pool", and the window threw it away:

    result, _ := settings.CheckRunSelection(next)
    walk.MsgBox(owner, "Archipelago run selection", result.Summary(), ...)

settings_windows.go:451. On an error CheckRunSelection returns a zero Preflight,
and Preflight.Summary opens with "Selection is valid:" unconditionally, so the
zero value reads as a pass with nothing in it.

Two ends, and both are worth closing:

- The caller has to report the error. It is the one thing that button exists to
  find out.
- Summary should not be able to say a selection is valid. It is only ever called
  on a report that came back with no error today, which is exactly the sort of
  invariant that stops being true in one line.

Separate from the pool being empty in the first place, which is its own bead.
notes:
Fixed at both ends. checkRunSelection reports the error instead of dropping it,
and Preflight.Summary refuses to call a report of no missions valid, so a caller
that drops an error again cannot print a pass.

title: Saving a run-shape setting restarts the server for nothing
description:
Likai, 2026-09-07:

| In general fudging with settings often restarts the server
| That probably is too aggressive - might take time to hit the UX now that
| weve done an initial pass on most of the in game stuff

Separate from apw-ylq, which is SourceMod's restart landing while the window is
open. This is the restart the save itself does, and the policy behind it.

editSettingsOn (gui_windows.go) restarts unless botlive.LiveOnly says the bot
team is the only thing that moved. LiveOnly is written as a comparison of
everything else, which is the safe way round and was the right call, but nothing
has been added to it since, so every other setting restarts.

Most of them have to: the server reads server.cfg and its command line once at
startup. The run shape does not. MvmGoal, MvmMissionCount, MvmExcludedMissions,
MvmDifficulty, MvmStartMission, MvmStartClass and MvmDeathLink go into tf2.yaml
and from there into the seed. Nothing in internal/srcdsconfig reads an Mvm
field. The one place they reach a running server is StartTestRoom
(supervisor.go:365), which builds the fake room at start, so in Test mode the
restart is real.

So: outside Test mode, saving a Player options, Rewards or Missions change ends
the mission the team is playing and changes nothing about the server it comes
back as. The run keeps the shape it was generated with either way.

Work: say which settings a running server actually reads, the way LiveOnly says
which the bot mod re-reads, and restart only for those. Test mode keeps the
restart for the run shape because its room is built at start. Whatever the
answer, the log line has to say what the restart is for.
notes:
Done. internal/saveplan answers what a save asks of a running server, as two
independent facts: Team, whether the bot team moved, and Restart, whether
anything read once at startup did. Quiet is neither.

- readAtStart is a subtraction, the same shape botlive uses for the team, so a
  setting added later needs a restart until somebody says otherwise. All 18 Mvm
  fields are taken out; Test mode keeps them, because StartTestRoom builds its
  room out of the run shape at start.
- botlive.LiveOnly is gone: it answered one case of the same question, and
  asking it twice in two packages is how the two drift apart. Its test moved to
  saveplan and grew the run-shape cases.
- The window has a Restart on save tick beside Save, shown only when what is on
  screen now would need one, and never with the server down. Off is the only way
  to get a save that does not restart; a tick nobody was shown reads as yes,
  which is what the launcher always did.
- Visibility is tracked on the dialog, not asked of the control: Win32 calls a
  child of an unshown window invisible, and what Save does cannot depend on
  whether anybody has looked at the window.
- The terminal has no tick, so a restart it needs is a restart it does.

Tested under Wine, not on a real Windows server.

title: Community missions on Valve maps are not in the catalogue
description:
Glitch, 2026-09-07:

| Is it possible to load custom missions on Valve maps, such as Moonlight's
| Trouble in Mann Town (Coaltown) and Manntenance (Mannworks)? Can't seem to
| find them in the list of missions but they are in the downloaded community
| assets

Likai answered that they ignored most of the modded maps and that a mission on

| They're custom missions that happen to be on official base game maps so I
| believe the standard bot nav should work fine on those missions

never asks what the map is. A mission entry naming map_id 2 for mvm_coaltown
loads today.

That is the whole fix on this side: rows in community.json with the Valve map id
and pack mlarchive-assets.zip. The mission needs the pack for its popfile and
nothing else, because the map and its navigation mesh ship with the game, so
these are the one group of community missions with no requires at all.

Work: name the Moonlight missions that run on Valve maps, read their waves,
tank and giant off the popfiles the way the rest were read, and add them.
notes:
Done. 30 missions added to gamedata/community.json, ids 160-189, including the two
Glitch named: Trouble in Mann Town on Coaltown and Manntenance on Mannworks.

- Read out of the two archives on disk by inspectPopulation, the same function
  communitycheck validates the existing 55 with, so the waves, the tank and the
  giant are the popfiles' own answers and not a transcription. The difficulty
  and the name come from the popfile name, the way the rest did.
- Reverse missions are not among them. mvm_bigrock_rev_adv_numerator and its
  kind name a mode this does not support, and they fall out of the match on
  their own rather than by a list.
- ValidateCommunitySources asked every playable community mission's map for a
  .nav out of the archive. A Valve map has no reason to be in one: the .bsp and
  the .nav ship with the game, which is Glitch's point and why these need the
  pack for the population file and nothing else. Now asked of community maps
  only.
- safeConsoleName took letters, digits and underscores, so it refused
  mvm_mannworks_int_xlr-8, a real popfile. A hyphen is no more a command
  separator than the underscore beside it, and leaving it out was not a safety
  property but a mission nobody could offer.
- The two ledgers that record what is in the catalogue moved with it, and the
  export was regenerated.

The pool with every mission kept goes from 82 to 112 at the normal floor.
communitycheck agrees with both archives. make check is green.

Not play-tested: no run has drawn one of these yet.

title: Generate seed refuses over the room address, and the box names no field
description:
Roseburst's screenshot, Discord 2026-09-07, on v1.11.0. Player options is filled
in, Archipelago app points at C:\ProgramData\Archipelago, and a second screenshot
of that folder shows ArchipelagoGenerate.exe sitting in it. Pressing Generate seed
gives a message box titled "Generate seed" saying, in full:

| the address is empty

That string is settings.ParseRoom (settings/room.go:30). It is about the
Archipelago room, which generateSeed never uses: generation runs the app over the
player file, and the success box then tells the player to upload the archive and
paste the room address afterwards. The room cannot exist yet at the moment the
button is pressed.

It got there through collect. generateSeed calls it for the settings
(settings_windows.go:414), collect runs form.Apply over every field
(settings_windows.go:147), and on that build the room field's setter returned the
parse error, so one empty field two tabs away refused the whole read.

Probably already fixed on nightly, as a side effect rather than on purpose:
roomAddress's setter now swallows the parse error (form/specs_run.go:404) and the
Save path notes an unparseable room instead of refusing it (98a4510). Nobody has
pressed Generate seed on nightly with an empty room to confirm it, and that is the
first thing to do here.

Two things are wrong either way:

- generateSeed shows a bare err.Error() in a box titled after the button. Whatever
  collect refuses on, the player gets a sentence with no field in it. The Save
  path learned to switch to the page holding the reason before saying it
  (8e7eaaf); this path did not.
- ParseRoom's messages are written for a field label beside them. "the address is
  empty" has to name the address once it can be read anywhere else.

title: The mission count ceiling counts missions the generator will not draw
description:
[-SAM-], 2026-09-07:

| I set it to 82 including all community missions
| also is 29 the limit of how many missions you can have or is that just all
| that can be displayed on the session tab?
| In the room it says there's only 265 checks so it's probably the latter

The launcher let them ask for 82 and the run holds 29. Nothing said why.

The two sides count different pools. The launcher's ceiling is
runshape.MissionsInPool, which walks gamedata.PlayableMissions and counts every
mission at or above the chosen difficulty floor. The generator's pool is
_available_missions in apworld/tf2_mvm/__init__.py, which drops any mission
failing mission.seedable_with(mods): a community mission whose pack is not in
server_mods is not drawable. Then generate_early does
min(mission_count, len(available)) and says nothing to the player about the
difference.

So a player who ticks the community missions but leaves their packs out of the
server mods gets a silently smaller run, and the number the launcher offered them
was never reachable.

The ceiling has to be counted the way the generator counts: the difficulty floor
and the enabled mods together. Second, a run that draws fewer missions than asked
should say so on the screen that asked, not only in the generator's log.
notes:
Roseburst's settings screenshot, same afternoon, shows the ceiling side directly:
the Easiest tier row reads "intermediate  draws from 78 missions". So the number
the launcher puts in front of a player already counts the community missions,
before anything asks whether their packs are in server_mods. 78 offered, and
[-SAM-]'s run drew 29.
Fixed on main by 3dfbc80. runshape.Pool counts the difficulty floor, the exclusion
list, the community toggle and server_mods together, and the tier labels, the
ceiling and the preflight all read it. With a fresh settings file the tiers now
read 29/25/17/4 where they read 82/78/52/12, and 29 is what [-SAM-]'s run drew.
generate_early warns when the pool is smaller than the ask.

Not in a release: it waits on apw-grt.

title: The debug bundle ships crash dumps from unrelated programs
description:
A bundle sent in for apw-ep5 carried three crash dumps under crashes/, none of them the game server:

  crashes/stellaris.exe.37788-tail.dmp
  crashes/Hearthstone.exe.40640-tail.dmp
  crashes/ShiftAtMidnight.exe.5048-tail.dmp

A player sends this file to whoever is helping them. A memory dump of somebody's Hearthstone is not ours to pass on, and the summary tells the reader those files are the ones worth reading first.

newestCrashDumps already knows this is wrong. It filters the Windows Error Reporting directory with isGameServerDump, which wants a name starting with srcds, hl2 or tf2ap, and the comment above it says two earlier bundles carried GameBar, Refunct and THPS12 dumps for the same reason.

The filter is on one of the two paths. The directories built from the game folder are collected with isCrashDump, which takes any .dmp or .mdmp, and the bases include filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(gameDir)) plus a crashdumps and CrashDumps folder under each. Work out which of those matched here and apply the same filter to all of them, or invert it: name what is wanted rather than exclude what is not.

Worth checking at the same time whether the -tail truncation leaves enough of a dump to read. If it does not, the bundle is carrying somebody's memory for nothing.

title: Feature: a web UI, and make it the launcher's default face
description:
The window and the terminal are both hand-driven native toolkits, and the settings are the launcher's whole job. apw-ep5 is a player who could not save a setting and could not find where the launcher put it: neither interface could tell them, and neither can be looked at by anybody helping them.

The port to internal/form was done for this. A Spec is declared once, Build resolves the specs and the state into a Model of plain data with no closures and no styling, and it encodes as JSON. Change goes back the same way. So the web mode is a renderer over an existing seam, not a fourth list of rows:

  GET  /api/settings -> form.Model as JSON
  POST /api/settings/change {field, value} -> form.Apply, then the new Model
  POST /api/settings/action {id} -> the dispatcher, same IDs both interfaces use

Default face: opening tf2ap.exe serves on loopback and opens the default browser. The window stays for a machine with no browser, and -configure keeps the terminal.

Reuse ~/projects/kado/frontend rather than starting one: Angular 22, its eslint config, and its design system. Port the eslint rules across as they are, so the standalone-and-signals, no-effect, signal-forms and path-alias rules hold here from the first commit rather than being argued again.

Two things to decide before any code:
- Loopback only, or reachable from another machine. It changes nothing about form, and it decides whether SrcdsRconPw, SrcdsPw, APPassword and SrcdsToken cross a network and whether a Change needs auth and CSRF.
- Whether the Go side serves the built assets from an embed, which is what makes it one .exe with no install step.
notes:
Likai is building it, 2026-09-08:

| im doing an experiment with a web UI for the thing instead of the local one
| hoping to condense the code there a lot since it's kinda spaghetti
| gives us linux ui for free basically if i do it this way

Their screenshot is the main window, working: the status line reading "running
test mode Doe's Doom", Stop, Restart, Join, Settings and Quit, the join line
with the Steam public IP and the local addresses and a Copy button, the Session,
Unlocks, Bots and Log tabs, and the rcon box. Dark, and laid out like the window
rather than like a new thing.

The linux point is this bead's own argument made by somebody else: apw-035 is
the Linux screen being unreadable next to the server's output, and a browser
answers it without a fourth toolkit.

Settings is a button in the shot, so the form.Model half is still ahead.

title: Replace the source-scraping plugin tests with spshell drivers
description:
gamedata/plugin_weapon_buffs_test.go and gamedata/weapon_buffs_test.go check the plugin by looking for substrings in its source. Measured on the cooldown floor: inverting the comparison so every cooldown collapses to the minimum, a real gameplay bug, leaves every watched string in place and the scraping test passes. The driver catches it and names the wrong numbers. The reverse holds too: renaming a local breaks a scraping test without changing behaviour.

weapon_buffs_math.inc exists now and four functions are run rather than read: the destruction cooldown curve, the passive effect set, the on-kill effect set, and the definition-to-weapon lookup over every row of the generated table. The paste-by-brace-counting helper that the first drivers needed is deleted; a driver includes the file the plugin includes.

What is left needs the engine, and the file's own rule is what says so: no native, no constant out of a SourceMod include. Checked and refused:

- WeaponBuffs_IsDamageOverTime is pure arithmetic and still does not qualify: TF_CUSTOM_BLEEDING comes from tf2_stocks. It was moved in and moved back out.
- WeaponBuffs_ThermalThrusterEffectiveCost and WeaponBuffs_EnergyMaxCharge need RoundToFloor, which the standalone VM does not bind.
- WeaponBuffs_IsSyringeGun and the classname predicates need StrEqual and StrContains, same reason.
- WeaponBuffs_DistanceToShot needs SquareRoot through GetVectorDistance. The projection either side of it is pure and could be split from the distance.
- WeaponBuffs_ClassBaseHealth is a switch over TF2_GetPlayerClass. The mapping is worth running and the lookup is not: splitting the table off from the call would do it.

So the next ones need a change to the plugin before they need a test. Take them one at a time; each is a function that stops needing something rather than a test that gets cleverer.

Keep the key-literal tests in pluginkeys_test.go: those check that the plugin's string constants match gamedata's, which is a text question and correctly answered by reading text.

title: Port the six remaining settings pages into internal/form
description:
Player options, Missions, Archipelago room, Game server, Bots and Networking still carry a hand-written row list in both the window and the terminal, and the help text drifts between them unwatched.

Each page moves the same way Rewards did: a Spec per row in form, the terminal calls modelFields(page), the window calls modelPage.widgets(page), and both delete their literals.

Three need design first, they are not plain rows:
- Missions has a row per mission, an All/None pair and the community asset pack flow.
- Bots has the seat and loadout builder, which writes through settings.WithBotTeam rather than by field.
- Player options and Missions have Text rows with a Browse button beside them, so form needs a Text row that can carry an action.

The form.text constructor was deleted when the last Text row left it unused. It comes back with the first one ported.

uiparity goes when this is done: form.WrittenFields will cover everything and its two lists will be empty.
close_reason: Done, all nine pages. form.Specs is a function of the state because Missions has a row per mission and Loadouts a row per slot; form.State carries the draft the Bots page edits, which is not a setting. TestEverySettingIsOnAPageOrSaysWhyNot walks settings.Settings and refuses a field no row writes.

title: weapon_buffs_math.inc: the pure arithmetic, includable on its own
description:
The spshell drivers in gamedata/spdriver_test.go paste a function's text out of weapon_buffs.inc by name, because that file opens with sourcemod, sdkhooks, tf2 and ripext and cannot be compiled alone.

Pasting works and the tests run, but it means a driver can only take a function whose whole body is self-contained. The cooldown curve and the passive-effect predicate qualify. WeaponBuffs_EffectIncrement nearly does and would be a true differential test against gamedata, which owns the increments and the syringe-gun exception.

Split the arithmetic that touches no engine call into weapon_buffs_math.inc, including nothing. The plugin includes it and so does a driver, and the paste goes.
close_reason: Done. plugin/scripting/tf2_archipelago/weapon_buffs_math.inc holds the decisions that need nothing but their arguments and the generated tables, includes nothing itself, and is included by both the plugin and the drivers. The paste-by-brace-counting helper is deleted; the linter found it unreachable. Plugin byte counts are identical before and after. What the file will not take, and why, is on apw-6l9.

title: The Linux launcher screen is unreadable next to the server's own output
description:
CowsertheKhelinace, GitHub #33:

| Linux could use a GUI like the Windows version currently does. The terminal
| is prone to being bumped or overwritten by other messages, leading to messy
| screens that require you to change screens often to be able to read or use
| it.
|
| Additionally, the Unlocks tab does not show every unlock if a lot are
| currently unlocked. [...] there are more items below the final line, but no
| way to scroll to them.

Two reports, and they part.

The scrolling one is already fixed on main and not in anybody's hands: f4634f8
scrolls every tab that lists more than fits, and it landed after v1.11.0 and
after the nightly tag, so his build cannot have it. Nothing to do here but
release it.

The unreadable screen is open. Linux does run the same bubbletea TUI as
Windows, on the alt screen, so this is not a missing GUI: something else writes
to the same terminal and tears it. His screenshots are the shape of srcds or a
child process printing to the launcher's stdout rather than into the log pane.
The cause is not in the report, so this stays a report until somebody reproduces
it and names the writer.
close_reason: Fixed by apw-srw: the terminal interface that drew over the server's output is deleted. Linux gets the same browser screen Windows does, and -console prints the log and nothing over it for a machine with no desktop.

title: Weapon buffs bugged in the plugin, from Cowser's sheet
description:
CowsertheKhelinace, GitHub #32, names these as bugged rather than ineligible.
Each is a plugin change in weapon_buffs.inc, not an eligibility rule, so they
are here rather than on apw-4ck.

What is left:

• Afterburn duration does nothing. Ignite on hit does not feed it either: only
weapons that give afterburn natively do. Either fix it or take it off
flamethrowers at least.
• Crits while airborne and mini-crit jumpers only fire while blast jumping,
whether the player launched himself or a robot did it. Cowser calls that funny
rather than wrong, so read it before changing it.
• Explosive headshot only triggers on a Sniper Rifle headshot. It should fire
on the Huntsman and the Ambassador too. He also warns it would be as strong as
explode on ignite once fixed, which is the buff that was cut for ending waves
on its own.
• Projectile count on the Huntsman spawns the extra arrows and shows them, but
only one of them hits anything. Same shape as apw-30v; re-read after its Linux
play-test.
• Speed boost on hit natively: a heavy bot with it on the Minigun landed a
thousand hits and never got the condition, while heal on hit on the same gun
did. Not in Cowser's list. Read once by the plugin's own probe; needs a human
to confirm before it becomes a bug.

Landed on main, each with its measurement in a comment here: heal on hit and
speed boost on hit on the jars, the on-kill buffs of a weapon that is not in
hand, the Gas Passer's kills through afterburn, and destroy projectiles, which
kelly-cs fixed for the hitscan and non-explosive energy guns in #38 and left
off every projectile weapon.
acceptance_criteria: Each is either fixed and seen working on a server, or written down as refused with the reason.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
CowsertheKhelinace, GitHub #32, after a pass on the current build:

| Doing some testing, unless certain combinations of buffs conflict with it,
| Heal on Hit (effect 22) and Speed on Hit (effect 80) do NOT work with Jar
| weapons (Jarate, Mad Milk).
|
| the effects on Kill (Health 7, Crits 8, Speed 23, Mini-Crits 71) are very
| inconsistent with the Gas Passer. If the Gas Passer is still considered
| "active" when the robot dies, it will grant the effects, but if the robot
| dies after the Pyro swaps to another weapon, it does not grant the effect.
|
| Huntsman now shows multiple projectiles, but only one is currently
| functional.

Reading, none of it measured here yet.

The jar pair is a hole in the reading that opened them. Note 9 says a direct
hit with a jar counts as a hit, and ignite on hit does fire on one, so the
plugin does see the hit. Heal on hit and speed boost on hit read something else
about it and come out empty. Until somebody reads which event each of the three
hangs off, this stays a report rather than a fix.

The Gas Passer is the afterburn credit question, not an eligibility one. The
kill lands on the weapon held at the time of death, so a robot that burns down
after a swap credits whatever the Pyro is carrying. Cowser suggests marking the
robot as ignited by the Gas Passer and crediting that, which is a flag on the
victim rather than a lookup on the killer.

The Huntsman moved rather than closed: the arrows now spawn, and one of them
hits. Extras that spawn and never collide is the same shape as apw-30v, where
the native arrow the fanout creates never had its launcher set through the
native path, so the collide-with-teammates state was never reset. Worth
re-reading once that lands rather than chasing separately.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Measured on the native tree at ~/tf2-native with the bots carrying the buffs, decoy waves 1 to 4, sm_ap_projectile_debug on:
- crit-on-kill natively lasts 3 s for an attribute value of 2 (four samples 2.93-2.98 at the first 0.1 s poll), so the plugin adds one second to the value when it pays crits itself.
- speed_boost_on_kill natively lasts 1 s. The plugin uses 1 s for its speed on kill and speed on hit.
- heal on kill natively caps at max health (popup 0 at 449/450), so the plugin's heal caps the same way.
- mini-crit on kill never fired natively while crit on kill was on the same weapon; through the plugin it lasts the attribute's 3 s.
The measurement plugin was a throwaway; the only things kept are the defender-bot convar and the slot argument on sm_ap_buff_give, which is what note 49 asked for.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Über on hit, which this bead never listed but the same reply covers, was measured out of the server binary rather than in play, because a defender-bot Medic only ever holds his medigun and never fires his syringe gun.

CTFWeaponBase::ApplyOnHitAttributes at 0xdf61b0 reads add_onhit_ubercharge (0xdf6b49) and add_onhit_addhealth (0xdf62fe) in the same function, on the weapon that landed the hit, with no weapon-class branch between them. add_onhit_addhealth is what the Blutsauger carries natively, so that function demonstrably runs for a syringe gun. The uber read is gated on CTFPlayer::Weapon_OwnsThisID(0x32), TF_WEAPON_MEDIGUN, and then calls CWeaponMedigun::AddCharge. So the buff works on any weapon whose owner carries a medigun and does nothing for the other eight classes, which is why the pool is Medic-only.

Also measured on the native server with tf2ap_buffs_for_defender_bots 1: a Scout bot given movement speed and jump height on his bat, holding his scattergun, read mult_player_movespeed 1.0499 and mod_jump_height_from_weapon 1.1499 on the player, with m_flMaxspeed 419.9 against a 400 base. The passives reach him off a weapon he is not holding.

title: Tabs that list more than fits cut the rest in silence
description: Unlocks and the Bot Switcher build their rows and then cut them at the body height, so a run past a screenful of unlocks showed the first screenful and nothing said there was more. The keys were already bound; nothing read them.
acceptance_criteria: A list longer than the body scrolls and names the rows off both ends.
close_reason: window in launcher/internal/tui/view.go cuts at the offset and spends the last line on the count; Unlocks and the Bot Switcher both go through it. Covered by TestALongListScrollsAndSaysSo and TestTheSwitcherScrollsWhenTheTeamIsLong.

title: Remove the buffs a weapon cannot use
description:
kelly-cs, GitHub #20, enhancement:

| Lots of redundant buffs exist that have no effect on certain weapons. We
| need to clean these up more so you get less useless upgrades.

The same spreadsheet the sibling bead carries. This is the ask, that one is
the data: a buff offered on a weapon that cannot use it is a check the player
opens for nothing, and the pool is finite.

The sweep was held until the eligibility questions on apw-4ck were answered,
because half of them were "this is bugged" rather than "this weapon cannot use
it", and deleting a buff that only needs fixing is the wrong cure. Cowser
answered all four on 2026-09-07 and they are shipped, so the hold is off.

What is missing is the sweep itself: walk the sheet against
gamedata/weapon_eligibility.go, weapon by weapon, and say for each pair still
in the pool whether the game can act on it. Each refusal is a case plus a test.
The pairs already gone are in weapon_cuts.go, which is the sheet's N cells.
notes: Cowser again on 2026-09-10 with a screenshot, and GitHub #47: "Not all useless buffs were culled ... Check all reskins to make sure they were all properly called." The reskins are the named half: a buff culled for a weapon has to be culled for its 15xxx and 30xxx twins too, and the sheet does not list them separately.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text: The three decisions this waits on (meter weapons and clip or ammo, banner and medigun buffs landing on another slot, speed, jump and regen as passives) were put to the players on GitHub #32 on 2026-09-07, in one comment, with Cowser's 1% and 5% for Uber on hit as a fourth. Nothing moves here until somebody answers.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text: The three decisions this waited on were answered on GitHub #32 on 2026-09-07 and are implemented on main: meter weapons take neither clip size nor ammo capacity, a buff that only one item can use stays out of the other slots' pools, and movement speed, jump height and health regeneration are passive. Über on hit came back at Cowser's 1% and 5%. Nothing here is blocked on a decision any more.

title: Buff eligibility follows Cowser's sheet, buff by buff
description:
CowsertheKhelinace, GitHub #32:

A buff by buff pass over which weapons should be offered which buff, from his
Weapon Buffs Eligibility Sheet, written as thirty odd numbered notes. The
substance, kept here because a spreadsheet is not a source anybody can diff:

Straightforward: damage boost on any damaging weapon except Mantreads and
Thermal Thruster, which read fall damage; firing speed on anything that swings
or fires, jumpers included; reload speed on anything with a reload animation;
projectile speed on anything that becomes an object in the world and never on
hitscan; health on kill, crits on kill and speed on kill on anything that can
get one, Gas Passer included through afterburn; heal on hit, bleed on hit, milk
on hit and mark for death on anything that lands a hit, throwables included,
since a direct hit with a jar counts.

What is left is the diff itself: nobody has walked the sheet line by line
against gamedata/weapon_eligibility.go to say which of those rules the code
already keeps and which it does not. That walk is the sweep apw-aof asks for,
and it is no longer blocked, because the four decisions this bead was holding
are answered and shipped.

The maintainer decisions, answered by Cowser on 2026-09-07 and implemented:
a recharging weapon takes neither clip size nor ammo capacity; a buff only one
item can use stays out of the other slots' pools; movement speed, jump height
and health regeneration are passive, the way MvM's own class upgrades are;
Uber on hit comes back at one percent on syringe guns and five elsewhere.

Named as bugged rather than ineligible, and tracked on apw-jpm: afterburn
duration; crits while airborne and mini-crit jumpers, which only fire while
blast jumping; explosive headshot, which only triggers on sniper rifle
headshots and should work on the Huntsman and the Ambassador. Destroy
projectiles was on that list and kelly-cs fixed it in #38. Explode on ignite is
gone from the pool and he would keep it for the Gas Passer alone.
notes:
## Knockback on a jar was mine, not his (2026-09-06)

Caught on a reread. Note 21 argues knockback should stay allowed in general and says nothing about a thrown jar throwing anybody, so it is out of the jar set. Ignite and heal on hit stay: notes 10 and 22 point back at note 9, which is the one that says a direct hit with a jar counts as a hit.

Eight permutations became eligible, not ten.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Peppy, on Discord:

| I'd like to add here that sniper rifles with increased firing speed messes
| up the scoping but reload speed doesn't so that's something to take into
| account

Reading: this is a case against Cowser's note 2 ("if it swings or fires, it
can get it") for one weapon family. A sniper rifle's fire-rate attribute
shortens the bolt cycle, and the scope's charge and rezoom are timed on that
cycle, so a faster cycle desyncs the scope. Reload speed does not touch the
cycle, which is why it reads fine. The likely rule is a line in
weapon_eligibility.go: fire-rate off sniperRifles (the Huntsman is not a
rifle and keeps it), reload-rate left as is. Not measured on a server yet, so
this stays a report until somebody scopes with the buff on.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text: Already handled on main: weapon_cuts.go cuts fire-rate on every sniper rifle (Sniper Rifle, Bazaar Bargain, Classic, Hitman's Heatmaker, Machina, Sydney Sleeper) and on the Huntsman, from Cowser's sheet (e5dfe0b), and reload-rate stays. It is in the v1.11.0 changelog section and not yet in a tagged release, so Peppy either saw it on an older build or on a rifle before that commit. Nothing more to do here unless it comes back on a build past e5dfe0b.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
CowsertheKhelinace, GitHub #32:

| Heal on Hit (effect 22) and Speed on Hit (effect 80) do NOT work with Jar
| weapons (Jarate, Mad Milk).
|
| Uber on Hit (effect 40) still functions, if it was removed because OP, maybe
| tone it down to +1% Uber on Hit for syringe guns? Keep +5% for Melees.

Reading. Two of the eight jar permutations opened here do nothing in game, so
the eligibility line is right and the plugin is not delivering it. They moved to
apw-jpm; ignite on hit and the rest stay as they are.

Uber on hit went out with explode on ignite because both hung off the same note,
not because it was measured as too strong on its own. He says it still fires and
wants it back at one percent on syringe guns and five on melees. That is a
maintainer call and it stays on the decisions list above until it is answered.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text: Speed boost on hit is not in the jar set (substanceEffects in weapon_eligibility.go has heal-on-hit and not speed-on-hit), so Cowser saw it on a jar through an older seed or sm_ap_buff_give. The plugin pays it on a splash now anyway, so opening it there is one word in that list if wanted.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
CowsertheKhelinace answered all four maintainer decisions on GitHub #32, and they are implemented on main.

| Meter weapons and clip or ammo: "Bonk and Sandvich (and derivatives) can do
| without." Thermal Thruster already has kelly's launch charge; Sandman and Wrap
| Assassin already draw projectile count for extra balls.
|
| Banner or medigun buff on another slot: "just remove the other slots from the
| pool. Probably won't be worth the trouble."
|
| Movement speed, jump height, health regen: "Passive is better, the base MvM
| upgrades are all on the class, not weapons."
|
| Uber on hit at 1% syringe / 5% melee: "That sounds perfect already."

What changed:

title: The bundle should say when the plugin did not load
description:

kelly-cs, GitHub #26, help wanted:

PR #27: the launcher serves tf/ over HTTP in process on FASTDL_PORT and writes sv_downloadurl with its LAN address; the compose stack gets a caddy service. On the local network nothing to set up. ## A follow-up proposal is open, PR #30 (2026-09-06)

This bead closed on PR #27, which serves tf/ from the launcher over the local network and leaves a forwarded port to the host. kelly-cs has proposed the missing case as PR #30: a public HTTPS address through a Tailscale Funnel, so a player outside the LAN downloads maps without the host forwarding a port. Opt in, off by default, with the Funnel backend bound to loopback, six asset directories exposed and nothing else, paths checked with fs.ValidPath and os.Root at both the TF directory and the asset directory, and cfg, addons and passwords kept out. Fifteen files, docs included, and CI is green.

It is a design decision rather than a fix, so it wants the maintainer rather than a review of the code: it adds Tailscale as a thing a host may have to install, and a public URL is a public URL.

title: Extra crossbow bolts from projectile count do not heal
description:

| would be cool if we got the healing to work with all the extra projectiles

CBaseProjectile::SetLauncher, which sets both launcher handles and resets

built it to. It also keeps the unscaled m_flDamage so the extra is not

234 that works on Windows, and 234 is Destroy(bool, bool). Nobody has fired a

title: The self-blast buffs do nothing on rocket launchers and the Loose Cannon
description:
kelly-cs, GitHub #15:

> The "No self inflicted blast damage" buff doesn't appear to work for things like the loose cannon, rocket launchers, etc. (The same also appears to be the case for reduced damage from rocket jumping)

Effects 63 (no self blast dmg) and 73 (rocket jump damage reduction) in gamedata/weapon_effects.go, applied through the private attribute provider in weapon_buffs.inc. Both attributes are read by the game on the player, not on the weapon, so a provider on the weapon never reaches them. Fix on the damage hook: self damage with DMG_BLAST from the player's own weapon, scaled or zeroed by the effect level.
notes:
## Revised by PR #31, open (2026-09-06)

kelly-cs found that the fix this bead closed on costs the blast jump. The OnTakeDamage hook set damage to zero, and TF2 stops processing a zero damage event before it applies the explosion's push, so a rocket jump with the buff moved nobody and drew no ordinary explosion.

The PR replaces it: the SDKHook keeps only the rocket-jump-protection multiplier, and no-self-blast is applied as the game's own attribute, blast dmg to self increased at 0.0, written onto every loadout slot in WeaponBuffs_SyncNativeSelfBlast and cleared on removal and disconnect. TF2 then zeroes the health damage inside its own rules, after the explosion and its force exist. CI is green on go, apworld, plugin and stack.

Read on review, one thing to answer before it lands. The eligibility rule for no-self-blast is explosiveWeapons in gamedata/weapon_eligibility.go, which holds the Detonator, the Scorch Shot, the Ullapool Caber and the Cow Mangler 5000 as well as the launchers. The PR's validation covers rocket, grenade and stickybomb launchers. The old hook zeroed any self-inflicted DMG_BLAST whatever fired it; the attribute only works where the game's damage rules consult it. So a flare jump with the Detonator or the Scorch Shot, and the Caber blowing up its own wielder, are three eligible cases whose behaviour changes and that nobody has tried.
close_reason: Fixed on main, 5128b2e: an OnTakeDamage hook applies both effects to self-inflicted blast damage. Compiled; not yet watched on a server.

title: The bundle points at a crash dump that belongs to another program
description:
k-kaneta's bundle of 2026-08-30 holds eight srcds crashes (0xc0000005) and a crashes/ folder with GameBar.exe, Refunct-Win32-Shipping.exe and THPS12.exe dumps. EMann's of 2026-09-02 carries FileCoAuth.exe and THPS12.exe. None is srcds. summary.txt still says "A crash dump is in crashes/. That is the file worth reading first."

title: The Python tooling should be Go, except the apworld that has to be Python
description:
This repository is Go with Python scattered through it, and most of the Python is not there for a reason: it is a script somebody wrote in the language they had open.

What has to stay Python: apworld/tf2_mvm, which Archipelago loads and which is Python by Archipelago's own contract, and its tests.

What should be Go:

- tools/import_tf2_weapons.py, 149 lines. It parses TF2's item schema keyvalues, reads the localisation file, merges prefabs and prints candidate weapons as JSON for a maintainer to review. A keyvalues parser and a JSON printer are ordinary Go, and the repository already has Go tooling to put it beside.
- deploy/player-yaml.py, deploy/package-zip.py, deploy/rcon.py. rcon.py in particular is a third copy of a protocol tf2-mvm-bots-go already has as internal/rcon.
- gamedata/cmd/weapons/generate.py
- docs/shadow.py

Do them one at a time, each with the output of the Python and the output of the Go compared on the same input before the Python goes. A rewrite of a maintainer tool that nobody checks is how a catalog quietly changes.

## Done when

No Python outside apworld/tf2_mvm and its tests, and each conversion has a commit showing the two agreed on real input before the Python was deleted.
notes:
## The bots side is Go already (2026-09-05)

Worth knowing before anybody costs this: the defender mod is authored in Go and generates its own SourcePawn, and this repository runs that generator through a tool directive in go.mod. So the pattern this bead asks for exists next door and is pinned here.

Each conversion is its own commit.

title: A Cash Bundle heals the player it pays
description:
Reported 2026-08-27, and not intended.

MvM_DropCredits pays a bundle by spawning an item_currencypack_custom at the
player's feet and letting them walk into it, which is how the game itself pays.
A currency pack in MvM heals whoever picks it up. That is the game's behaviour,
not ours: nothing in this repo asks for it, and it is not from kelly-cs's weapon
buff work, which touches no currency code.

So every Cash Bundle is worth its credits plus a free top-up, and the bigger the
bundle the less that matters, which is backwards.

## Why the obvious fix is not free

MvM_DropCredits already has a second path that writes m_nCurrency directly, used
when a pack cannot be told its amount. That one does not heal. But the comment
above it says why the pack is tried first: money written straight onto
m_nCurrency is money the game's own record never saw, so the refund button and
the wave-loss restore do not know about it. That is what g_BundleCredits and the
bundle ledger exist to paper over.

Swapping the order trades a heal nobody asked for against an accounting hole
that has already produced bugs. Both are worth measuring before choosing.

## Other ways out

- spawn the pack and suppress the heal, if a property or a hook on the pickup
  can do it, which nobody has checked
- pay through the pack and take the healed amount back off, which is exact but
  visible as a flicker
- decide the heal is small enough to keep and write it down as intended, which
  is the one option that needs no code

Worth measuring first: how much a pack actually heals, since none of the above
is worth doing if it is a handful of health.
close_reason:
Kept on purpose, decided with the numbers in hand.

The heal is Scouts only, 25 points of decaying overheal per pile between waves,
and the same whether the bundle is worth 50 credits or 1000. On servers where
item_currencypack_custom carries no amount property the pack path never runs at
all and the fallback heals nothing.

All three fixes cost more than that. Reordering the payment paths pushes every
bundle through g_BundleCredits and widens the surface that produced apw-6hf.
Suppressing the heal has no hook, since the pickup is the payment. Subtracting
the healed amount reads health across a frame boundary against overheal the game
is already decaying.

Recorded in the doc block above MvM_PackCredits so the next reader does not file
this again. Reopen if a Scout-heavy team ever makes 25 points matter.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Picked up for a fix. The agent is told to establish how much a pack actually
heals before choosing between the options, since none of them is worth doing for
a handful of health, and to treat reordering the two payment paths as a trap
rather than the obvious answer: that is the accounting hole apw-6hf came out of.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Measured the heal from the game's own rule rather than the server: only Scouts are healed by a credit pile, and the amount is per pile, not per credit. 50 health when below full, 25 as overheal at full, dropping to about 5 once a Scout is over 700. Every other class gets nothing.

Two things shrink that further here. A bundle only pays between waves (MvM_CanPayCredits requires RoundState_BetweenRounds), which is where everybody is standing at the upgrade station at full health, so the realistic case is the 25 overheal, and MvM overheal decays on its own. And the pack path is inert on every server seen so far: MvM_PackCredits gives up when none of m_nAmount, m_nCurrencyAmount or m_iAmount exists on item_currencypack_custom, which is the case the AP_Debug line reports, and the m_nCurrency fallback does not heal at all.

So the heal is at most 25 decaying overheal on one class in the common case, and zero on the servers where the pack cannot carry an amount. Not worth trading against the accounting hole that produced apw-6hf, and not worth a health read-back and rewrite either. Taking the bead's no-code option: the heal is accepted and written down where the pack is spawned.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Correction: the description above was wrong about who gets healed, and it
changes the size of the problem.

Credit piles in MvM heal Scouts only. Every other class gets nothing. The amount
is per pile, not per credit: 50 when below full, 25 as overheal at full, tapering
to about 5 above 700 health. So a bundle worth 1000 credits and one worth 50 give
the same 25 points.

Two things shrink it further. MvM_CanPayCredits only pays between rounds, when a
Scout is at the station at full health, so the realistic case is the 25 point
overheal, which decays on its own. And the pack path is inert on every server
seen so far: MvM_PackCredits bails when item_currencypack_custom carries none of
the three amount properties, and the m_nCurrency fallback heals nothing at all.

The three fixes all cost more than that. Reordering the paths pushes every bundle
through g_BundleCredits and widens the surface that produced apw-6hf, to claw
back decaying overheal from one class. Suppressing the heal has no hook: the
pickup is the payment. Subtracting the healed amount means reading health across
a frame boundary against overheal the game is already decaying.

Reopened rather than closed because it was reported as unintended and that stands
until the reporter has seen these numbers. The question is now narrow: is 25
points of decaying Scout overheal per bundle worth any of the above.

title: Spare checks are cash, and cash is forgettable
description:
What kelly-cs's PR #3 solves, filed so the change has a reason on record rather
than only a diff.

## The problem

A run has more checks than it has things worth finding. The ones left over paid
cash, and cash is the weakest reward the game has: it is spent within the wave
it arrives in and leaves nothing behind. A player who found a spare check five
waves ago cannot point at anything it gave them.

## What the PR does

Turns the spare checks into stackable weapon buffs drawn from the game's own
item attributes: damage, reload rate, clip size, projectile count, and the
substance effects across weapon families. They persist for the run, so a check
found in wave 2 is still doing something in wave 8.

Two options with it: WeaponBuffPercentage, how much of the spare space is buffs
rather than cash, and WeaponBuffStackChance, how often a buff adds a level to
one already drawn instead of a new permutation.

## Worth knowing about the shape of it

- Buffs are on by default. WeaponBuffPercentage is 75, and with cash rewards
  off every spare check is a buff. Existing runs change shape on upgrade, which
  is the intent rather than an accident, but it is not opt-in.
- 227k lines, and 224k of them are generated: items.json, the plugin's key table
  and the frozen ids. The hand-written part is about 3k.
- The plugin's data size goes from 19 KB to 2.8 MB, all of it the static key
  table for 212 weapons by 80 effects. Memory, not frame time: there is no
  OnGameFrame in it and the hooks are event driven.

## Follow-ups the author names

More custom upgrades beyond the vanilla attribute list.
close_reason: Merged as PR #3 and shipped. The Balancing tab in both interfaces carries the options, on by default at 75 per cent of spare checks. CI on the merged code caught one test the branch had never run; fixed in d7b32eb.

title: A cancelled nightly leaves a half-pushed image, and the next one fails on unknown blob
description:
Run 32995004890 failed on `build and push the archipelago image`:

    unknown blob
    ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1

(The `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'requests'` lines above it are
Archipelago's own optional apworlds failing to import. They are normal and are
not this.)

## Cause

`unknown blob` is the registry being asked for a layer it does not hold whole.
The nightly makes that likely by design:

    concurrency:
      group: nightly
      cancel-in-progress: true

Three runs around the failure were cancelled: 0b82ec8d, 54ca4539, 22ab60cd. A
run cancelled part-way through `docker push` leaves the blob it was uploading
incomplete in the registry, and the next run pushing the same layer refers to
it and gets this.

The run after it succeeded on its own, which fits: a fresh push re-uploads the
layer and the reference resolves. So this is intermittent and self-healing,
which is the worst kind of red in a log, because it teaches everybody to ignore
a failed nightly.

GitHub also had a major Actions incident the same afternoon, so registry
flakiness on its own cannot be ruled out as a second cause. Either way the fix
is the same.

## Fix

Retry the push. It is the whole answer for both causes: a re-push re-uploads
the missing layer, and a registry having a bad minute usually stops having one.

Three steps push (`bridge`, `srcds`, `archipelago`) and each writes the same
two lines, so a small helper doing build-then-push-with-retry covers all three
and stops the retry being added to one and forgotten on the others. Bound it:
three attempts, a few seconds apart, and let the step fail on the third so a
genuine registry refusal still shows.

Do not drop `cancel-in-progress`. It is there because two runs racing would
both delete and recreate the `nightly` tag, and the loser would leave the
release describing a commit the tag no longer points at. That is worse than a
retried push.
close_reason: Fixed. deploy/push-image.sh retries a push three times with a widening delay, and both workflows call it so the retry cannot be added to one image and forgotten on the others. Exercised against a stub docker in both directions: recovers when the third attempt succeeds, and still exits 1 with 'push failed 3 times' when every attempt fails. cancel-in-progress deliberately left alone.

title: Scale the run's difficulty to how few humans are on the slot
description:
Peppy, on Discord:

> How about an upgrade multiplier that adds up depending on how few humans are
> playing on the slot? So less players mean that the effect of an upgrade you
> buy is increased but the cost stays the same

And the shape it should take, from the same thread:

> Peppy: Maybe could be an option you set in the yaml
> Peppy: Or it could even be an unlock
> omaewh4: that's smart yeah

## Why this and not better bots

The reason it is worth doing at all, from the thread:

> omaewh4: I think having a way to balance the difficulty without relying on
> bots AI is really important, like damage multipliers, more health, etc

Every other lever on difficulty here is the bot mod playing better, which is
slow, uncertain, and measured a wave at a time. A multiplier is none of those.
It moves the whole curve, it is one number, and it works the same on a mission
nobody has tuned. It also covers the case the bots never will: a solo player
against a mission written for six people.

## What Peppy is asking for exactly

The upgrade keeps its price and gains effect. That is deliberate and it is the
better half of the idea: it leaves the credit economy alone. Prices are what
missionsanity, the wave payouts and the Cash Bundle item all balance against,
and a discount would move every one of them. An effect multiplier moves none.

Scale it on the humans on the slot, not on RED's size. The bots fill RED to six
whatever happens, so RED's size answers the same on a solo run as on a full one
and is useless as a signal.

## The two ways to expose it, and they are not exclusive

**A yaml option** is the plain one: a number in the player file, read at
generation, applied for the whole run. Predictable, and it is how somebody sets
the difficulty they want before they start.

**An unlock** is the interesting one, and it is the one that belongs in a
randomiser. The multiplier arrives as an Archipelago item, so the run gets
easier as the multiworld hands it over, and a seed can gate it behind another
world. That gives the same knob a place in the item pool instead of a settings
page.

Both can exist: the yaml sets the floor, the items raise it. Decide the floor
first, because an item that raises a number nobody set has nothing to raise.

## Open questions before any of it is built

- Which effect. "Upgrade effect" is not one number in Mann vs Machine: damage,
  fire rate, resistances and the building upgrades are separate attributes. The
  smallest honest version is a damage multiplier and a resistance multiplier,
  not a single global one.
- Whether it recomputes when somebody joins or leaves mid-run. A player joining
  should probably not weaken the team mid-wave, so recompute between waves.
- Whether it counts humans on the server or humans on RED. A spectator is not
  playing.
- How it shows. A run silently 40 per cent easier is a run nobody trusts; the
  session tab should say what multiplier is live and why.

Related: apw-no9 (Progressive Starting Money) is the same idea aimed at the
economy rather than the effects, and the two should not both be turned up
without measuring, or a solo run is easy twice over.
notes:
[-SAM-], Discord 2026-09-07, playing a run without bot support:

| I think damage multiplier for players would help a lot because tanks are the 1
| thing that are currently preventing me from being able to get through a run
| without bot support
| well alternatively would be to give players damage resistance or damage output
| multipliers

Second person asking for the same lever, and they name the wall: the tank. A tank
is a fixed health pool with no AI to outplay, so a solo player either has the DPS
for it or does not. That makes the tank the cheapest thing to test a player-side
multiplier against.
The shape argued out on Discord, 2026-09-08. It started from a buff idea and
turned into this bead's own question.

| [-SAM-]: But I think instead of a buff it should just be a default thing when
| there's only 1 player in the team
| Cowser: Generation cant count how many players there will be
| Cowser: Bc it can change
| [-SAM-]: it could though, you could just tell it to
| Cowser: Keep in mind the server is what gets the items, not the players
| [-SAM-]: exactly, which is why it should just be a setting where you pick how
| many players are going to be playing in the team at the same time and then the
| generator can take that into account
| [-SAM-]: I dont think there would be any other way to balance something like
| this for every possible team sizes

Cowser is right about the constraint and it is the reason this is not simply
read at runtime: a slot is one server, items go to the server, and the humans on
it change wave to wave. So the multiplier cannot be a function of who is
currently connected without the run meaning something different every wave.

[-SAM-] lands on the answer that follows from it: the player says at generation
how many humans the team expects, and the generator scales from that. It is a
number in the YAML like every other run-shape option, it is fixed for the run,
and a team that plays short of it is playing harder than it asked for, which is
the player's own choice rather than the seed changing under them.

That is a decision this bead did not have. Peppy's original "maybe an option you
set in the yaml" is the same answer reached twice, a fortnight apart.

title: A nightly build calls itself by the release version it was built past
description:
The window title on a nightly reads:

    Mann vs Archipelago  1.9.0-837b556

That build is not 1.9.0. It is main, some commits past the 1.9.0 tag, and it
says so nowhere a player looks.

## Why it says that

`Makefile:16` takes `RELEASE_VERSION` from the apworld's `world_version`, which
is the last release the apworld declares. The launcher string was then

    assets.LauncherVersion=$(RELEASE_VERSION)-$(BUILD_COMMIT)

so every build between releases carries the previous release's number. That is
right for a release build and wrong for a nightly, and the two were the same
expression.

## What it costs

Bug reports. A player on a nightly says "I am on 1.9.0", and every triage of
that report starts from the released code. Today's session hit this from the
other side: two bundles were read as 1.9.0 and the launcher line in both said
`1.9.0-c42e61c`, which is only distinguishable by knowing that `c42e61c` is not
the release commit. Nobody knows that from a chat message.

The short commit is in there and it is definitive, but it only helps somebody
who already suspects the build is not what it claims.

## Fix

A `BUILD_CHANNEL` variable, empty by default:

    BUILD_CHANNEL ?=
    LAUNCHER_VERSION := $(if $(BUILD_CHANNEL),$(BUILD_CHANNEL),$(RELEASE_VERSION))-$(BUILD_COMMIT)

`.github/workflows/nightly.yml` passes `make dist BUILD_CHANNEL=nightly`, so a
nightly titles itself `nightly-837b556`. `release.yml` keeps plain `make dist`
and is unchanged, and so is a local build.

Only the displayed string moves. `RELEASE_VERSION` stays as it was because the
Windows version resource takes it as `$(RELEASE_VERSION).0` through
goversioninfo, and that field has to be four numbers: a channel name in it would
not build.

The same string reaches `summary.txt` in the debug bundle through the assets
version map, so the next bundle from a nightly says which it is on its own.
close_reason: Fixed. BUILD_CHANNEL is empty by default so release and local builds are unchanged; nightly.yml passes BUILD_CHANNEL=nightly and the title becomes nightly-<sha>. Verified the Windows -file-version resource stays 1.9.0.0 with the channel set, since goversioninfo needs four numbers.

title: The connect address is not on the session tab
description:
Cowser, on native Linux, running 1.9.0:

> also, there's no clear display of where the IP is to connect unless you click
> C on the log screen :P
> so def some more visibility on how to connect on the sessions tab?

The address exists, and the launcher already knows it. It is only reachable by
pressing C on the log tab, which is a keystroke nobody finds without being told.

The session tab is where a player looks for it, and it is where the server's
own state already lives. Put the connect line there, and make it copyable in
place rather than only from the log.

His bundle has `srcds_reach: "port"` and port 27015, so this is the plain
direct-connect case, not the SDR one. Whatever the tab shows must still be
right for `reach=sdr`, where the FakeIP is what a player needs and the LAN
address is useless to them.

Worth showing the whole `connect <addr>` command rather than the bare address,
since that is what gets pasted into the TF2 console. If a server password is
set, the command needs it too, and the session tab is the one place the
launcher can say so without printing the password to a log.
close_reason: Fixed for the terminal, which is where the gap was. The Windows window already carried the join addresses on its Session tab; the TUI only had a truncated header list and the C key on the log tab, and the report came from a native Linux player. The session tab now renders ConnectLines: the connect command rather than a bare address, untruncated, with what each reach still needs and the server password when set. No test: the TUI session view needs a running supervisor to render, and ConnectLines has its own tests in internal/runtime. Worth a visual check on a real run.

title: Cut the README down and give it a shape
description:
252 lines, fifteen headings. Copy https://github.com/gastownhall/beads:
headline, quick start, features, a diagram, then links out. Under a hundred
lines.

## Cut

Eighty two lines are install instructions that docs/en/setup/install-windows.md
and install-linux.md already carry. Two copies of a procedure is one that goes
stale, and this is the copy nobody edits.

How it works, Directory tree, Why MvM and Code signing policy are documentation

What is cut moves to a docs page. Credits stays, it names people. Code signing

## Add

A quick start above the fold. The first instruction is on line 45 under a
Windows heading, so a Linux reader scrolls past it.

A feature list: bold label, one line, about eight.

The Archipelago list, missing entirely, and what an AP player reads first.
Check the numbers against the tree before publishing them:

- checks, four kinds (gamedata/locations.go): wave cleared, mission cleared,
  tank destroyed, giant killed, across 29 missions and 181 waves
- items, 40, of which 39 progression and 1 filler: Mission Ticket per mission,
  Class per mercenary, Progressive Weapon Slot, Cash Bundle at 200 credits
- goals: Final Boss, or Missionsanity for a share of the missions
- options worth naming: mission count, difficulty pool, excluded missions,

A diagram nobody has drawn: game, plugin, bridge, room. Mermaid, so both forges

Documentation as a list of links. 47 files under docs/, linked 19 times now.

## Then

Run it through /rewrite. It is the front page and the first English many players

What was cut moved to repository.md, code-signing.md and licences.md in both languages, or was deleted where the setup guides already carried it. Vale clean, book builds.

title: Lock an Australium Medal onto every mission clear
description:
Split out of apw-o75, which carried it as "what is still open". It is a design
change with a data format bump behind it, not the tail of a bug fix, so it waits
on its own bead rather than holding that one open.

The goal currently reads a list of locations this server checked itself. That
works. The better shape, which the original play-test report suggested, is to
stop asking about locations at all:

- Lock a trophy item, an Australium Medal, onto every mission clear. No other
  player's item is ever under a clear, so !collect cannot touch one.
- The goal becomes state.has("Australium Medal", player, target) rather than
  can_reach_location, which is what generation logic wants anyway.

Costs:

- Eight locations' worth of other people's items. A mission clear is one of the
  better checks this world offers, and locking it means the multiworld loses it.
  That is the real argument against, and it is why this is not obviously right.
- An item id, so a gamedata change on the Go side, a regenerated data.py, and a
  data format bump. Seeds and saves on the old format do not survive it.

Do it the next time the format moves for another reason, so the break is paid
for once. Not on its own.
notes:
## The format bump these two wait on may not be needed (2026-09-06)

Both this bead and its sibling say the change wants a data format bump and that the two should ride one bump rather than moving the format twice. Checked while adding the Grappling Hook, which is a new item kind and needed no bump:

- The data files travel inside the world. apworld/tf2_mvm/data is copied into the world directory in the image and packaged into the .apworld by launcher/cmd/packagezip, so data.py and the JSON it reads can never be a version apart. format_version guards a stale export against the Go tables, which the committed-export test already catches.
- Item ids are additive. A new block in gamedata/ids.go renumbers nothing that has shipped, and the frozen id table refuses a move. An existing seed simply never had the new ids in its pool.
- What would break is narrower than a format: data.py asserts exactly one weapon_slot item. Per-class slots as a new kind, rather than as more items of that kind, walks past that assertion untouched.

So each of the two can land on its own, with its option off by default, and neither has to wait for the other. The Grappling Hook is the worked example: a new kind, a new id block, an option defaulting off, and no format change.
close_reason: medal_on_clear ships off by default. Trophy is a new item kind with its own id block, one medal per mission rather than one name in copies, because Final Boss asks for a named mission and missionsanity counts. No format bump was needed, as the note predicted. Reachable from the launcher, the terminal settings and the window.

title: Mission progress shows other people's collect as your own clears
description:
Peppy, confirming the apw-o75 fix and naming what it left behind:

"it seems that other worlds collecting their remaining items on goal complete
still mark your missions as cleared without having actually cleared them
yourself"
"but i guess it doesnt actually complete your own goal on itself anymore it
seems so thats good"
"But it does make it harder to keep track of what you've actually completed or
not"

apw-o75 split played from checks and pointed the goal at played. The goal is
right now. What still reads checks is everything the player looks at: a mission
another player's !collect touched is drawn as cleared, so the list no longer
says what this player did.

Same fix, one level up. Anything that reports this player's own progress reads
played; !checked keeps reading checks, because reporting what the room has is
its whole job. Where both matter, show them apart rather than merging: cleared
by you, versus checked by the room.

Cheap, no data format change, and it does not wait on the Australium Medal work
in apw-o75.
close_reason: Fixed. /missions serves played alongside cleared, and the GUI and TUI both draw them apart: 'cleared' means this server played it, 'collected' means only the room holds the check. Cleared keeps its old meaning because the plugin chains on it. Test covers the disagreement directly. Not seen against a live room with another world collecting.

title: No weapons when the item server is unreachable, with no message saying so
description:
Cowser: "was the item servers just down yesterday or do you need to do something
specific to have weapons in the server" / "bc i couldnt connect to the item
server and had to run full stock on me and my bots"

He could not tell whether it was an outage or a missing setup step, which is the

ItemServerLine matches the 'Current item schema is up-to-date' success line, verified against two real bundles, and passes anything else about the schema through without interpreting it. The GUI prints it; the TUI keeps it on the session tab so it does not scroll away. Whether the fetch itself belongs here or on the mod side is still unresolved and out of scope for the message.

title: Item and location names print as raw IDs
description:
Cowser: "Also it didn't print names of items or locations, just IDs"

Same session as his crash reports, so possibly a client that never received the
datapackage rather than a formatting bug. Not diagnosed.
close_reason: Fixed, and the bead's guess was wrong: not a client that missed the datapackage, but the bridge never asking for one. printJSON.text read only the Text field, which carries the id itself for typed parts. The bridge now sends GetDataPackage on connect for the games in the room, keeps names per game because two games may both number an item 77, and takes player names free from Connected. Five tests cover resolution, the game-picking, unresolved and ambiguous ids, and the pre-handshake case. Not seen against a live room: worth one look at chat on the next run.

title: Rafmod missions do not run on a Windows server; Potato converted theirs to VScript
description:
[-SAM-], 2026-09-10: "I wanna quickly bring up that whole thing with sigmod and how it doesnt work in windows server. I know that the Potato community has converted has converted missions that use rafmod over to use Vscript instead which works on any server. so maybe thats something to consider looking into?"

title: Confirm the loadout editor's class menu against 1.13, then close or fix
description:
Glitch, 2026-09-10, on 1.12: "Custom loadouts don't seem to be able to be configured anymore (Dropdown defaults to Scout's weapons instead of giving options for the other classes' weapons) and the saved loadouts I had just use the stock loadouts instead".

CaptPurpleHeart confirmed and gave a workaround: "if you set the bots to a class, set their loadout to stock, then save. Reopen the loadout changer, then you can change their set".

Half of this is fixed: the saved loadouts playing stock was the key-versus-name bug, fixed in #55 and shipped in 1.13.0. The other half, the class menu offering only the Scout's weapons, was reported against the window and Kelly's page, both of which are gone. The builder in 1.13 picks the class with chips and rebuilds the slot rows off the model, and form.NewState seeds the draft with the first class so the menu's value matches an option.

So this needs one player on 1.13 to say whether it still happens, not a guess. Ask before touching it.
acceptance_criteria: Either a reproduction on 1.13, or the reporter confirms it is gone.

title: Cut the doc and comment sprawl back to what carries a constraint
description:
kelly-cs, GitHub #42: "I think the AI agents are getting a bit too excited about docs / comments. It's turning into a lot to maintain and I don't think it's all necessary. Ideally the code is self-documenting, and if it isn't, there's a problem. Most of this stuff doesn't really need user-facing docs unless it's referring to how to use the app itself."

Fair, and the maintainer's own rule says the same: no comment that restates the code. What earns its place is a hidden constraint, an invariant, a workaround, a surprising behaviour. Everything else goes.

Do it as one pass per package with a diff somebody can read, not as a sweep across the tree.

title: Say which apworld a seed needs when the data format version does not match
description:
Wonton, 2026-09-09: "launcher bridge stopped: seed has data format version 2, this bridge reads 4 ... is this just a version mismatch between the server on my end and the yaml used to generate the world?" vixon2 answered it ("mismatch between client and apworld used to gen") and said he had hit the same thing a week earlier.

Two people, one week apart, on a message that names two numbers and no action. It should name the action: regenerate the seed with the apworld that ships with this launcher, and say which version that is.

Likai, same day: "Might be nice to call out when the format version is getting bumped in release notes". Same problem from the other side, and cheap: the release notes are a CHANGELOG section.
acceptance_criteria: The error names the apworld version to regenerate with, and a format bump is a changelog line.

title: Buff idea: an ubercharge that survives a weapon switch
description:
CowsertheKhelinace, 2026-09-08:

| Oh i just thought of a good buff idea
|
| Mediguns: Uber remains active while using a different weapon

New, not a variant of anything on the sheet. The catalogue has one uber effect,
UberOnHitEffect 39 in weapon_buffs.inc, and that builds charge rather than
holding it.

What it is worth: a medic who pops uber is holding a medigun and shooting
nothing for eight seconds. A medic who can switch to the syringe gun or the saw
without dropping it is a medic who contributes during his own uber, which is the
one stretch of a wave where he cannot. That reads as a real buff on the class
whose buffs are the thinnest.

The mechanism is already here. Effects hold conditions with TF2_AddCondition
today, TFCond_SpeedBuffAlly and TFCond_CritOnKill among them, so keeping
TFCond_Ubercharged on across a switch is the same shape.

Unknown and worth trying before designing it: whether the game takes the
condition back on the switch, and what happens to the patient's own uber, which
is a second condition on a second player. Neither is answered by reading.

Ineligible on anything but a medigun, so it wants the eligibility work of
apw-4ck rather than being bolted on before it.

title: Nothing tells anybody bot_names.txt exists
description:
Sirknobbles, 2026-09-07: "also can i change the names of bots? that would be fun
i think". Nobody answered.
