title: The lineup does not react to the class the human picked
description:
Sirknobbles, 2026-09-07:

| also, is it possible to make bots not pick duplicate classes/not pick whatever
| class im playing?
| i can set the bots myself if i have to, but itd be nice to be able to swap what
| class im playing on the fly without having to set up a whole list

The team is six named seats, so the answer today is Cowser's: build the list.
Bots_MakeRoom already steps a bot aside for a human who arrives (bots.inc:330),
but it is a seat that moves, never a class.

Two rules, either one useful on its own:

- No two bots on the same class.
- No bot on a class a human on RED is playing.

The second is the one they asked for, and it only pays off if it survives the
human switching class mid-mission: the bot on the class they just took swaps to
something the lineup is missing, without a restart. The live apply path
(botlive.Commands) is already the way a lineup changes without ending a mission,
so the reaction has somewhere to go.

title: The player hosting their own server is not an admin of it
description:
Sirknobbles, 2026-09-07:

| and notably im just doing the test thing, but when i try to type "!ap bots"
| in the game chat, it says only admin can change the bots

Cowser answered it: put your own SteamID in the admins setting. It worked, and
they came back with "the !ap bots works now and its really simple".

The refusal is right and the setting exists. What is wrong is that a player
hosting a server for themselves is not an admin of it until somebody in a Discord
tells them where to look, and the refusal states the rule without naming the
setting that changes it.

Either the installer asks for the SteamID, or the refusal says which setting to
put it in. The second is one string.

title: The launcher rewrites the player YAML, so an edit made there is lost
description:
Roseburst, 2026-09-07:

| But the Yaml doesn't define server settings, and the settings it does define,
| the launcher doesn't recognize; if I enable deathlink and change mission number
| for example, the launcher does not reflect the changes

They read the YAML as an input. It is an output. settings.PlayerYAML renders it
from the launcher's settings and w.writePlayerFile writes it again after every
Save (gui_windows.go:744), so death_link and mission_count edited by hand survive
until the next Save and then go. Nothing on the file or on the screen says which
way the arrow points.

Two things belong on the generated file: a header saying the launcher wrote it
and that editing it is pointless, and the settings screen naming the file it
writes. A player who wants a run shape the launcher does not offer still has the
hand-authored path, but that has to be a decision rather than a surprise.

title: Drop the GitHub Pages book: people read the Markdown on GitHub
description:
The book is built with honkit and deployed to GitHub Pages, and nobody goes there. The links that are out in the world point at the Markdown files in the repository, which GitHub renders on its own, and that is what people navigate.

So the site is a second copy of docs/ that costs a Docker image, a CI job and a slot in the local gate, and can drift from the files everybody actually reads.

What goes:

- .github/workflows/ci.yml, the whole "pages" job, plus the "book" step in "stack" that validates the same image for pull requests.
- Makefile: docs-build, docs, docs-down, HONKIT_VERSION, and docs-build's place in the "check" target.
- deploy/Dockerfile.docs, deploy/compose.docs.yml, deploy/docs-index.html.
- .gitbook.yaml.
- The Pages environment and its deploy permissions on the GitHub side, which is a settings change rather than a commit.

What stays: everything under docs/. The Markdown is the documentation and it is not moving.

Check first that nothing in it only makes sense as a rendered book. honkit reads a SUMMARY-style navigation that GitHub does not, so a page reached only through the book's sidebar becomes a file nobody can find. Those need a link from README.md or from index pages under docs/en and docs/fr.

Also check docs/LANGS.md and the en/fr split still make sense without a language switcher, since that was the book's.

Worth doing after apw-wbj if the web UI ends up serving help of its own, in case any of this is reusable there. It probably is not.

title: The sheet notes nobody has picked up yet
description:
CowsertheKhelinace, GitHub #32. The eligibility pass (apw-4ck) and the bugged
buffs (apw-jpm) cover most of the list; these notes are neither, and this bead
holds them so the issue comment saying "they are on the list" is true.

• 37 Disposable sentry: the Rescue Ranger carried the buff and could not build
one. Carrying it on the PDA instead does not help either.
• 42 Crit from behind only works on flamethrowers; he would allow every weapon.
• 44 Melee range is barely noticeable; suggests +35 to 50% per step.
• 49 Cloak regen does not seem to raise the Dead Ringer's recharge. The tooling

• 55 Accuracy should also tighten the spread projectile count adds.
• 58, 59 Flame size and flame range seem bugged: fix or remove.
• 60 Charged airblast does nothing but stop airblast spam: remove.
• 65 Slow on hit favours fast multi-hit weapons; wants tuning per weapon type.
• 66 Consumption speed halves lunchbox healing at one point and removes soda

Each is a plugin or eligibility change in weapon_buffs.inc or

Closed off this list: 69, recharge speed, which reached neither weapon because
both fill the item meter and the buff scales the effect bar; it is off the Gas
Passer and was never offered on the Thermal Thruster. 70, ammo on hit, which
kelly-cs fixed in #35 for clipped, melee, shield, energy and Thermal Thruster

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
CowsertheKhelinace, GitHub #32, two of these retested:

| Meter Recharge Rate does not affect the Gas Passer (effect 69).
|
| Disposable Sentry does not let me place it, even when applied to the PDA.

Reading: 37 was open on where the buff had to sit, and the PDA answers it. The

comments.author: m-this

The Gas Passer and the Thermal Thruster fill a different meter, item_meter_charge_rate, scaled by mult_item_meter_charge_rate, so the buff cannot reach them whatever it is set to. On top of that the buff provider carries the held weapon's buffs only, and both of those meters fill while holstered. Either the eligibility rule takes meter-recharge off those two (weapon_eligibility.go, meterWeapons), or the plugin puts mult_item_meter_charge_rate on the weapon entity itself, which is the one place it has avoided writing attributes.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Note 69 is closed on main. Recharge speed is no longer offered on the Gas Passer: the eligibility rule now excludes the two weapons that fill CTFWeaponBase's item meter rather than the effect bar, read off their own item_meter_charge_rate in the game's item schema. The Thermal Thruster was already outside the meter-recharge set, so the Gas Passer was the only pair in the pool.

title: Watch a trap grant land: the hold has never run
description:
The hold in `ApplyTrap` (`plugin/scripting/tf2_archipelago/bridge.inc`) has
never run. A trap that arrives from the room while no wave is running should
announce itself once, sit on the cursor, and fire when the next wave begins.

It could not be reached on a botless server. `MvM_CanPayCredits` needs
`!IsFakeClient`, so with no humans connected a Cash Bundle is never payable,
it holds for good, and every effect behind it waits: the trap included. That
is the ordering rule working, and it means only a human with a Team Fortress 2
client can watch a real trap grant land.

Both inputs the hold rests on are measured (apw-929): `MvM_WaveInProgress`
reads correctly in each state, and the identical credits hold was seen live,
announcing once and pinning the cursor.

To close it: play a wave with `trap_percentage` above zero, take a check
between waves that pays out a trap, and read the chat. Expect one line saying
the trap waits, then the Jarate at the start of the next wave, and no repeat
of either.

title: Trap: drop a squad of Spies or Snipers into a wave
description:
From the trap list in `docs/en/spec.md` and Roseburst's `Trap Checks` in
`docs/en/discord-mvm-thread.md`. Team Jarate (apw-929) built the wire, the
`Traps` table and the hold; this adds one entry to that table.

The idea: a trap drops a squad of Spies or Snipers into the wave, anywhere,
any time. Snipers on Rottenburg's balcony while the team fights the front is
the shape of it.

**The unsolved part is how to spawn a BLU robot at runtime.** MvM builds its
robots from the `.pop` file through the game's own spawner, and nothing in
this plugin spawns one today. `tf_bot_add spy blue` makes a plain TFBot, not
an MvM robot: no robot model, no robot behaviour, no bomb logic, and the wave
counter does not know about it. Establish which of these works before writing
anything:

- A `CTFBotSpawner` built at runtime, or a `SpawnBot` entity already on the map.
- OfficerSpy's mod, which already spawns bots for RED. `tf2-mvm-bots-go` is a
  Go module this repository depends on, so its spawn path is readable.
- The community's `MvM Bot Spawner` plugins, whichever one is current.

Answer that first and put the answer in the bead. Only then decide the trap's
shape: how many, which class, where, and whether they carry the bomb.

Two design rules the trap has to keep. It may cost the team a wave and it may
never touch what the run already holds. A spawned robot that drops cash also
inflates the A+ money check for that wave, so either it drops none or the
money-bonus location group has to account for it.

title: Feature: traps, starting with team Jarate
description:

title: The engine watchdog does not exist on Windows, so it cannot explain the crash there
description:
Recorded so the question is not reopened. It came up because the Windows crash
in apw-r85 looked like it might be the watchdog, and because disabling it on
Windows the way apw-4cb did on Linux sounds reasonable until you look.

## The watchdog is POSIX only

From the TF2 tier0 source. On POSIX it is real:

    PLATFORM_INTERFACE void Plat_BeginWatchdogTimer( int nSecs )
    {
        ...
        nSecs *= s_nWatchDogTimerTimeScale;
        nSecs = MIN( nSecs, 5 * 60 );
        if ( nSecs )
        {
            s_WatchdogTime = nSecs;
            signal( SIGALRM, WatchDogHandler );
            alarm( nSecs );
        }
    }

On Windows all four of `Plat_BeginWatchdogTimer`, `Plat_EndWatchdogTimer`,
`Plat_GetWatchdogTime` and `Plat_SetWatchdogHandlerFunction` are empty bodies.
It is `alarm()` and `SIGALRM`, and Windows has neither.

The local Linux install agrees: `-nowatchdog` appears in `bin/libtier0.so`,
`bin/libtier0_srv.so` and `bin/linux64/libtier0_srv.so`, and nowhere else in
the tree. `libtier0_srv.so` also carries the message,
`WatchDog! Server took too long to process (probably infinite loop).`

Three consequences:

- Passing `-nowatchdog` on Windows does nothing. Worse than nothing: it reads
  like a protection is being turned off, so the next person assumes one was
  there.
- apw-4cb is correctly scoped and finished. Linux is the only platform with a
  watchdog to disable.
- The `0xc0000005` in apw-r85 is not the watchdog. That was the leading guess
  and it is now ruled out, which leaves the access violation needing a real
  cause and the minidump to find it.

## There is no softer setting

Worth writing down, because "make it less aggressive" is the obvious next idea.

- The flag is parsed as `strstr( g_CmdLine, "-nowatchdog" )`. It is on or off.
- The timeout is whatever the engine passes, capped at `MIN( nSecs, 5 * 60 )`.
- `s_nWatchDogTimerTimeScale` is the only knob and it is not exposed: 10 in a
  debug build, 1 in a release one.

Nothing on the command line moves the threshold. The comments in
`launcher/internal/runtime/runtime.go` now say all of this at both branches.
close_reason: Recorded, nothing to build. The finding is in the bead and in the comments at both branches of srcdsArgs.

title: docs/fr/glossary.md is a second copy of CONTEXT.md
description:
CONTEXT.md is the glossary and the first file an agent reads, which is why
CLAUDE.md names that path. docs/fr/glossary.md is a translation of it, 200-odd
lines, and nothing keeps the two in step: a term added to one is missing from
the other until somebody notices.

The English side no longer has this problem. docs/en/SUMMARY.md used to link a
glossary.md that never existed, and the page written for it points at
CONTEXT.md rather than copying it.

The French cannot do the same, because the target is in English. So either the
translation is accepted as a real document and gets a line in CONTEXT.md saying
it must be updated too, or docs/fr/glossary.md becomes a page that says the
glossary is in English and links it.

The first if the French book is meant to stand alone, which the rest of docs/fr
suggests it is. Then the duty belongs in CONTEXT.md where the editor will see
it, not in the translation where they will not.
close_reason: Fixed. docs/fr/glossary.md is now the same pointer to CONTEXT.md that the English page is, 209 lines down to 15, with a paragraph saying why the terms stay in English. Vale clean on FR rules, make docs-build exit 0.

title: Keep the pinned versions current
description:
Standing task for the /upgrade-deps sweep, so a version bump is tracked rather
than remembered. Everything this project pins is in deploy/env/versions.env by
design, except the Go version, which is the go line in go.mod because that
directive must be a literal.

## Done 2026-08-28

DEFENDERBOTS_VERSION v2.30.0 to v2.32.0. The pin had gone stale over a week of
mod work: two feature switches, a convar name fix and the test-bed changes were
all in the mod and none of them in a build of the launcher.

## Done 2026-08-26

Go 1.26.6 to 1.27.0, in go.mod, deploy/Dockerfile.bridge and the ci.yml
container image. golangci-lint v2.12.2 to v2.13.1, ruff 0.16.3 to 0.16.4,
pillow 12.1.0 to 12.3.0, nginx 1.30.4-alpine to 1.31.4-alpine. go get -u ./...
moved five indirect deps, golang.org/x/text v0.3.8 to v0.41.0 among them.
gofumpt, govulncheck, goversioninfo and honkit were already current.

The Go bump was not optional. golangci-lint v2.12.2 carries staticcheck v0.7.0,
which panics on the Go 1.27 standard library.

## Next

Check DEFENDERBOTS_VERSION at every release. Nothing fails when it is stale, so
nothing catches it: the launcher builds and runs against whatever tag is named
here, and an old one ships old bots without a word.
design:
## The drift this bead kept re-creating is now caught

Three places carried the Go version and only one could be read by the others.
`go.mod` owns it, the two release workflows already take it with
`go-version-file: go.mod`, and two pins could not: the `FROM` line in
`deploy/Dockerfile.bridge` and the container image in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

Both were hand-edited on every bump. Forgetting one is not harmless: the
2026-08-26 sweep found golangci-lint v2.12.2 carrying a staticcheck that panics
on the Go 1.27 standard library, so a tree on 1.27 with a builder still on 1.26
could not lint at all, and the failure read as a linter bug rather than a stale
pin.

`deploy/check-go-version.sh` compares both against the go directive and `make
check` runs it first, so the stale pin is named before anything downstream fails
for it. A pin shorter than the directive is accepted, because `golang:1.27`
serves 1.27.0.

That does not close this bead. It stays open as the standing task for the next
`/upgrade-deps` sweep; what changed is that one whole class of mistake inside it
now fails loudly instead of quietly.
close_reason: Done on main: the four pins that had moved are current; the plugin compiles and both linters pass. Archipelago 0.6.7, ripext 1.3.2, CBaseNPC, TF2Attributes, gofumpt, govulncheck, Pillow, honkit and goversioninfo were already at their latest.

title: Document that logic is per mission, not per wave
description:
MarioSpore had to ask three times to get this, which makes it a documentation

do? UT does not give me any details on what locations are in logic or not when I
receive a ticket or a class"

omaewh4's answer, which is the text worth publishing:

"Logic works per mission, not per wave. A mission is one region, every check
inside it sits behind one gate: the waves, the tank, the giant, and the clear.
So when a ticket goes into logic, the whole mission goes into logic. There is no
case where wave 3 is in logic and wave 6 is not. You do the whole mission."

title: Feature: Progressive Starting Money
description:
CaptPurpleHeart: "an option to have 'Progressive Starting Money' items, where
at the start of every Wave 1, you get X amount more starting money per every
progressive starting money upgrade found."

Same shape as the three progressives in item 3: a YAML option that is a count,
off at zero, so a seed that leaves it out keeps meaning what it meant.

It is blocked on item 1 for the same reason progressive credit amount is.
Money handed over by writing `m_nCurrency` is money the game's bookkeeping
never saw, so a starting grant inherits the negative balance on a lost wave and
the refund that hands back 400. Item 1's ledger covers a bundle; a starting
grant is the same money by a different door, and it wants the same ledger,
which is one more argument for `DistributeCurrencyAmount` over writing the
property.

Note also that this one interacts with the wave-one restart: "at the start of
every Wave 1" is a mission start, and a mission restarted from the vote menu is
a wave one too. Decide whether restarting pays again before implementing, or
the answer will be decided by whichever event handler happened to be wired.

title: Feature: per-class weapon slot unlocks
description:
CaptPurpleHeart: "I personally would love per-class weapon slot unlocks."

Today a slot unlock is one item for every class: `Unlocks_EnforceSlots` strips
a weapon from a slot the run has not opened, without asking who is holding it.
Per class it is nine items a slot instead of one, which is a much larger pool
and a much longer run, and both of those are the point of asking for it.

It is one option, a boolean, off by default: with it off the run keeps today's
one-item-per-slot unlocks and nothing about an existing seed changes.

It is a gamedata change on the Go side, so it wants an item id per class per
slot, a regenerated `data.py` and a data format bump, and it should ride the
same bump as the Australium Medal in item 7 rather than moving the format
twice.

The open design question is what a run starts with. Nine classes times three
slots with nothing unlocked is a team that cannot shoot; the honest shape is
probably that the primary of the class you spawn as is free and everything else
is earned, but that is a generation-logic argument and it needs writing down
before any id is minted.
design:
## The generation argument, written down (2026-09-06)

The bead asks for this before any id is minted. Here it is, for a maintainer to take or refuse.

### What a slot item becomes

Twenty-seven items rather than three: one per class per slot, keyed by class id and slot id in a block of their own. Progressive within a class, so copy n of "Scout Weapon Slot" opens Scout's nth slot, which keeps the shape the single progressive item already has and needs no new logic in the plugin.

### What makes a class usable

A class is deployable when the run holds its class item and its primary. That definition is the whole of the change to the rules: today the access rule counts slots held, and per class it counts classes that are deployable and then asks for slots on that many of them.

A mission at tier T needs T.classes deployable classes with T.slots slots each. The tiers are unchanged: normal 1 and 1, expert 4 and 3, haunted 5 and 3.

### What a run starts with

The starting tier's requirement, spelled per class. Normal starts one class with its primary. Expert starts four classes with all three slots each, which is sixteen precollected items against today's seven.

That is the honest answer to the question in the description, and it is the same guarantee today's start makes: whatever tier you start on, you can play it from nothing.

### The constraint that decides whether this can ship

The pool grows by 24 items and the checks do not. A playable mission holds 4 to 11 checks, 9 at the median. The pool with the option on is roughly 27 slots plus one ticket per mission past the first plus 8 classes, so a run of 6 missions has about 54 checks against 40 items and works, and a run of 2 has about 18 against 36 and cannot be generated at all.

So the option needs a guard rather than a hope: refuse at generation with a message naming the smallest mission_count that fits, computed from the drawn missions rather than from a constant, because a run of Mannhattan's four-check missions is not a run of eleven-check ones.

### What it does not need

No data format bump. Item ids are additive, the block is new, and no shipped id moves. data.py asserts exactly one weapon_slot item, so these are a new kind rather than more items of that kind, which walks past the assertion. That is what the Australium Medal did on 2026-09-06 and it is the worked example.

open                                                                        

## The format bump these two wait on may not be needed (2026-09-06)

Both this bead and its sibling say the change wants a data format bump and that the two should ride one bump rather than moving the format twice. Checked while adding the Grappling Hook, which is a new item kind and needed no bump:

- The data files travel inside the world. apworld/tf2_mvm/data is copied into the world directory in the image and packaged into the .apworld by launcher/cmd/packagezip, so data.py and the JSON it reads can never be a version apart. format_version guards a stale export against the Go tables, which the committed-export test already catches.
- Item ids are additive. A new block in gamedata/ids.go renumbers nothing that has shipped, and the frozen id table refuses a move. An existing seed simply never had the new ids in its pool.
- What would break is narrower than a format: data.py asserts exactly one weapon_slot item. Per-class slots as a new kind, rather than as more items of that kind, walks past that assertion untouched.

So each of the two can land on its own, with its option off by default, and neither has to wait for the other. The Grappling Hook is the worked example: a new kind, a new id block, an option defaulting off, and no format change.

title: Feature: four optional unlocks from Peppy's post
description:
From the second post in
[`docs/en/discord-mvm-thread.md`](docs/en/discord-mvm-thread.md). Not started,
and none of them is in `gamedata/items.go` yet.

Four items, one shape: each one is a plugin-side effect on a server-wide
value, and each one gets its own YAML option, off by default, the same shape
as `death_link` in `apworld/tf2_mvm/options.py`. A seed that leaves them off
gets none of them in its pool, so an existing seed keeps meaning what it meant.
Three of the four are progressive, so the option is a count and not a boolean:
zero copies is off, N copies is the number of steps the run walks.

Order to build them in is the order below, easiest first. The first two are one
value each and are worth doing before the pool grows further. The last one is
not designed yet.

**Progressive Respawn Time.** RED starts on a longer respawn wave time and each
copy shortens it back toward the stock value. The candidate is the team respawn
wave time that MvM already sets per team, not `mp_respawnwavetime` alone;
confirm which one MvM actually reads before wiring it. Felt every wave, one
value, no interaction with anything else in the item table.

**Progressive Random Crits.** The team starts with random crits off and each
copy raises the chance. `tf_weapon_criticals` and `tf_weapon_criticals_melee`
are the candidates, but they are booleans, so a chance ramp needs either a
per-shot hook or a coarse ladder of off, melee only, on. Decide which before
promising a percentage in the option's docstring. It hits classes unevenly:
Heavy and Demo notice, Sniper barely does. That is a difficulty knob, not a
fair one, which is fine for a randomizer as long as the docstring says so.

**Grappling Hook.** One convar, `tf_grapplinghook_enable`, granted once, so a
state grant and not a progressive. `useful`, not progression: no access rule
may ever need it, because a wave has to stay winnable without it. Cheapest of
the four and the largest change to how a map plays.

**Progressive Returning Bomb.** The bomb walks itself back toward the robot
spawn while no robot carries it, and each copy speeds that walk up. The most
original of the four and the only one that changes the shape of a wave rather
than a number. It is also the least specified. Before designing it, find out
what MvM's existing idle-bomb behaviour is and whether a plugin can reach the
value behind it; if the answer is that the bomb only resets on a timer the map
owns, this becomes a different feature. Note also that it deflates any
bomb-reset location group, so the two should not ship into one seed without
someone thinking about it.

Not in this batch, and why. Progressive credit amount is blocked on item 1
above: money granted by writing `m_nCurrency` does not survive the wave-loss
restore, so a credit-scaling unlock inherits the negative balance. Random-effect
canteens belong in the trap pool that `spec.md` already describes, not here.
Randomized weapons with tiers need the tier to be the item id, because ADR 0001
forbids an id whose meaning is rolled per seed, and that is a feature of its
own size.
notes:
Imported from TODO.md item 3 — section: Features. All requested, all off by 
default                                                                     
Original heading: Feature: four optional unlocks from Peppy's post. Off by  
default, open                                                               

## One of the four is built (2026-09-06)

The Grappling Hook, which the bead called the cheapest and the largest change to how a map plays. It arrives as a new item kind, server_setting, in its own id block so nothing that has shipped is renumbered, and the frozen id table records it. It is state rather than an effect: the bridge resends it freely, the plugin holds the granted set and replays it in OnConfigsExecuted, because server.cfg runs on every map change and puts the host's convar value back. Useful and never progression, so no access rule can need it and a wave stays winnable without it. The apworld option server_settings is off by default, so an existing seed keeps meaning what it meant.

Not yet done and not started: the three progressives. Respawn time still needs somebody to confirm which value MvM actually reads, random crits still needs the ladder decided before a percentage is promised in a docstring, and the returning bomb is still the least specified of the four.

title: Sign the Windows exe
description:
Players report SmartScreen blocking `tf2ap.exe` and Defender quarantining it.
Nothing is wrong with the binary. The launcher unpacks embedded archives into
the TF2 directory, writes Metamod's and SourceMod's DLLs there, downloads a
game server and starts it. Behaviourally that is a dropper, and an unsigned
binary gives a scanner nothing to weigh against the heuristic. Go makes it
worse only in that a static Go binary is a shape malware uses a lot; rewriting
in another language would change nothing.

The fix is a code signature. The application to the SignPath Foundation, which
signs open-source projects for free, is in. `release.yml` already carries the
signing step, skipped until `SIGNPATH_API_TOKEN` exists, and it runs before the
checksums and the attestation so those describe the signed exe. Granting needs
`SIGNPATH_API_TOKEN` as a secret and `SIGNPATH_ORGANIZATION_ID` as a variable.

The application is a long shot and should be treated as one. SignPath asks for
an established project, and this one was four days old with no stars and about
130 downloads when it applied. A rejection is the likely answer, and the
fallback is a paid certificate.

Azure Trusted Signing is the paid fallback at roughly nine euros a month, but
it wants three years of verifiable identity history from an individual. Do not
buy a certificate before SignPath answers.

Two things are already done and do not need repeating here. The exe carries a
VERSIONINFO resource and an icon, so it is no longer an anonymous blob to the
heuristics, and every release publishes SHA-256 sums. Neither removes the
warning: only the signature does, plus the download reputation that accrues
behind it.

One thing is worth doing regardless of SignPath. Submit each release to
[Microsoft's false-positive form](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/filesubmission)
as a software developer. It is free and they usually clear a file within days.

Signing `tf2ap.exe` does not cover the files it writes. If reports come in
about Defender eating the extracted SourceMod DLLs instead of the launcher,
the answer is a documented exclusion for the TF2 install path in the Windows
guide, not more signing.
